# Changelog Archive

## Gate Pass and Vendor Bill ERP mappings — 2026-11-09

`routers/import_export.py` now prioritizes exact headers, then applies a small one-to-one alias set for common ERP labels. Gate Pass/Vendor Bill document IDs accept `#`/`no`; `Qty`, Supplier and purchase references map to their matching template fields; Price, Sales Tax and the verified Vendor Bill `Total` map to Rate, Tax Amount and footing Amount. Gate Pass `Unit` maps to Unit of measurement, leaving Factory Unit unmapped when the workbook has no such header. Saved mappings, positional fallback, dates and import controls are unchanged.

`tests/test_upload_performance.py` covers the aliases, one-to-one assignment and the Unit safeguard. The focused upload/reconciliation/lifecycle selection passes (172 tests). Isolated Playwright checks against GP 03-11.xlsx and Supplier billing 03 Nov.xlsx confirm 10/14 and 15/18 mappings; Vendor Bill `Total` reconciles exactly to the 54 detail rows (986,654.06). Source workbooks were unchanged, no import was performed, and the isolated test app/PostgreSQL services are stopped. Aadil's local acceptance remains pending.

## Upload performance review — 2026-11-09

`routers/import_export.py` now maps headers without loading detail rows, bounds pure text-date interpretation caches, reuses strict fingerprints within a document comparison, and streams unconfirmed XLSX format samples where Footing gates coverage. Confirmed ranges retain full-sheet scans; sparse samples, native dates, ambiguity, legacy XLS, source precision and import safeguards remain protected. `test_upload_performance.py` covers these boundaries; the reconciliation test now reflects the previously approved sub-cent tolerance without rounding source values.

Folders 1–6 were exercised with copied originals, fresh guarded local PostgreSQL/app services, Playwright, API and independent SQL controls. All 33 original hashes match; test services are stopped. Source-based import/repeat, mutation, coverage, concurrency and browser checks pass. Separately approved fixture alignment covers backup settings, configuration locks/history reads, actual staged workbooks, template roles, confirmed display-format dates and current upload/Data Bank messages; no-write, scope, multiplicity and rollback assertions remain. Final selection: 625 tests plus five subtests pass, with one existing Starlette/httpx deprecation warning. Working-app Data Bank access was read-only apart from authentication; no working transactions/configuration changed. No packages were installed. Timings, test-only template adjustments and limitations are in `experiments/upload_safety/PERFORMANCE_REVIEW.md`; private source/evidence remains ignored. Local acceptance and Git authorization are pending.

## Template-first upload toolbar — 2026-11-09

Upload starts with Template only. Selecting it reveals Download and Upload File; mapped workbooks reveal file details, Sheet, Date format and Data Bank in one desktop row, with 32px controls and narrow-screen wrapping. Data Bank sits at the panel's right edge with centered contents. Long filenames shorten visually with the full name in a tooltip. Removing a file retains Template; Reset clears the workflow. Replacement uploads hide stale tables while loading. Script version 34; no backend, schema or dependency changes.

Verification: the full 67-test upload-dialog suite passed; three focused checks passed after visibility changes. Two focused Chromium toolbar checks at 1366px/390px pass after the right-edge/centering correction, measuring panel and text positions. Syntax/whitespace checks pass. Live Playwright checked initial/template/file states, removal, reupload and Reset using both PO workbooks, desktop/narrow layouts, and slash/dash/slash date suggestions. No validation/import was performed. Aadil confirmed local acceptance and authorized commit/push; performance review follows this layout phase.

Reset/reupload passed with that file and PO 11.xlsx; date locking, report-type toggles and manual order changes passed. No validation/import was run. Aadil confirmed positive local testing and authorized commit/push.

## Upload date delimiter auto-selection — 2026-11-09

After mapping, the Upload page scans all values in mapped Date columns and selects `/` or `-` when one date-shaped delimiter is consistent across the sheet. Blank/native date values are ignored; mixed or undetectable values leave the current selection unchanged. The existing date order stays user-controlled, and the format label and sample preview refresh. No backend, parsing, coverage, or storage changes.

Verification: upload-dialog tests pass (62); JavaScript syntax and scoped whitespace checks pass. Playwright on GRN 04-11.xlsx selected `-`, retained DMY and previewed 04 November 2026; validation/import were not run. Local acceptance remains pending.

## Footing variance safeguards — 2026-11-09

Source Footing differences below 0.01 currency units pass as precision noise. Differences from 0.01 through 1.00 require an explicit per-upload acknowledgement, bound to validation and import; larger differences block. Validation and import results/reports retain exact Excel totals, detail totals and variance. Stored transaction values are never rounded or rewritten.

Verification: both focused upload modules pass (164 tests), covering positive and negative 0.01/1.00 boundaries, sub-cent tolerance, over-limit rejection, signed-plan acknowledgement, exact variance display and cancellation. Python/JavaScript syntax and scoped whitespace checks pass. A validation-only browser run on GRN 04-11.xlsx reached the old rejection because the running server had not loaded the backend change; restart and local acceptance remain pending. No import was performed.

After a file is mapped, the existing Document Date preview now fills From/To with the earliest/latest valid transaction dates. Manual date edits remain intact across preview refreshes. ## Upload report dates — Phase 4 — 2026-11-07

Template setup now supports one Date-typed Document Date role. The role uses existing template-mapping storage; no schema change or automatic legacy assignment. Changing the effective report-date source on a populated template is blocked for migration review.

The read-only date preview suggests the earliest/latest parseable dates from transaction rows after blank, recognized-total and confirmed-Footing controls are removed. Suggestions never confirm coverage. Complete reports require a mapped Document Date, an explicit full-ERP-period confirmation and valid ordered coverage dates; coverage may be wider than surviving transaction dates, but must contain every valid incoming detail date. Date edits clear confirmation and invalidate validation. Partial extracts retain their existing behavior.

Verification: focused template and upload checks pass (130 tests); Python compilation and JavaScript syntax checks pass. Aadil confirmed the date flow works with the selected headline format. No schema migration or live data write.

An explicitly confirmed Excel control row is validated only through mapped Footing cells. Values in Document ID, Date, account or other neighboring columns no longer reject the selected row. ## Preview controls — Phase 4 — 2026-11-06

The eight-file scope and approach were separately approved after Phase 3 acceptance/push (`a1da3e01`). Current Client Data eye previews now show compact Rows, Documents and individually configured Footing totals beside the title. Template roles remain authoritative; no new upload choices. Filters include client/template/dates, uploaded ledger account, search, amount, Sunday and data quality. Pagination, page size and displayed subtotal lines never change these source controls. History and Cashflows classification retain their presentation.

The existing preview response optionally includes exact metrics and current column order. One shared parameterized aggregate replaces the ordinary count; page, configuration and controls use an enforced read-only snapshot. Other callers retain their contract. Invalid amounts, missing metrics and failed requests remain explicit; empty scopes show genuine zeros and absent Footing configuration is named. Decimal strings are formatted without floating-point conversion. Document-restricted callers receive no hidden Footing metadata.

Bounded pages remain reusable within a view; reopening or returning focus clears that scope and fetches fresh data. Scope/request guards reject wrong-context responses before caching or presentation; old figures disappear while loading or after failure. No schema/dependency changes or live financial writes. Full performance acceptance remains Phase 5.

Verification: 185 backend/browser checks pass across recorded runs, including delayed-response and HTTP-query coverage. One unchanged history-button assertion was excluded because it predates Phase 4 and conflicts with existing backup/delete presentation. Coverage includes exact totals, filters, ledger isolation, missing settings, failed checks, fresh reopening/focus, page independence, safe text and 390/768/1366px headings. Python/JavaScript syntax, scoped whitespace and documentation budgets pass. Desktop/mobile screenshots were visually reviewed. A live PostgreSQL preview ran in an enforced read-only snapshot with zero writes; the selected client/template/day was empty and returned genuine zero controls. This does not establish populated-scope performance. Aadil's local test and explicit Phase 4 commit/push approval remain pending; unrelated changes are preserved.

## Stored-data reconciliation — Phase 3 — 2026-11-06

The ten-file scope and approach were separately approved after Phase 2 acceptance/push (`90773636`). Import Successful now compares approved Excel detail with actual scoped SQL row counts, distinct Document IDs and each Footing total in one three-column table. Scope, completion time, missing Footing configuration, exact differences and unavailable checks remain explicit. Matching unchanged uploads open No changes required after fresh guarded verification; no detail rows are rewritten. Partial extracts never certify a complete period; absent declared coverage never triggers an unbounded count.

One parameterized aggregate runs after source writes inside the existing transaction. Its compact result shares the atomic import receipt and is returned after commit; recovered responses reuse that completion-time evidence without repeating writes or claiming current freshness. A savepoint isolates optional verification errors; mismatches remain visible without misreporting committed transactions as failed imports. Source/configuration guards protect no-op verification against concurrent corrections. Unicode whitespace normalization matches source arithmetic/counting. Existing change classifications, repeated occurrences and ledger-account isolation remain intact.

The browser-generated upload workbook includes a Reconciliation sheet with scope, exact values, differences and status. The pre-import impact review remains separate. Desktop/mobile results use a contained table scroll for long amounts. No schema, dependency or live source/history writes were made. Phase 4 preview headlines and Phase 5 full performance/acceptance remain pending.

Verification: 201 focused checks pass across recorded runs, covering matching/mismatching metrics, partial/missing scopes, absent Footing settings, query failures, guarded unchanged uploads, concurrent corrections, recovery, rollback, safe text, downloadable XLSX and responsive layouts. Python/JavaScript syntax, scoped whitespace and documentation budgets pass. Read-only PostgreSQL checks verify exact decimals, Unicode keys, scoped filtering, ledger-account separation and recovery after a genuine SQL division error; the transaction remains usable/read-only. The selected live period was inspected only through aggregate counts/totals. Desktop/mobile previews were visually reviewed; ordinary currency values remain on one line at 390px. The exact commit snapshot passed 222 isolated checks; six pre-existing input-error HTTP fixtures were deselected (see Source control totals — Phase 2). Aadil confirmed positive local testing and authorized the Phase 3 commit/push on 2026-11-06; unrelated work is preserved.

## Source control totals — Phase 2 — 2026-11-06

Approved ten-file scope adds a reusable reconciliation service/test and extends Upload's existing mapping area. Template Footing roles require a confirmed, file-specific Excel total-row number; a unique labelled candidate is suggested but never confirmed automatically. Users see each mapped amount before validation. The selected row cannot contain document/date/account information, is excluded from transactions and selection/preview counts, and cannot be reselected through Select All. Existing unconfigured templates retain optional controls and legacy summary recognition.

Validation compares each Footing's saved numeric total with exact Decimal sums of full-sheet detail, excluding recognized blanks, summaries and ledger controls/notes. Missing/invalid totals, formula errors/results, mismatches and app-side cell edits block controlled uploads. Source and approved-subset counts, distinct configured IDs and separate amount totals remain independent; every detail occurrence survives. Complete-report date/exclusion safeguards remain. Formula metadata reuses the existing workbook inspection pass; ordinary amounts avoid redundant canonical-row copies. No schema, dependency or live data changes.

Compact controls accompany existing temporary validation plans and direct results. Request/file/configuration guards bind footer choices, mapping, dates and selection; configured Footing imports require a matching validated plan. Source confirmation is never stored as a reusable mapping/session default. Existing recovered-import receipts remain unchanged. Phase 3 must add actual stored-SQL assurance, including recovery presentation; Phase 4 preview headlines and Phase 5 full performance acceptance remain pending.

The new SQL helper returns scoped row/document counts and each Footing sum in one parameterized PostgreSQL aggregate, including optional ledger-account scope and invalid-value detection. It is prepared for Phase 3, not called during Phase 2 validation and not exercised against live PostgreSQL. Full-sheet footer matching does not establish complete-period equality for partial extracts.

Verification: 146 focused backend and 32 browser checks pass across recorded runs, covering footer selection, strict inputs, exact decimals, cached/missing formulas, repeated lines, partial exclusions, empty reports, stale plans, bypass prevention, safe text and 390/768/1280px layout. Python/JavaScript syntax, scoped whitespace and documentation budgets pass. The supplied Vouchers sheet matches 116 details, 29 documents and Debit/Credit 77,108,960 each; row 118 agrees and source positions 2–117 remain intact. The workbook was read only. Two control passes over 100,000 synthetic rows/50,000 documents took 0.609 seconds with zero SQL calls; this excludes workbook parsing, matching and import. Broader ledger tests expose unchanged template-query and retired-receipt fixture failures; those files were not changed. The exact commit snapshot passed 199 isolated checks; six legacy input-error HTTP fixtures were excluded after their missing settings mock reproduced on unchanged HEAD. Unrelated Drive/backup changes were excluded. Aadil confirmed manual Footing checks and authorized the Phase 2 commit/push on 2026-11-06.

## Template comparison settings — Phase 1.1 — 2026-11-05

Selected template columns now show one Compare for changes heading with a checkbox per row, alongside the independent reconciliation role. Defaults are checked for every field except the configured Account Ledger Balance. Edits remain local until Save Template; older API edits preserve existing choices. Prepared-ledger creation follows the same defaults. Upload no longer offers comparison checkboxes or applies client-saved choices; server-side comparison ignores legacy request overrides. Unchecked-field refresh/history semantics are retained.

Nullable comparison values and a conflict-review flag are stored on template mappings. Idempotent PostgreSQL/SQLite upgrades preserve unanimous old client choices and flag disagreements for explicit template review; unresolved conflicts block validation. Header-mapping saves preserve retained legacy values without making them authoritative. Template saves supersede pending plans and fingerprints include policy metadata. New/old setup backups preserve scoped choices or identify legacy conflicts before restore writes.

The upgrade passed isolated agreement/conflict/rollback tests and a live rollback rehearsal, then was committed: 35,867 source rows and 93 mappings unchanged, six existing settings preserved, zero conflicts. A read-only call to the new handler verified seven templates/93 fields; Account Ledger Balance is the sole unchecked field. The initial running process needed a restart before acceptance.

Verification: 127 affected template/duplicate/lifecycle/dialog tests pass; two focused policy tests additionally verify request-override rejection and stale-plan fingerprints. An offline browser preview confirms the shared heading and checkbox-only cells. Syntax and scoped whitespace checks pass. Aadil accepted Phases 1/1.1 and authorized their combined commit/push, limited to this work. Transaction data was not rewritten. The exact staged snapshot passed 156 isolated tests; pending Drive/backup/cleanup work was excluded.

## Template-specific reconciliation roles — Phase 1 correction — 2026-11-05

Safety review found global roles incorrectly classify shared references: PO No can identify Purchase Orders while remaining a reference in GRN/Vendor Bill. The earlier global-role design below is superseded. Existing Text/Numeric/Date values and all transaction identities remain unchanged; no Git reset/revert was used.

Role selectors now belong to each selected column in Create/Edit Template and save through Save Template. Master-column editing returns to base types. Template APIs, upload configuration/fingerprints, previews/counts and setup backup/restore read template_column_mappings.reconciliation_role. One Document ID and multiple numeric Footing fields are supported independently per template; multiple document values/repeated detail occurrences remain preserved. Existing unsafe identity changes still block for reviewed migration.

Fresh schemas have no global role field. Existing databases retain the obsolete master field without using it at runtime. A transactional, one-time mapping upgrade preserves a legacy Document ID where it was the first key or its template already has data; empty reference-only templates do not inherit it. Legacy global Footing choices require explicit template selection. Startup conversion preserves source rows/links, supersedes old plans and never repeats inheritance after local edits. Backup role validation occurs before restore opens a connection.

Phase 2 remains pending; Phase 3 still reconciles approved Excel detail against stored SQL in Import Successful. No live database startup/migration, client upload, package installation, stage, commit or push was performed. Local acceptance remains required.

Verification: 118 template/duplicate/lifecycle/dialog tests pass. Tests cover independent PO/GRN roles, omitted-role compatibility, master-type preservation, migration idempotence/source preservation and pre-connection backup validation. A broader preview run reports 65 passed/one unchanged Data Bank action-expectation failure. Syntax/whitespace checks pass; an offline screenshot confirms the existing template editor fits the controls. PostgreSQL DDL remains mock-verified rather than exercised against a live server.

## Import reconciliation column roles — Phase 1 — 2026-11-05

Setup offers Text - Document ID and Numeric - Footing with concise guidance. Base types remain Text/Numeric; nullable reconciliation_role metadata is added for fresh/existing PostgreSQL and SQLite schemas. Existing roles are not assigned automatically. Column/template APIs and backup restore carry the metadata.

One configured Document ID column governs upload grouping, critical-field validation, document labels, row-selection hints, Data Bank grouping and distinct counts. It supports many document values per voucher and repeated lines; occurrence-based transaction identities remain separate. Multiple ID columns in one template are rejected. Unconfigured templates retain legacy behaviour.

Shared-column/template edits serialize configuration checks, invalidate pending plans and refresh caches after commit. Marking the current key retains stored identities. Selecting a different key is allowed only when existing values agree; identity-changing edits are blocked for a separately reviewed migration. No source rows, verification links or financial values are rewritten. Ledger Voucher-role compatibility remains enforced.

Footing is metadata in this phase; mandatory source-footer checks follow in Phase 2. No live database migration/import or Git mutation was performed. Local acceptance is pending.

Verification: 16 focused role/schema/form/preservation tests pass; the wider run reports 243 passed/33 failed (32 legacy upload-count tests with documented fixture/message issues; one Data Bank action expectation). The three-file focused run reports 61 passed/that same Data Bank failure. These unrelated fixtures were not changed. Python/JavaScript syntax and scoped whitespace checks pass. Read-only workbook processing produces 116 source lines, 29 document groups and 116 distinct line identities. PostgreSQL DDL is tested with mocks; a real server upgrade remains for local acceptance.

## Template deletion and storage closure — 2026-11-04

The agreed deletion/re-upload plan includes two accepted scope changes: administrator deletion works on local and Render, and Account Ledger workbook compatibility remains deferred. Data Bank's bin offers backup/delete or cancel, prepares all current rows on Data and prior rows on Changed-Deleted History, starts the XLSX download, then invokes protected-reference/fresh-preview-gated purge. Full database backups remain optional and separate. Browser initiation cannot certify that the user saved the download. Phases 1–2 were pushed as a6891e7f and 76f7b03d; scoped purge removes source/history, derived links, upload/validation/lifecycle metadata and matching deletion audit entries without creating another deletion receipt, while retaining reusable cross-module settings. The standard-template re-upload check matched all 8,013 Purchase Order rows/16 fields and numeric totals, with fresh upload/creation details and no imported history sheet. Existing attribution/date/history-indicator limitations are recorded in KNOWN_ISSUES.md.

Phase 3.1 distinguishes live records from allocated files and reusable pages. Storage Cleanup inventories all 96 public tables, labels estimates/unavailable evidence, shows automatic-vacuum/audit allocation and keeps index decisions separate. Dashboard size is labelled Allocated Database Size. No index was removed based on size, overlap or scan count; no automatic rebuild or VACUUM FULL was added. The safeguards addition was accepted/pushed as 8014b8b9 and remains a check of the defined baseline, not a physical index-entry inspection or a speed/storage guarantee.

The approved finalization service is operator-only, with no new API/startup/UI action. A fresh content-bound preview and exact confirmation authorize one scoped old audit entry plus the eight existing empty classification-table indexes. NOWAIT locks reject a busy table; nonempty tables, changed definitions/evidence or protected-value mismatches abort and roll back together. Writes are never retried. Its read-only controls compare complete row-value fingerprints in 93 public tables and all 281 index definitions; sessions, presence and error traffic are explicitly excluded, alongside only the approved audit row. No duplicate records or maintenance receipt are stored in the database. The isolated rehearsal guard still rejects live targets.

Verification: 168 tests and 52 subtests pass across cleanup, deletion, duplicate, integrity/UI and pool coverage; one broader upload-receipt fixture still expects the retired lifecycle contract (KNOWN_ISSUES.md). Real isolated PostgreSQL exercised 20,000 unchanged synthetic source rows, stale/nonempty/busy rejection and rollback after an actual rebuild. No package installation. Approved live finalization removed only Leather Crop/Purchase Order audit entry 5534. Classification allocation fell from 10,420,224 to 90,112 bytes: 10,330,112 bytes (9.85 MiB) recovered; all eight index definitions remain, using 65,536 bytes. Database allocation fell from 271,076,499 to 260,746,387 bytes (258.5 to 248.7 displayed MB). Independent committed-state reads matched all protected fingerprints/index definitions, found zero remaining scoped deletion audit entries, retained module inventory values and passed all 14 safeguards. Counts remain 97,979 Client Data / 2,986 Trial Balance / zero reconciliation inputs; 49 unavailable staged files limit size measurement only.

Authenticated Playwright confirms the live dashboard shows 248.7 MB, Data Integrity refresh remains Passed, Module inventory/Data Bank retain the verified counts, and the purge preview reports zero scoped deletion audit entries. Storage Cleanup renders 96 tables, updated explanations and no added mutation controls; 320/390/1280px layouts have no page overflow, with readable rows and horizontal table scrolling. JavaScript/Python syntax, whitespace and documentation budgets pass. File_Map's 158 existing lines were rewritten without expansion. Private evidence is outside Git under the session's visualization directory (template-finalization-live-result.json, before/after controls, native-rehearsal and browser results). Aadil accepted closure and authorised the final scoped commit/push. The plan, including additions, is closed; Account Ledger compatibility and finer deletion-role assignments remain future scope. Unrelated Drive-retirement changes are excluded.

## Transaction change history — Phase 2 — 2026-11-03

Added `client_data_history` in SQLite and PostgreSQL for full prior-row snapshots when imports change or remove active transactions. PostgreSQL startup now ensures the table and scope/time index for both fresh and already-bootstrapped databases. The import writes history in the same transaction as replacement, preserving rollback safety; `client_data.created_at` records newly added rows. Both import paths retain snapshots with source/replacing upload IDs and identity. Scoped permanent purge deletes matching history; replacement purge preserves it. Duplicate comparison and active identity gates are unchanged.

## In-app Google Drive reconnect — 2026-11-03

## Storage Cleanup 503 fix - 2026-10-12

**Root cause:** The `client_data` index inventory query called `pg_relation_size(indexrelid)` while joining `pg_stat_user_indexes` and `pg_index`; PostgreSQL rejected the unqualified column as ambiguous.

**Fix and verification:** Qualified the expression as `pg_relation_size(stats.indexrelid)` and added a regression assertion. A fresh database-connected server returned HTTP 200 from `/api/storage-cleanup/preview`; Playwright confirmed the Storage Cleanup page displayed a fresh preview and 16 index rows. The optional `pgstatindex` function is unavailable in the current database, so the UI correctly reports bloat evidence unavailable and blocks reindexing. No data or indexes were changed.

Playwright login with `codex` and Leather Crop confirmed live Data Bank values of 105,471 records, 58.4 MB, and 6 templates. No cleanup, index maintenance, or database mutation was performed; the database is not certified fully optimized until a fresh live preview succeeds.

## Locked upload and deletion contract - 2026-10-11

**Historical:** This contract and the duplicate-gate entries below predate the current history and legitimate line-multiplicity policy. Follow CLAUDE.md, Database management and backup rules; the old results remain historical evidence.


**Decision:** `client_data` is the only durable canonical transaction set. Raw values and report-required derived columns stay together; reports and analysis do not receive a second transaction copy. Upload validation must count exact duplicate lines, retain only the first copy, stop an unchanged previously imported file as a no-op, apply corrections in place, insert new/backdated rows once, and block conflicting identities before a write.

**Deletion boundary:** The guarded administrator preview/apply flow is the only source-data deletion path. It permanently removes canonical rows, derived classifications, occurrence metadata, audit payloads, upload metadata, validation plans, and staged files. Soft-delete and restore are blocked. A successful logical purge may leave PostgreSQL table/index pages and bloat; that physical compaction is a separate approved maintenance operation, not retained client data.

**Live evidence:** Playwright testing used the Leather Crop Jan-26 workbook: the first import produced 3,514 canonical rows; an unchanged re-upload reported 3,514 existing, 0 new, and no-op; a changed copy reported 1 changed, 0 new, and 3,513 unchanged; guarded purge removed 3,514 source rows plus related occurrence/audit/upload metadata and returned zero logical rows. The final physical database reading was about 79.1 MB because PostgreSQL pages/indexes were not vacuumed.

**Deferred controls:** Import-path 300/400 MB enforcement, production backup/export gating, stable source line identifiers for reorder-safe corrections, and Data Bank UI wiring to permanent purge remain separate work. Two protected external backups and quarterly restore tests remain mandatory policy.

## Single-source data management and backup policy — Phase 1 — 2026-10-10

**Status:** Documentation complete. **Files:** `CLAUDE.md`, `CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md`, `KNOWN_ISSUES.md`.

**Decision:** `client_data` is the only canonical transaction set. A stable client/template/transaction identity may exist once in the active set; raw values and report-required derived columns live together and are indexed. Repeated cumulative uploads compare normalized identity and fingerprint: unchanged rows are skipped, corrections update in place, and newly supplied backdated rows are inserted once.

**Storage boundary:** Durable transaction copies in classifications, occurrence registers, prepared lines/rollups, report snapshots, and historical revisions are not part of the target policy. They are legacy migration targets and must not grow. Configuration, compact audit metadata, counts, fingerprints, checksums, and procedure/run metadata remain allowed where operationally necessary.

**Backup boundary:** Source workbooks, exports, SQL dumps, reports, and workpapers remain external/offline. Supabase stores no backup files. Production deletion requires an approved scoped export or logical dump as appropriate, two protected backup copies, and tested restoration; development deletion remains temporarily exempt per the existing rule.

## Database management and backup policy - Phase 1 - 2026-10-09

**Status:** Historical baseline; current rules, including scoped change history, are in CLAUDE.md, Database management and backup rules. **Files:** `CLAUDE.md`, `CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md`.

**Decision:** Supabase is the production working store, not the permanent archive. Keep one active client dataset/import, retain only current operational rows, prevent duplicate re-imports through normalized source and row identity, and keep generated files outside Supabase.

**Controls:** Client deletion requires a scoped CSV/XLSX export package; whole-database or schema destruction requires a logical SQL dump. Backups must have two protected external copies and quarterly restore tests. Supabase retains only compact metadata, counts, fingerprints, checksums, and necessary procedure definitions/run summaries.

**Capacity and maintenance:** Warn at 300 MB, stop new imports at 400 MB, and never intentionally approach the 500 MB Free-plan quota. Keep only primary/unique and measured query indexes; inspect bloat after large deletes and reserve `VACUUM FULL` or compaction for approved maintenance.

**Boundary:** This phase changes documentation only. No live cleanup, deletion, migration, schema change, backup upload, or code implementation was performed. Later phases will implement and verify these controls.

## Cashflows performance-balancing plan — 2026-09-29

**Desi operating model:** upload transactions once, derive Month/Fortnight and other period keys at upload time, store the prepared rows, and let Cashflows read them like an Excel PivotTable. Raw transaction rows remain read-only; a re-upload replaces the active source, while a category or treasury change invalidates and rebuilds affected preparation.

**Integrity rule:** prepared results are valid only for the same client, template/upload set, configuration, receipt presentation, and source date bounds. If preparation is unavailable, Cashflows falls back to the canonical transaction calculation; no optimization may silently omit rows or alter totals.

**Performance levers:** use vectorized pandas derivation for deterministic period fields, bulk database writes inside one transaction, fewer repeated database round-trips during mapping and validation, bounded stale-connection retries, and prepared daily rollups for selected report groupings. JavaScript caching/compression is secondary because report responses are already small; the measured delay is server/database waiting.

**Measured starting point:** the 3536-row workbook uploaded in 1.36 seconds and auto-mapped in 1.68 seconds; mapping persistence took 14.63 seconds; validation waited 70.4 seconds before an SSL/database EOF failure. These timings make database round-trips and connection recovery the first balancing target.

**Acceptance checks:** compare upload, mapping, validation, import, first Cashflows load, and repeat load timings; reconcile daily, fortnightly, monthly, quarterly, half-yearly, and annual totals against the canonical source; verify that category/configuration changes rebuild or safely fall back without stale results.

**Phase implementation:** saved mapping replacement now uses one atomic transaction and bulk insert; Cashflows snapshot preparation is scheduled after the import response, while canonical data remains the safe fallback until preparation completes.

**Technique check:** local parsing of the 3536-row workbook took 1.376 seconds, while vectorized Month/Fortnight derivation took 0.014 seconds. Vectorization is worthwhile for derived fields, but database round-trips and Supabase connection stability remain the dominant constraint; JavaScript optimization is secondary for these small response payloads.

**Balancing implementation:** validation now counts exact JSONB row matches inside PostgreSQL instead of downloading historical rows; the controlled 3536-row validation fell from 12.8–19.1 seconds to 4.0 seconds with counts unchanged. Import change detection now compares each document as an exact normalized row multiset, so harmless line reordering does not trigger writes; the repeat controlled import reported 3536 unchanged rows and 0 updates in 7.1 seconds. The remaining import cost is primarily the historical `row_data` read (about 4.5 seconds in the final run), so the 2–3 second target is not yet claimed.

## Verification Speed Optimization — Phase 4 — 2026-09-22

**Scope:** historical working-tree experiment only; no Phase 4 code is retained.

This working-tree experiment followed a live HAR trace showing `save_and_verify_voucher_bundle` taking 7.6s for a
2-line voucher (captured right after the Postgres migration fix above got Save/Verify working
again), `compute_and_persist_cleared_status()` — already named in `PERFORMANCE_INVESTIGATION.md`
as firing "6-10+ sequential, non-batched" queries per line — still had 5 genuinely independent,
still-separate `execute_query_pg()` calls reading this specific voucher line's own recorded state
(linked evidence, signature exceptions, procedure ticks, Form values, voucher-check ticks). Step 6
(Rulebook snapshots, above) had already eliminated the other 4 round-trips that read rule
*definitions*; these 5 read this line's own *state*, so they can't be snapshotted the same way.

Combined into one query using CTEs, each wrapped in `COALESCE(json_agg(...), '[]')` so an
unmatched CTE returns an empty list rather than SQL NULL — the same "skip when the id set is
empty" behaviour the removed per-query `if ...:` guards gave, now expressed as an empty `ANY(%s)`
array matching zero rows. Every `WHERE` clause is byte-identical to the query it replaces; only
the number of round trips changes (5 → 1). `checked_at`/`entry_updated_at` are pulled as
`EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM ...)` rather than left as `timestamptz`, since `json_agg` serializes
timestamps to text and `_ts_sort_key()`'s comparisons require real `datetime` objects — a small
`_epoch_to_ts()` helper converts them straight back (both columns are `TIMESTAMPTZ`, matching
`_MIN_TS`'s own tz-aware UTC, confirmed against the Postgres schema before writing the query).
`json_agg`/named dict params are new to this codebase but standard, mature psycopg2/Postgres
features; `= ANY(%s)` array params were already this file's own established pattern.

Deliberately excluded from this pass (kept small per the user's "safe limits" instruction): the
category-resolution lookup a few lines above (`upload_rows`/`tb_rows`/`assignment_rows` — a true
sequential dependency, only runs once per line's lifetime since Category freezes after first
save), `evaluate_cross_checks_for_line()` and `_get_voucher_line_physical_bills()` (separate,
independently-reused functions), and `_has_pending_account_head_note()`/
`_has_voucher_line_correct_confirmation()`.

**Verification:** 6 new tests added — one asserting the combined query's SQL text references all
5 expected tables and executes as a single round trip, five parametrized scenarios (all
satisfied; required role not ticked; linked-template doc not linked; signature exception flagged;
voucher check not ticked) proving the unpacked combined-query result drives the same Cleared/
Query outcome the five separate queries gave, including the epoch-timestamp round-trip actually
exercised. Full `tests/` suite: 301 passed, 36 subtests passed, 17 failed, 1 error — identical
failing/erroring test list to the pre-change baseline (already individually confirmed pre-existing
against `HEAD` during the Postgres migration fix above); no new failure. Live server restart and a
real Save/Verify retest (ideally with the endpoint's existing `?perf=true` component timing) to
confirm the actual round-trip reduction against real Postgres remains the user's to do.

The diagnostic response is deliberately opt-in: only `?perf=true` adds `_perf` (request total,
database calls/reads/writes/database time) and `_perf_components` (line saves, support-data writes,
post-support status evaluation, and verification). The ordinary response remains unchanged. Its
wrapper now preserves an error response even when diagnostics are requested, and focused HTTP
coverage confirms the unchanged ordinary contract, diagnostic shape, and validation-error path.

Opening the Verification page with `?perf=true` now carries this existing opt-in flag through only
the normal Save/Verify request, so no DevTools command is needed. `?perf=1` remains supported for
existing diagnostic bookmarks; ordinary pages issue the unchanged request and expose no timings.

**Outcome:** live Save/Verify captures ranged from about 7 to 21 seconds, with virtually all time
spent waiting for the server. The first two final captures (7.02s and 7.47s) matched the earlier
7.6s baseline, while a comparable save still reached 14.25s. The CTE did not produce a repeatable
benefit, so it and its fixtures were removed. The separate Rulebook snapshot safety design remains
retained; remote Supabase/service latency is the remaining practical limitation.

## Cross-Check Matrix Redesign

**Requirement:** Rebuild the Audit Rules Cross-Check feature as a document × field matrix —
Documents are columns, user-added field rows have no stored label (row ID + order only), and each
cell holds a column name picked from that Document's linked template (empty cell = not applicable).
Also removes the duplicate cross-check-eligible fields section from the Documents tab. Old
cross-check data is discarded/rebuilt, not migrated. 5 phases: (1) DB storage, (2) backend CRUD +
template column-list lookup, (3) remove Documents-tab fields section, (4) build matrix UI,
(5) wire UI to backend.

### Phase 1 of 5 — DB storage

**Date:** 2026-09-01 | **Files:** `database.py` (committed). Schema test class
`CrossCheckMatrixSchemaTests` written and passing but **held out of this commit** — it shares
`tests/test_audit_rulebook.py` with an in-flight Phase 4 of the earlier per-document-field
requirement; it lands with a later commit. Backup:
`scratchpad/test_audit_rulebook_with_matrix.py`.

Additive schema change — two new tables in both `init_db()` (SQLite) and `init_db_postgres()`:

- `audit_rule_cross_check_fields` — the row axis. `id`, `cross_check_id` (FK → `audit_rule_cross_checks`,
  `ON DELETE CASCADE`), `sort_order`. No label column; a row is identified by its id, order by
  `sort_order`.
- `audit_rule_cross_check_cells` — one row per (field row × Document) cell. `id`,
  `field_id` (FK → `audit_rule_cross_check_fields`, CASCADE), `document_id` (FK →
  `audit_rule_documents`, CASCADE), `column_name TEXT` nullable (`NULL`/missing cell = not
  applicable), `UNIQUE(field_id, document_id)`. `column_name` is free text, not FK'd — validity
  against the Document's linked template is a Phase 2 backend concern, matching how the existing
  `compare_field` columns are already free text.

Indexes: `idx_audit_rule_cross_check_fields_crosscheck`, `idx_audit_rule_cross_check_cells_field`.

The document column axis reuses the existing `audit_rule_cross_check_documents` junction unchanged.

**Deliberately deferred to Phase 2:** the old `compare_field` columns on `audit_rule_cross_checks`
and `audit_rule_cross_check_documents` are left in place this phase so `routers/audit_rules.py`
(untouched here) and the current tests keep working. No data migration/purge code — old rows are
discarded as a separate cleanup later. Confirmed with Aadil: additive, keep old columns.

`CrossCheckMatrixSchemaTests` covers table shapes, `column_name` NULL, the
`UNIQUE(field_id, document_id)` constraint, and cell CASCADE on field-row delete (the CASCADE
test enables `PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON` locally since the app never does).

### Phase 2 of 5 — matrix CRUD + column lookup

**Date:** 2026-09-01 | **Files:** `routers/audit_rules.py`, `routers/templates.py`,
`tests/test_audit_rulebook.py` (the held-back schema tests land here too).

**Scope change from the brief, confirmed with Aadil:** the brief assumed the old `compare_field`
columns get dropped this phase. They don't — they're still consumed by the flat Cross-check CRUD,
`compile_verification_rulebook()`, the `verification.py` cross-check evaluation engine, guidance
emission, the frontend editor, and tests, and no phase in the 5-phase plan rewires the engine to
the matrix. The column drop is deferred to a later phase (after the matrix UI lands and a phase
migrates the engine). This phase is purely additive.

Also: the superseded in-flight "per-document field names Phase 4" WIP
(`routers/audit_rules.py` + `verification.py` + two test files) was **discarded** (`git restore`)
— the matrix generalises that concept, so finishing the old approach is wasted work.

New endpoints (all in `routers/audit_rules.py` unless noted; mutations gated by
`ensure_no_active_verification_sessions` + `invalidate_audit_rules_cache`, cross-checks are
global so no `client_id`):

- `GET /api/audit-rules/cross-checks/{id}/matrix` — one call returns ordered document columns
  (`document_id`, `name`, `template_id`, `sort_order`) + ordered field rows, each row's `cells`
  as `{ "<document_id>": "<column_name|null>" }`. Read-through the `cache_get`/`cache_set` layer,
  key `cross_checks:matrix:{id}`.
- `POST /api/audit-rules/cross-checks/{id}/fields` — append a label-less field row
  (`sort_order` = current max + 1). Returns `{field_id}`.
- `DELETE /api/audit-rules/cross-check-fields/{field_id}` — deletes the row; clears its cells
  explicitly first (FKs aren't enforced on this app's connections; Postgres would cascade anyway).
- `PUT /api/audit-rules/cross-checks/{id}/field-order` — body `{field_ids: [...]}`, must be an
  exact permutation of the cross-check's current field-row ids (400 otherwise); rewrites
  `sort_order` = list index.
- `PUT /api/audit-rules/cross-check-fields/{field_id}/cells/{document_id}` — body
  `{column_name}`. 404 unknown field row; 400 if the document isn't a column of that cross-check;
  400 if a non-empty `column_name` isn't a real column on the document's linked template. Non-empty
  → `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (field_id, document_id) DO UPDATE`; empty/None → `DELETE` the cell
  (= not applicable).
- `GET /api/templates/{template_id}/columns` (`routers/templates.py`) — thin wrapper over the
  existing `get_cached_template_columns()` (shared TTL-cached column source); returns
  `[{column_id, column_name, data_type, sort_order}]`, 404 on inactive/missing template. The
  reusable "column-list by template" the matrix UI (Phase 4) calls per distinct `template_id`.

Helpers: `get_document_template_columns(document_id)` (resolves `template_id`, reuses
`get_cached_template_columns` via a local import to keep the router import graph acyclic),
`validate_cross_check_cell()`, `get_cross_check_matrix()`. Models: `CrossCheckFieldOrder`,
`CrossCheckCellUpdate`. Full suite: 83 passed.

## Cross-check per-document field names

**Superseded 2026-09-01 by the Cross-Check Matrix Redesign (above).** Phases 1–3 shipped
(commits `ffe8b12`, `e87d586`, `a52a615`); Phase 4 (engine/guidance wiring) was in progress,
never committed, and discarded — the matrix generalises per-document field names, so the flat
`compare_field` model is on its way out entirely.

**Date:** 2026-09-01 | **Files:** `database.py`, `tests/test_audit_rulebook.py`.

Confirmed 4-phase requirement. Cross-checks currently force one shared `compare_field` name
across every Document in the chain. Quantity fields are now named differently per stage
("Quantity" for PO / Purchase Demand vs "Quantity Received" for Store Receiving / Vendor Bill),
so a Cross-check must support a different field name per Document, matched by chain
position / comparison intent rather than by identical name.

**Phase 1 of 4 — schema only (this entry).** Added a nullable `compare_field TEXT` column to the
`audit_rule_cross_check_documents` junction table (both SQLite `init_db()` and Postgres
`init_db_postgres()`), plus an idempotent backfill that copies each parent Cross-check's shared
`audit_rule_cross_checks.compare_field` onto its junction rows where the new column is still NULL.
A NULL junction value therefore means "fall back to the parent's shared field", and every existing
Cross-check is backfilled on the next startup so nothing breaks or needs re-saving. SQLite upgrade
uses the established PRAGMA-gated `ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN` + `UPDATE ... WHERE compare_field IS NULL`
pattern (runs every startup, cheap no-op once populated); Postgres uses
`ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS` + an `UPDATE ... FROM` backfill. New-DB CREATE TABLE statements carry the
column directly. Two tests added (`CrossCheckPerDocumentFieldSchemaTests`): column presence, and
backfill of a NULL junction row from the parent's shared field after a re-run of `init_db()`.

Locked assumptions: eligible-fields sourcing (global active-Master-Columns mirror) unchanged and
out of scope; `comparison_type` logic unaffected; `compare_to_voucher_line` stays a single anchor
field; UI (Phase 3) shows one field-picker per Document row, not a matrix.

**Phase 2 of 4 — backend validation / save / response (`routers/audit_rules.py`,
`tests/test_audit_rulebook.py`, `tests/test_verification_performance_metrics.py`).** Both
Cross-check request models (`CrossCheckCreate` / `CrossCheckUpdate`) gain
`document_fields: Dict[int, Optional[str]] = {}` — an optional `document_id -> own compare_field`
map. `normalize_compare_field()` (new helper) trims a value and treats blank as `None`.
`save_cross_check_documents()` now writes the junction `compare_field` column per row from that
map (absent / blank -> NULL). `validate_cross_check_payload()` no longer does a single-name
intersection across every Document: per Document it resolves the *effective* field
(`own override or shared compare_field`) and checks that against that Document's own
`get_document_cross_check_fields()`; the 400 message names the effective field.
`get_cross_check_documents()` takes the shared field as a second arg and each returned document
dict now carries `compare_field` (own, nullable) and `effective_compare_field` (own or shared);
`row_to_cross_check()` passes `row["compare_field"]` through. Top-level `compare_field` on
`audit_rule_cross_checks` untouched (still the fallback). Backward compatible: a client sending
only `document_ids` writes all-NULL junction rows -> every Document uses the shared field, exactly
as before. Five unit tests added (patched pg helpers, existing pattern in the file).

**Phase 3 of 4 — per-Document field-picker UI (`static/audit_rules.html`,
`static/audit_rules.js`; frontend only, no backend touched).** The Cross-check editor's
Documents list (`renderCrossCheckDocsList()`) now renders an inline `<select>` per row,
scoped to that Document's own eligible fields (new `eligibleFieldsForDoc(docId)` =
`getDocumentById(docId).cross_check_fields`, no intersection — mirrors Phase 2's
per-Document server check). New page state `crossCheckDocFields = {docId: field}` holds
explicit overrides only (keyed by docId so it survives reorder; pruned on remove; reset in
`startNewCrossCheck()`; hydrated in `selectCrossCheck()` from each `cc.documents[].compare_field`
— the raw override, not `effective_compare_field`). A blank row's first option reads
`(use default: <field>)` and is omitted from the save payload so the backend stores NULL.
The old shared `#arCompareFieldSelect` is relabelled "Default field to compare" and its
options are now the **union** of all selected Documents' eligible fields
(`computeEligibleFields()` changed from intersection); still required on save as the
fallback. Amber `.ar-field-warning` now renders per-row: when a saved override is no longer
eligible on that Document (stale value kept visible as a `⚠️` option), or when a blank
row's fallback default isn't eligible there. Save payload adds
`document_fields: {docId: field}` for explicit picks only, per Phase 2's contract.
`updateCompareToVoucherLineHint()` now shows the anchor's *effective* field
(`crossCheckDocFields[anchorId] || shared`). Default-dropdown render reordered before the
docs-list render so `(use default: …)` labels are correct on first open; the shared
dropdown's `change` re-renders the docs list. Inline `<select>` sizing only (margin/maxWidth/
fontSize set in JS) — no `style.css` change, no stylesheet `?v=` bump; `audit_rules.js?v=7 -> ?v=8`.
Full backend suite (66) still green; `node --check` passes.

Deferred to Phase 4 (validation engine): `compile_verification_rulebook()` and
`get_category_guidance_cross_checks()` still emit only the shared `compare_field`.

Later phase: 4 — validation engine (`routers/verification.py`) compares using each
document's own field name.

## Code Health Review — Rulebook and shared-modal reconciliation

**Date:** 2026-08-31 | **Scope:** `routers/audit_rules.py`, `routers/verification.py`,
`routers/templates.py`, `database.py`, `static/procedure_modal.js`, `static/verification.js`,
`static/audit_workbook.js`, `KNOWN_ISSUES.md`, `DEVELOPMENT_PLAN.md`.

Claude's six reported findings were independently compared with the current source and commit
history. Finding 1 is superseded rather than current: `a09258a` used the overly broad
`verification_sessions.status = 'In Progress'` guard, but `d7a7c6f` replaced it with the current
`verification_presence` lease query requiring an unended heartbeat within 90 seconds. Therefore
old In Progress sessions do not currently create the reported permanent Audit Rules lock. The
missing terminal session lifecycle remains a separate design pendency for cleanup and reporting.

Finding 2 is confirmed and high risk. `_audit_rules_config_version` is process-local and starts at 1
after a restart, while existing sessions retain their captured version. Template/master-column
invalidation also increments the same version. `load_verification_rulebook_for_session()` rejects
any mismatch with HTTP 409 and is used by session activation, line saves, grouped Save/Verify,
voucher-check verification, and status-reason reads. A controlled restart-safe compatibility or
recovery design is required before treating the Rulebook lock as complete.

Finding 3 is confirmed as a shared-host contract regression. The voucher-level check controls in
`procedure_modal.js` currently issue immediate individual/batch writes for both hosts, while the
Verification close/grouped path also submits the state. The Audit Workbook requirement for direct
persistence and Verification's local-first/grouped requirement must be separated explicitly; the
current behavior can perform duplicate idempotent writes and undermines the intended network-saving
design.

Finding 4 is confirmed as a display-only Rulebook adapter defect. Verification maps Rulebook
documents and roles but passes cross-checks through without converting `document_ids` to document
names or exposing document-level `cross_check_fields`. Audit Workbook's
`awRulebookCategoryToGuidance()` already contains the proven normalization pattern. No status gate
or audit conclusion is changed, but the Verification guidance popover can omit the visible chain.

Findings 5 and 6 are valid deferred hardening items. The sibling-ID memo is held in a ContextVar and
is not automatically available in ThreadPoolExecutor workers, so concurrent modal helpers can repeat
the resolution. Audit Workbook's observation and no-match-note flushes occur before its `try`, so a
flush failure can bypass the adapter's `{ok, data/error}` contract. Neither changes current audit
conclusions; both should be addressed only after the correctness fixes.

Additional unique pendencies recorded in the plan are explicit terminal Verification-session
lifecycle design, targeted regression tests for version drift/restart recovery and host-specific
voucher-check behavior, and reconciliation of stale historical Markdown status lines. The full
current test suite passes 49 tests with four non-blocking warnings; earlier Postgres-cutover failure
notes are stale and should not be treated as active failures.

The final stabilization order is: Rulebook recovery, shared-modal host gating, Verification guidance
normalization, Safety Phase A/B acceptance, targeted regression coverage, deferred hardening only if
still justified, documentation/Git closeout, then real product development. Further Supabase/free-tier
performance tuning remains deferred because the measured variability is infrastructure/connection
wait dominated and no safe additional rewrite is proven.

## Audit Workbook voucher-check persistence regression

**Date:** 2026-08-31 | **Files:** `static/procedure_modal.js`, `DEVELOPMENT_PLAN.md`,
`CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md`, `KNOWN_ISSUES.md`.

The Audit Workbook Procedure Modal's voucher-level check handlers contained unreachable returns
immediately before the existing individual and batch save requests. The UI therefore changed check
states locally but never persisted them. Verify and Verify & Next then reached the backend with
server-side checks still `untouched`, producing the expected HTTP 400 response.

Only those two returns were removed. The existing optimistic update, API persistence, failure
rollback, button gating, and Verify flow were preserved. Automated browser regression against
session 877 confirmed: individual check save HTTP 200, batch check save HTTP 200, Verify HTTP 200,
and Verify & Next HTTP 200, with no page errors. `node --check` passed. Aadil then manually
confirmed the target Audit Workbook flow is performing well. This phase is ready for Git staging,
commit, and push.

## Audit Workbook Rulebook reuse

Audit Workbook's adapter supplied ordinary line saving but not Verification's optional grouped
`saveAndVerifyVoucher()` method. The shared modal close handler called that method unconditionally,
so its `×` button raised `hostAdapter.saveAndVerifyVoucher is not a function` and left the modal
open. Audit Workbook's `awSaveLineItems()` also returned no result after a successful save, so the
shared Verify fallback treated the save as failed and did not call `verify_voucher_checks`.

host's ordinary line save. `awSaveLineItems()` now returns the shared `{ok, data/error}` contract;
its database payload, status patch, cache invalidation, and table refresh are unchanged.

Browser regression testing confirmed that `×` closes after saving, `✅ Verify` calls
`save_line_items` and `verify_voucher_checks` with HTTP 200 and closes, and `✅ Verify & Next Line`
calls both endpoints with HTTP 200 and begins the next-line transition. No page errors were
observed. Both changed JavaScript files passed `node --check`; the focused dirty-save suite passed
9 tests. Aadil manually confirmed the target behavior; this phase is ready for Git commit/push.

approximately 0.72 seconds of Rulebook/audited work before a roughly 2.38-second `/next` request.

dominant remaining read and extra concurrent pool work could worsen free-tier Supabase latency.

`node --check static/verification.js` passed, and `tests/test_verification_performance_metrics.py`

## Audit Workbook batched voucher-support fetch

Frontend-only (`static/audit_workbook.js` + `?v=6` bump in `static/audit_workbook.html`), no
backend change. Brings Audit Workbook in line with the Verification-side `voucherSupportCache`
fix and resolves the 2026-08-28 KNOWN_ISSUES row for the AW physical_bill completion drift.

**Phase 2a (discovery, no code change):** confirmed the existing
`GET /api/verification/voucher_support_data/{anchor}` endpoint (already used by Verification's
`loadVoucherSupportData()`) covers all four of Audit Workbook's per-line data needs — linked
documents, procedure checks, observations, physical bills — with byte-identical field shapes
(`voucher_line_documents`/`procedure_checks` share the same SQL columns; physical bills go
through the same `_shape_physical_bill()` helper) and equivalent sibling-session resolution.
No endpoint param/response tweak needed; `routers/verification.py` stayed off the file list.

**Phase 2b (implementation):**

- **New voucher-level cache** (`awVoucherSupportCache` / `awVoucherSupportLoading` /
  `awVoucherSupportLoadingAnchor`) + `awLoadVoucherSupportData(anchorUid)` +
  `awInvalidateVoucherSupportCache()` — the direct analog of verification.js's
  `voucherSupportCache` / `loadVoucherSupportData()` / `invalidateVoucherSupportCache()`. One
  `window.ApiUtils.apiFetch('/api/verification/voucher_support_data/{anchor}')` call per voucher
  group (anchor = `voucher.lines[0].detail_id`), result indexed by each line's own `detail_id`.
  The in-flight guard only reuses a pending promise when it's for the **same anchor** — unlike
  verification.js (one voucher on screen at a time), Audit Workbook can refresh lines from
  different vouchers, so a blind reuse could hand back another voucher's data. Fail-soft to `{}`.

- **`awRefreshLineProcedures()` / `awRefreshLineObservations()`** repointed: replaced the
  `Promise.all` of `awFetchAssignedDocumentRecords` / `awFetchProcedureChecksForLine` /
  `awFetchPhysicalBillsForLine` (and, in the observations function, `awFetchLineObservationEntries`)
  with reads off `supportLines[String(uid)].{linked_documents.documents, procedure_checks.checks,
  physical_bills.bills, observations.entries}`. The `needsPhysicalBills` gate is gone — the
  batched fetch returns bills unconditionally (one request regardless). `ensureVoucherChecksLoaded()`
  still runs in parallel, gated on `needsVoucherChecks`, unchanged.

- **`isDocDone` physical_bill branch** ported verbatim from verification.js's
  `updateProceduresCellForLine()`: `physicalBills.filter(b => b.document_id === doc.id)`,
  `docBills.length > 0 && docBills.every(bill => bill_no/bill_date/vendor_name trimmed &&
  bill.bill_total != null)`, `Math.abs(sum of bill_total - voucherLineAmount) <= 0.005`. The old
  code used `physicalBills.find(...)` + `bill.amount` — but the shaped bill has no `amount` field
  (it's `bill_total` + nested `items` since the Multi-Bill/Multi-Line work), so `bill.amount` was
  always `undefined` and **a physical_bill document never counted toward done/total in the AW
  Procedures cell**. Pre-existing bug, fixed here as part of the same file's work.

- **Post-save invalidation:** `awSaveLineItems()` calls `awInvalidateVoucherSupportCache()` in
  its success path (after the `cleared_status` patch). Single chokepoint — covers the adapter's
  `saveLineItems` / `saveAllVoucherLines` and `performVerifyVoucherChecksImpl()`'s fallback save
  (AW's adapter has no `saveAndVerifyVoucher`, so the modal always takes that fallback path).
  Without this, `hideProcedureModalOnly()`'s fire-and-forget badge refresh serves the pre-save
  copy and badges show stale done/total until the page reloads — the exact bug the
  Verification-side fix addressed.

- **Dead code removed:** all four `awFetch*` helpers (`awFetchAssignedDocumentRecords`,
  `awFetchProcedureChecksForLine`, `awFetchPhysicalBillsForLine`, `awFetchLineObservationEntries`)
  plus the `fetchPhysicalBillsForLine: awFetchPhysicalBillsForLine` entry in
  `buildAuditWorkbookAdapter()`. Confirmed the only callers were the code replaced above —
  `procedure_modal.js` never calls these adapter methods (it reads its own `procedure_modal_data`
  composite batch on modal open).

**Untouched:** `awFindLineByDetailId`, `awFetchAuditGuidanceData`, the gating logic, and
`applyFilterAndRender()` are all fetch-agnostic — they operate on already-fetched data and
needed no change. `pytest` → 36 passed (frontend-only change; confirms nothing broke on import).

## voucherSupportCache invalidation after save + dead fetchPhysicalBillsForLine removal

Correctness/staleness fix, no backend changes. Resolves the two 2026-08-28 KNOWN_ISSUES rows for
`voucherSupportCache` staleness and the dead `fetchPhysicalBillsForLine()`.

**Why:** on Verification, the Procedures/Observations column badges are refreshed by
`updateProceduresCellForLine()` / `updateObservationsCellForLine()` (`static/verification.js`),
which read from `loadVoucherSupportData()` — a single voucher-wide cache object
(`voucherSupportCache`, `.lines` keyed by line, anchored on `currentVoucherLines[0].detail_id`).
It was populated once per voucher load and cleared only on voucher navigation
(`seedVoucherLineState()`). After a successful in-modal save/Verify nothing invalidated it, so
`hideProcedureModalOnly()`'s fire-and-forget badge refresh (in `procedure_modal.js`, every close
path — ✕, outside-click, Verify, Verify & Next) recomputed the badges from **pre-save** support
data until the next Prev/Next. Same bug class as the `procedureModalDataCache` staleness fixed
earlier the same day; the voucher-level cache never got the equivalent treatment.

**Changed (`static/verification.js`):**
- New `invalidateVoucherSupportCache()` next to `loadVoucherSupportData()` — nulls
  `voucherSupportCache` + `voucherSupportLoading`, mirroring `invalidateProcedureModalDataForVoucher()`
  in `procedure_modal.js` and the existing hard reset in `seedVoucherLineState()`.
- Called on the success path of `doSaveLineItems()` (covers `verifyVoucherChecks()`'s fallback
  branch and navigation saves via `saveAllVoucherLines()` → `saveLineItems()`, which flush
  observation text) and after `res.ok` in `saveAndVerifyVoucher()` (the bundle path — covers
  `closeProcedureModal()` and `verifyVoucherChecks()`'s primary branch).
- Removed the now-dead `fetchPhysicalBillsForLine()` and its `buildProcedureModalAdapter()` entry
  — no call site anywhere; the badge path reads `loadVoucherSupportData()`, `procedure_modal.js`

## Procedure modal cache invalidation after bundle save

`procedureModalDataCache` (`static/procedure_modal.js`, keyed per voucher-line uid) feeds
`openProcedureModal()`, which rebuilds `tabState.checklist` from that payload verbatim on every
open — so a stale entry silently un-ticked procedures that were correctly saved in the DB, on
reopening a line after a save.

Two call sites were leaving the cache stale, same root cause (missing/skipped
`invalidateProcedureModalData()` call):

1. The `save_and_verify_voucher_bundle` path (`hostAdapter.saveAndVerifyVoucher()`) never
   invalidated. The bundle persists **every** line in `currentVoucherLines`, so all those uids
   go stale, not just the open one. Fixed with a new helper
   `invalidateProcedureModalDataForVoucher()` (loops `hostAdapter.currentVoucherLines`, the same
   array `verification.js`'s `saveAndVerifyVoucher()` builds its `lines` payload from), called
   after the success check in `performVerifyVoucherChecksImpl()` (covers the bundle branch and
   the legacy `saveLineItems + verify_voucher_checks` fallback) and in `closeProcedureModal()`
   after the grouped-save success check.
2. `toggleAllProcedureChecks()` — the local-first refactor added an early `return;` that jumped
   over its own `invalidateProcedureModalData(uid)` call. Restored by adding the call immediately
   before the early return (the in-memory checklist has diverged from the cache, so the entry is
   definitively stale; a later reopen re-fetches once the background per-line save has run). The
   now-dead post-`return` copy at the old line was left as-is (other post-`return` dead code in
   this file is a separate cleanup).

No backend / DB-write / gate-logic changes. Cache-bust `procedure_modal.js?v=8→9` on
`verification.html` and `audit_workbook.html`. 33 backend tests pass (frontend-only change).

## Verification Speed Optimization — Phase 3

**Date:** 2026-08-27
**Full investigation/timing log:** `INVESTIGATION_VERIFICATION_PERF_PHASE3.md` (repo root).
**Scope so far:** Phase 3a (reconcile + map, no code) and Phase 3c (modal-open fetch fix).
Phases 3d/3e (Verify sequence) and 3f (Render test + docs) not yet done.

### Phase 3a — reconciliation + call-pattern map (no code changes)

Confirmed the ~7.9s procedure-modal open and ~21.7s Verify sequence are specific instances of
`PERFORMANCE_INVESTIGATION.md`'s Finding #1 (cross-region round-trip tax, Render Singapore ↔
Supabase Mumbai) multiplied by Finding #2 (sequential, non-batched round-trips) — no new
root-cause class. Corrected one stale note: the 2026-08-25 `Promise.all` fix covered page/session
load, not `openProcedureModal()` or the Verify sequence (both built later, 2026-08-26, still
sequential). Mapped the exact modal-open call sequence and Verify-sequence steps — see the
investigation doc. Confirmed the `audit_rules.py get_required_documents_with_authority()`
auth-role N+1 is reached only from the save/Verify path, never from `get_procedure_modal_data()`'s
fan-out — so it is not entangled with 3c and stays tracked separately (KNOWN_ISSUES 2026-08-25).

### Phase 3c — modal-open fetch fix

**Backend — per-request memo for `_resolve_sibling_voucher_line_ids()` (`routers/verification.py`):**
`get_procedure_modal_data()` is a thin sequential fan-out to 5 read sub-functions
(`get_voucher_line_documents` / `get_procedure_checks` / `get_line_observations` /
`get_voucher_line_physical_bills` / `get_cross_check_results`), each of which independently
called `_resolve_sibling_voucher_line_ids()` (2 cross-region queries) for the same id.
Added `import contextvars` and a module-level `_sibling_ids_request_memo` ContextVar
(default `None`). `_resolve_sibling_voucher_line_ids()` now checks the memo first and stores its
result (including `None` for a missing line). `get_procedure_modal_data()` sets a fresh `{}` on
the ContextVar as its first `try` statement and `reset()`s it in `finally`. Opt-in only — every
other caller (Verify path, standalone endpoints, Audit Workbook) is byte-for-byte unchanged
because the memo defaults to `None`. Chosen per-request rather than the `audit_rules.py` TTL
`cache_get/cache_set`: the `client_data_id → sibling verification_details ids` mapping changes
whenever a new verification session is created for the cashbook, which cannot happen mid-request,
so a process-lifetime/TTL cache would risk a stale sibling set.

**Frontend — parallelize `openProcedureModal()` (`static/procedure_modal.js`):**
Previously awaited 4 things in series: guidance (usually cached), template-columns `Promise.all`,
`procedure_modal_data`, `fetchLatestTbAccounts`. Steps 3–4 are independent of 1–2 and of each
other. Now the `procedure_modal_data` fetch is started (in a timed IIFE, own try/catch,
fail-soft to `null`) **before** the guidance await, and template-columns + modal-data are awaited
together via `Promise.all`. `modal_data_ms` is still measured truthfully inside the IIFE;
`template_columns_ms` now covers whichever of the two overlapping fetches finishes last.

**Frontend — `fetchLatestTbAccounts()` cache + lazy load (`static/procedure_modal.js`):**
Had no cache-hit guard despite its name, so it re-fetched `/api/trial-balance/latest-accounts`
on every modal open even though only the "Voucher Line" tab's Account-Head search uses it.
Now cached per client (`latestTbAccountsCacheClientId`) with in-flight dedup
(`latestTbAccountsInFlight`), removed from `openProcedureModal()`, and warmed lazily
fire-and-forget from `renderAccountHeadCard()` the first time that tab renders — safe because the
match-mode markup reads nothing from the cache; only the keystroke dropdown / Suggest / "Use"
handlers do, all strictly later. Result: 0 cost on the common modal open, at most one fetch per
client per page session.

**Cache-bust:** `procedure_modal.js?v=4→5` on `verification.html` and `audit_workbook.html`
(the only two pages that load it).

### Verification

- **Baseline script** (`scratchpad/bench_modal_data.py`, throwaway, read-only): calls

## Verification Save Performance — Phase 2

**Date:** 2026-08-27

### Developed

- Added a monotonically increasing dirty revision per loaded voucher line. New vouchers begin
  clean; line-specific evidence, procedure, observation, account-head, signature, and Physical
  Bill changes dirty only their line, while voucher-level check changes dirty every line.
- `saveAllVoucherLines()` now sends only dirty lines and reports saved, failed, and skipped counts
  under `?perf=1`. Writes remain sequential pending the later atomic voucher-save backend.
- A successful response clears a line only when its revision did not change while the request was
  in flight. Failed saves and newer edits remain dirty for retry.
- Verify forces the current line through the existing server-side status engine, then navigation
  recognizes that successful revision as clean instead of submitting it again. Voucher-level
  changes remain dirty on the other affected lines until safely recomputed.
- Physical Bills now have their own dirty flag, so opening/closing an unchanged manual Vendor Bill
  no longer rewrites it. Bills flush before the line status save so Cleared/Query sees current bill
  data; a failed bill write leaves the line dirty.
- Cache versions: `procedure_modal.js?v=3→4` in Verification/Audit Workbook and
  `verification.js?v=16→17` in Verification.

## Client Data Availability Loading Popup

**Date:** 2026-08-27 | **Files:** `static/databank.html`, `static/databank.js`, `CLAUDE.md`, `CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md`.

**Why:** On entering Client Data, the temporary “Fetching availability data” ribbon disappeared
before the template table became visible, leaving an apparently idle page during the remaining
wait. The page needed prominent feedback that stayed until its template list was actually ready.

**Implementation:** Added a centered, page-specific loading card backed by the shared
`LoadingUI` progress primitive. It starts in indeterminate mode while availability and database-size
requests run. Once availability arrives, it switches to determinate mode and renders template rows
one browser frame at a time, updating the exact count and percentage. It reaches 100% only after the
last row is inserted, remains briefly so completion is visible, then closes. Empty results finalize
as 100%; failures close the overlay and retain the existing error display. Data Bank JS cache-bust
advanced from `v=5` to `v=6`. No shared Loading UI or global stylesheet change was required.

**Verification:** `node --check static/databank.js` and `git diff --check` passed. A hermetic
Playwright test served the real Data Bank page with stubbed endpoints and verified: delayed success
showed the overlay at 0%, reached 100% with all three template rows present, then closed; an empty
response reached 100% with zero rows; and a forced 500 closed the overlay while preserving the
server error message. The test used no live database or credentials.

## Voucher Prev/Next Navigation (5 entries)


- 2026-07-15: Voucher Prev/Next navigation Phase A of 5 (backend) done — investigation found the Prev/Next arrow buttons don't call any backend "next/prev" endpoint at all: `goToPreviousTransaction()`/`goToNextTransaction()` (static/verification.js) step `currentTransactionIndex ± 1` through the flat line-level `sessionTransactions` array (from `/api/verification/audited_cashbook`), so a multi-line voucher gets split across clicks. `GET /api/verification/next/{session_id}` (`get_next_transaction`, routers/verification.py) was already voucher-grouped from an earlier phase and is left unchanged (still "jump to next Pending voucher", used only for initial load and post-complete refresh) — its internal fetch+grouping loop was extracted into a new shared helper `_fetch_session_details_grouped()` with no external behavior change (verified byte-identical response before/after). Added a new `GET /api/verification/voucher_nav/{session_id}` endpoint (`current_detail_id`, `direction=next|prev` query params) that walks the session's full distinct-voucher list (ordered by each voucher's earliest `client_data_id`, all statuses — not just Pending, so Prev can revisit already-verified vouchers) and returns the adjacent voucher's full line set, plus `voucher_index`/`total_vouchers`; boundary requests (before the first / after the last voucher) return `{"boundary": true, ...}` with HTTP 200 rather than an error, mirroring `/next`'s existing `{"completed": true}` pattern. Confirmed the existing "voucher X/7" position indicator is computed entirely client-side (`computeVoucherStats()`) from a separate data source and needed no backend change to keep working. Verified against live session 296 (7 vouchers, incl. 5-line `CPV-0726-126` and 2-line `CPV-0726-101`): `/next` unchanged; `voucher_nav` correctly steps to the *whole adjacent voucher* regardless of which line of the current voucher was passed as `current_detail_id`, returns correct `voucher_index`/`total_vouchers`, returns `{"boundary": true}` at both ends, and 404s on an unknown `current_detail_id`. No frontend wiring yet (Phase B) — `voucher_nav` has no caller until then, so the live UI's Prev/Next arrows are unaffected by this phase.

- 2026-07-15: Voucher Prev/Next navigation Phase B of 5 (frontend, main card multi-line rendering) done — the brief assumed a `renderTransaction()`/"one line at a time" main card still existed; investigation found that's stale (deleted in earlier phases) and `renderVoucherLines()` already renders every line of whatever voucher it's given as its own row. The actual remaining gap: `goToPreviousTransaction()`/`goToNextTransaction()` (static/verification.js) stepped the flat line-level `sessionTransactions` array one row at a time, so a 5-line voucher needed 5 "Next" clicks (each re-rendering the same already-fully-shown lines) before the view moved on. Fixed by wiring both to Phase A's `GET /api/verification/voucher_nav` via a new `moveToAdjacentVoucher(direction)` (fetches the adjacent voucher, applies it via the same state-assignment + `renderVoucherHeader()`/`seedVoucherLineState()`/`renderVoucherLines()`/`updateProgressDisplay()` pipeline `loadNextTransaction()` already uses for `/next`; silently no-ops on `{boundary: true}` or a fetch error, matching this file's existing silent-boundary convention). `goToNextTransaction()`'s existing validate-and-complete-current-line step is untouched — only its "validation didn't pass, still move forward" fallback now calls `moveToAdjacentVoucher('next')` instead of raw index-stepping. Two supporting helpers added: `getVoucherPosition()` (1-based index/total of `currentVoucherId` among `sessionTransactions`' distinct voucher_ids — used for the arrows' `disabled` state in `renderVoucherHeader()` and for cheap up-front boundary guards, replacing the old `currentTransactionIndex`-based checks) and `isCurrentVoucherValidated()` (replaces `isCurrentTransactionValidated()` — the "confirm before leaving if not validated" gate now checks that *every* line of the current voucher is Passed/Verified, not just one arbitrary line, since navigation is no longer line-granular). `renderVoucherLines()`, `seedVoucherLineState()`, `updateProgressDisplay()`'s own position computation, `navigateToTransaction()` (popover/Phase D-E territory), `completeTransaction()`, `validateTransaction()`, and all HTML/CSS were left untouched. No Playwright/browser tool was available this session, so verification was done by directly exercising the new `voucher_nav` endpoint against live session 296 end-to-end (walked all 7 vouchers forward via repeated `direction=next` calls starting from `/next`'s anchor, then all the way back via `direction=prev`, confirming each step lands on the correct whole voucher with correct `voucher_index`/`total_vouchers` and boundaries at both ends) plus a static trace confirming `sessionTransactions`' client-side voucher order (from `/audited_cashbook`) exactly matches `voucher_nav`'s backend order for this session, so `getVoucherPosition()`'s index/total will agree with the backend's — full DOM/click verification of the arrows themselves is still outstanding. **Known, deliberately unaddressed gap**: "Next" still validates/completes only the single line that happens to be `currentDetailId` before advancing — a multi-line voucher's other lines aren't auto-validated by clicking Next. Out of this phase's scope (rendering + navigation granularity only); flagged, not fixed. Phase C (click-to-lock/dim focus) not started.
