## Row-Exclusion Requirement (7 entries)


- **Known pre-existing bug, not yet fixed (found 2026-07-16 while verifying the row-exclusion phase)**: `compare_transactions()`'s existing-rows query (`routers/import_export.py`) does a `LEFT JOIN verification_details` that can return multiple rows per `client_data_id` when more than one `verification_details` row references the same `client_data_id` — this inflates `existing_docs`/the "missing" list with duplicate `client_data_id`s (harmless duplication on its own, since re-`UPDATE`ing the same id is idempotent) but also means `total_existing_before_import`/`missing_count` in API responses can overcount real rows. Caught the hard way: testing `/api/upload/import` against the *real* ACME client (client_id=1) with a small unrelated test file caused every real document not present in that test file to be correctly-by-design-but-dangerously flagged `change_detection_status='deleted'` (~1200 rows momentarily mis-flagged; reverted using `data_audit_log` history to confirm each row's true prior status, no data loss). **Lesson for future testing**: never call `/api/upload/import` (or anything that reaches `compare_transactions()`) against a client that has real/live data unless the incoming file is a genuine full re-upload of that client's data — use a disposable test client (create via `POST /api/clients`, delete afterward) for any import-path testing instead.

- 2026-07-16: Row-exclusion Phase 1 of 4 (backend, routers/import_export.py only) done — `ImportRequest` gained `excluded_rows: Optional[List[int]] = None` (row numbers match `validation_errors[].row_number`: header=1, first data row=2; `None`/absent = exclude nothing, identical to today's behavior); new `filter_excluded_rows(rows, excluded_rows)` is called immediately after `rows = df.to_dict('records')` in both `validate_only()` and `validate_and_import()`, before any validation, counting, or `compare_transactions()`/`get_document_group_id()` grouping — so excluded rows are invisible to validation, import, and change-detection grouping, per the brief. `check-duplicates` intentionally left untouched (brief scoped to validate/import only). No UI changes this phase. Verified end-to-end against the live app: a baseline `/api/upload/validate` call (43-row real file, no `excluded_rows`) was unchanged; excluding a row that would otherwise fail validation (blank required fields + bad date) removed it from `validation_errors` and dropped `total_rows`/`valid_rows` accordingly; a full `/api/upload/import` run (using a disposable throwaway test client created and deleted for this purpose, see the "known bug" note below) confirmed the excluded row produced no `client_data` row and was absent from `document_group_id` grouping. **Incident during this session's verification, since corrected — see the "known pre-existing bug" Convention note above**: an initial `/api/upload/import` test call against the *real* ACME client (client_id=1) with a small unrelated test file triggered a pre-existing, unrelated bug in `compare_transactions()` that flagged ~12 real rows `change_detection_status='deleted'` (the raw response claimed ~3989 due to a duplicate-join artifact in that same pre-existing query, not 3989 real rows). Fully reverted using `data_audit_log` history to confirm and restore each affected row's true prior status (`active`), with before/after status-distribution counts cross-checked to reconcile exactly (verified no net data loss); all test artifacts (client, rows, uploaded_files entries, physical files) removed afterward. Root cause is a separate, unfixed bug (documented as a Convention note above) — out of scope for this phase.

## Audit Rules Module (27 entries)


- **Modal Caching Phase 3, sub-phase 3 of 3, FINAL (verify, no code changes — this completes the 3-sub-phase Modal Caching Phase 3 track)**: confirmed the cache built in sub-phase 1 and wired in sub-phase 2 behaves correctly end-to-end via real HTTP requests against the actually-running dev server, not another repeat of the in-process function-call smoke test. **A real blocker surfaced first**: the dev server already listening on port 5000 pre-dated both sub-phases' code (`main.py` has no `--reload` flag; the process's start time was `12:58 PM`, `routers/audit_rules.py`'s last edit was `2:34 PM`) — every initial curl against it silently exercised the old, pre-caching code, producing a flat ~3s latency with zero difference between a guaranteed miss and a guaranteed hit. Per this file's own standing convention (never kill a port-5000 process without checking whose it is first), stopped and asked before touching it — confirmed with the user to restart it, then re-ran every check against the fresh process (PID confirmed new, `Application startup complete` logged). **Four checks, all passed live**: (1) cache-hit latency — a guaranteed miss (immediately after an invalidating write) costs ~3-4.6s per `GET /api/audit-rules/documents/{id}`, a guaranteed hit costs ~0.2s via `curl` (a Python `urllib`-based repeat of the same check initially showed a flatter ~2s "hit" cost — traced to per-call client-side connection overhead in that script, not a server-side effect, and confirmed as a red herring once `curl`'s numbers came back sharply different and consistent across 3 repeated rounds); (2) a paginated list (`GET /api/audit-rules/documents?limit=5&offset=0`) sets `X-Total-Count` identically on both a fresh call and a repeat cache-hit call (`18` both times); (3) no stale reads — `PUT`ing a new `kb_note` onto a live Document and immediately re-`GET`ting it returns the new value right away, not a cached stale one; (4) cross-file invalidation — created a disposable test Category, hit `GET /api/verification/audit_guidance?transaction_type=<name>` twice (confirming a real cache hit via identical `kb_overview` on both calls), then `PUT` a `kb_overview` change to that Category through `routers/audit_rules.py`'s own endpoint, and the very next `audit_guidance` call reflected the new text immediately — proving `verification.py`'s guidance cache correctly shares and is correctly busted by `audit_rules.py`'s own invalidation hooks, exactly as designed in sub-phase 2. All disposable test data (the temporarily-modified Document's `kb_note`, the test Category) was reverted/soft-deleted afterward. No bug found — nothing to report as a blocker beyond the stale-server false start above, which was an environment/process issue, not a defect in the cache logic itself. This completes the confirmed 3-sub-phase Modal Caching Phase 3 requirement: mechanism + write invalidation (sub-phase 1) → read-side wiring (sub-phase 2) → live end-to-end verification (this entry).

- **Modal Caching Phase 3, sub-phase 2 of 3 (read-side wiring, `routers/audit_rules.py` + `routers/verification.py`)**: wires the cache mechanism built in sub-phase 1 into every GET path it covers. **Two design decisions confirmed with the user before implementation, both departures from the original brief's literal wording**: (1) cache keys are **global, not per-client** — sub-phase 1 already confirmed `audit_rule_documents`/`audit_rule_cross_checks`/`audit_rule_categories` have no `client_id` column, so partitioning by client would just build N redundant copies of identical data; every key wired this phase omits client_id. (2) `GET /api/verification/category-for-account` was deliberately **left uncached** — it's genuinely client-scoped (client_id + account_code → category), but its data comes from `routers/trial_balance.py` (TB uploads, Assign Categories), a file with zero invalidation hooks into this cache; caching it now would risk serving a stale category mapping for up to the 10-min TTL after a TB re-upload with no way to invalidate sooner, so it stays uncached until (if ever) `trial_balance.py` gets its own hooks. Wired in `routers/audit_rules.py`: `get_documents`/`get_document`, `get_cross_checks`/`get_cross_check`, `get_categories`/`get_category`, and `get_category_cleared_requirements` — each checks `cache_get(key)` first, computes and `cache_set()`s on a miss. `fetch_paginated_rows()` (the shared helper behind the three list endpoints) was restructured to return `(rows, total)` instead of writing `response.headers["X-Total-Count"]` itself, since a cache **hit** now needs to set that same header from a cached total without re-querying `COUNT(*)` — each list endpoint stores `(result, total)` as its cached value and sets the header identically on both the hit and miss paths. Wired in `routers/verification.py`: `get_audit_guidance` (the only qualifying call site — `category-for-account` is the other endpoint in this file and was excluded per decision #2 above), keyed on `transaction_type` (the Category name) since guidance content doesn't vary by client; imports `cache_get`/`cache_set` from `routers.audit_rules` alongside the file's existing cross-router imports from that same module (`get_category_guidance_documents` etc.), no new import pattern introduced. No changes to `invalidate_audit_rules_cache()` or any write endpoint — sub-phase 1's 14 hooks already cover every write that can affect what's cached here. Verified: `py_compile` clean on both files; `pytest` shows the same 2 pre-existing failures as sub-phase 1's baseline (confirmed unrelated, both in Postgres-backed routers outside this change), no new failures. Direct smoke test against the live Postgres/Supabase database (disposable `SmokeTestDoc`/`SmokeTestCategory` rows, soft-deleted at the end — same create-then-soft-delete verification convention used throughout this module's build history) confirmed: a single-item GET makes real DB calls on a miss and zero on a hit with an identical result; an `update_document` call immediately invalidates that cached read (next GET reflects the new name, not stale data); a paginated list GET is a cache hit on the second call and still sets `X-Total-Count` identically to the miss path; `verification.py`'s `get_audit_guidance` hits the same shared cache (miss then hit, zero DB calls on the hit) and is correctly invalidated by an `update_category` write made through `audit_rules.py`, proving the cross-file reuse works end-to-end. No new files, no schema changes.

- **Modal Caching Phase 3, sub-phase 1 of 3 (TTL cache mechanism + write-side invalidation, `routers/audit_rules.py` only)**: adds an in-memory, process-level TTL cache in front of Categories/Documents/Cross-checks reads — server-side, separate from and complementary to the existing client-side session cache (matrix_version-based, from the original caching feature's Phase 2). Render is single-instance, so no Redis. New module-level `_audit_rules_cache: Dict[str, tuple]` (key → `(expires_at, value)`) guarded by a `threading.Lock()` (endpoints are sync `def`s, run in FastAPI's threadpool, so concurrent access is possible), with `cache_get(key)`/`cache_set(key, value, ttl=AUDIT_RULES_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS)`/`invalidate_audit_rules_cache()` — `AUDIT_RULES_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS = 600` (10 min) is a safety net only; TTL is not the primary invalidation mechanism. **Read-only finding that shaped the design**: none of `audit_rule_documents`/`audit_rule_cross_checks`/`audit_rule_categories` have a `client_id` column — they're firm-wide entities, not per-client (confirmed against the schema) — so a write from any one client's session invalidates the same data for every client equally, meaning `invalidate_audit_rules_cache()` always clears the whole cache rather than attempting a per-client scoped clear, regardless of whatever key scheme the read-side wiring (sub-phase 2) ends up using. Also checked the brief's question about `bump_category_matrix_version()`: confirmed it fires on only two triggers (Category document-membership change in `update_category`, and the `is_required` toggle in `update_category_document_required`) — it does **not** fire on Document field edits (`update_document`), Document soft-delete/restore, the `transaction_level_approval` toggle, or any Cross-check write, all of which can change a cached Categories/Documents/guidance read. Since `matrix_version` is a narrower, different concept (staleness of an already-persisted per-voucher classification, not API-response freshness), cache invalidation was wired as its own explicit `invalidate_audit_rules_cache()` call in each affected write endpoint rather than folded into `bump_category_matrix_version()` itself — 14 call sites total: Documents' `create_document`/`update_document`/`delete_document`/`restore_document`/`update_document_transaction_level_approval`; Cross-checks' `create_cross_check`/`update_cross_check`/`delete_cross_check`/`restore_cross_check`; Categories' `create_category`/`update_category`/`delete_category`/`restore_category`/`update_category_document_required`. Voucher-level Checks and Signature Specimens endpoints deliberately untouched — out of this brief's stated cache scope (Categories/Documents/guidance only). - **Audit Rules module (new, confirmed 9-phase requirement — distinct from the earlier 2-phase dashboard-card/row-icon placeholders)**: schema lives in `database.py`'s `init_db()` under the `audit_rule_` table prefix (kept distinct from the pre-existing, unrelated `audit_log`/`audit_procedure_library` tables). Three reusable entities assembled *by reference*, not duplicated: `audit_rule_documents` (name, one `kb_note`, `is_active` — added Phase 2 for soft-delete/restore, plus child tables `audit_rule_document_fields` — the fields on that document available for cross-checks, e.g. Quantity/Amount/Date — and `audit_rule_document_auth_roles` — a list of authorisation roles, e.g. "Approved by", modelled as a list from day one); `audit_rule_cross_checks` (name, `compare_field` free text, `comparison_type` CHECK-constrained to `'All equal'`/`'Sequential increasing'`/`'Sequential decreasing'`/`'Within tolerance %'`, `is_active` — added Phase 3, plus ordered junction `audit_rule_cross_check_documents`); `audit_rule_categories` (name, one `kb_overview`, `is_active` — added Phase 4, plus junctions `audit_rule_category_documents`/`audit_rule_category_cross_checks`). A Category is the entity a voucher will eventually reference (Phase 9 — no voucher/client_data schema change yet). This module is intended to **replace**, not run parallel to, the hardcoded `audit_procedure_library` lookup currently used by the verification module (confirmed migration target, Phase 9). Phase 1 was schema only; Phases 2-4 (all in `routers/audit_rules.py`) added full CRUD for all three entity types in order (Documents → Cross-checks → Categories) — do not wire anything into verification.py against these tables until Phase 9 confirms the migration. **Recurring pattern, now closed out across all three entity tables**: Phase 1's original `CREATE TABLE` for each entity never anticipated CRUD semantics, so each of Phases 2/3/4 had to add `is_active` both to the `CREATE TABLE` statement *and* a matching `ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN` upgrade block (the table already exists on any database that ran Phase 1's `init_db()`, so the `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` addition alone is a no-op there) — this happened identically for `audit_rule_documents`, `audit_rule_cross_checks`, and `audit_rule_categories`; any *new* `audit_rule_*` table added in a future phase should be checked against this same gap before assuming `is_active` exists. All three CRUD surfaces (Documents/Cross-checks/Categories — `GET/POST/PUT /api/audit-rules/{documents,cross-checks,categories}`, `DELETE`+`POST .../restore`) follow `routers/clients.py`'s soft-delete/restore convention exactly (`is_active` flag, not a hard delete) and `routers/templates.py`'s delete-then-reinsert pattern for replacing an ordered child/junction list on create/update (`save_document_auth_roles()`/`save_document_cross_check_fields()`/`save_cross_check_documents()`/`save_category_documents()`/`save_category_cross_checks()`) — plain `execute_write()` calls in a loop, no new transactional pattern introduced anywhere in this module. Reuse-count fields are now fully live end-to-end: Documents' and Cross-checks' `used_by_categories_count` (`COUNT(*)` against `audit_rule_category_documents`/`audit_rule_category_cross_checks`) needed zero code changes in Phase 4 and now correctly return non-zero as soon as a Category references them (confirmed live: creating then editing a test Category moved a referenced Document's/Cross-check's count `0 → 1 → 0`) — this is what "the counts were already querying the junction tables" in the Phase 4 brief meant, and it held up exactly as predicted. Categories' own `used_by_vouchers_count` is different: `get_category_used_by_vouchers_count()` is a **hardcoded 0 placeholder**, not a live query — no voucher/client_data column references a Category yet, so there's nothing to count against until Phase 9 adds that link; the field exists now purely so the frontend (Phase 7) doesn't need a later API contract change, and this function is the one place to swap in a real query once Phase 9 lands. SQLite foreign keys are **not enforced** on this app's connections (`get_db()` never sets `PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON`), so every `audit_rule_*` junction-table write in this module validates referenced-row existence explicitly at the API layer rather than trusting the schema's `FOREIGN KEY` clauses — `validate_cross_check_payload()` (Phase 3, checks `document_ids`) and `validate_category_payload()` (Phase 4, checks both `document_ids` and `cross_check_ids`) both do this. Cross-checks additionally validate `comparison_type` against the fixed set client-side (mirroring the DB's own CHECK constraint, so a bad value returns a clean 400 not a raw 500) and that `compare_field` is cross-check-eligible on every selected Document (reuses `get_document_cross_check_fields()` directly). Categories additionally enforce the brief's locked containment rule: every Cross-check attached to a Category may only reference Documents that are *also* in that Category's own `document_ids` list — `validate_category_payload()` rejects (400, naming both the Cross-check and the missing Document id(s)) any Category payload that violates this, checked by reading each selected Cross-check's own `audit_rule_cross_check_documents` rows and confirming they're a subset of the Category's document-id set. None of `audit_rule_documents.name`, `audit_rule_cross_checks.name`, or `audit_rule_categories.name` has a uniqueness constraint/check — not introduced in any of the three phases since the brief never asked for one; don't assume names are unique when building later phases (frontend, Phase 9 voucher wiring) against these tables.

- 2026-07-23: **Trial Balance — Periodic dates & overwrite warning, Section 2, Phase 5 of 6 (backend: accept period + detect overwrite — `routers/trial_balance.py` only)** done. **Confirmed with the user first**: since `trial_balance_uploads` has no `UNIQUE(client_id, as_of_date)` (every upload is deliberately its own row), "overwrite" needed a clarified meaning before writing any conflict logic — user chose **true delete-then-insert**, not just a soft "latest wins" convention: confirming the overwrite genuinely deletes the prior exact-period upload and its accounts before the new one is created. New shared `find_conflicting_uploads(client_id, period_start, period_end)` is the single source of truth for "does an exact-period upload already exist" — exact match only on `period_start`+`period_end` for the same client (never an overlap check: a monthly TB inside an already-uploaded quarterly one is never flagged, confirmed live), matches regardless of the existing row's `status` (parsed/error/pending — the schema draws no distinction, so a simple "does one exist" rule was used rather than special-casing failed attempts), returns the raw row list (most recent first) since more than one conflicting row can exist. Two new shared helpers sit next to it: `_validate_period_dates()` (ISO format + `period_end >= period_start`, same `strptime` pattern `as_of_date` already uses) and `_serialize_conflicting_upload()` (one response shape reused by both the check endpoint's `existing_upload` and the upload endpoint's 409 `detail`, so the frontend, Phase 6, can render both with one function). New read-only `GET /api/trial-balance/check-period-conflict?client_id=&period_start=&period_end=` is the two-step flow's "step 1" — touches no data, returns `{"conflict": false, "existing_upload": null}` or `{"conflict": true, "existing_upload": {...}, "conflicting_upload_count": N}`. `POST /api/trial-balance/upload` gained 4 new optional Form fields (`period_start`/`period_end`/`period_type`/`confirm_overwrite`, all backward-compatible — omitting `period_start`/`period_end` entirely skips all new logic and reproduces the endpoint's exact pre-Phase-5 behavior, confirmed live below) and a new validation/gate block inserted before the pending-upload-row INSERT: rejects if only one of `period_start`/`period_end` is given (400), validates both if given, then on a conflict either 409s with the same shape `check-period-conflict` returns (when `confirm_overwrite` is false — this is what protects against Phase 6's UI being skipped or a stray API call, per the brief) or deletes every conflicting upload's accounts then its own row (`DELETE FROM trial_balance_accounts WHERE upload_id = ?` before `DELETE FROM trial_balance_uploads WHERE id = ?`, for **all** matches, not just the latest) and logs the deletion via `log_audit()` before proceeding. The explicit two-step child-then-parent delete is deliberate, not relying on `ON DELETE CASCADE` — this app's connections don't enable `PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON` (already documented in this same Conventions section for Audit Rules/Trial Balance Phase 1), so a bare parent-row delete would silently leave orphaned account rows. The pending-row INSERT and final row now carry `period_start`/`period_end`/`period_type` (`None` when omitted, matching the columns' nullable Phase-4 schema). No schema/migration changes this phase (Phase 4 already added the 3 columns); `classify_accounts()`, mapping/suggestion logic, `list_trial_balance_accounts()`, `get_trial_balance_summary()`, `override_account_classification()`, and `download_trial_balance_template()` are all untouched. Verified end-to-end against the user's already-running `--reload` dev server (port 5000, `netstat`-checked first, not restarted) using a disposable test client (soft-deleted afterward) and a small 2-row test TB file: uploaded with `period_start=2026-06-01`/`period_end=2026-06-30`/`period_type=monthly` and no conflict — succeeded, `period_start`/`period_end`/`period_type` confirmed persisted via direct DB query; `GET /check-period-conflict` for that exact period correctly returned `conflict:true` with the right `existing_upload` details; re-uploading the same exact period without `confirm_overwrite` correctly 409'd with the expected message/shape and created **no** new row (confirmed via direct query — still only the original upload); re-uploading with `confirm_overwrite=true` correctly deleted the prior upload and its 2 accounts (confirmed via direct query: 0 accounts left under the old `upload_id`) and created a new upload as the sole survivor for that period; uploading an overlapping-but-different period (a quarterly range containing the just-uploaded monthly one) correctly did **not** conflict and both coexist; omitting period fields entirely still succeeds exactly as before this phase (`period_start`/`period_end`/`period_type` all `NULL` on that row) — confirming full backward compatibility; a request with only `period_start` given and a request with `period_end` before `period_start` both correctly 400'd with clear messages. `python -m py_compile routers/trial_balance.py` passes. Test client, its trial-balance uploads/accounts, and the local test Excel file were all removed/soft-deleted afterward. Phase 6 (frontend — period inputs + overwrite confirmation UI) not started.

## Save Column Mapping (3 entries)


- **Save Column Mapping feature (new, confirmed 3-phase requirement)**: `saved_column_mappings` (database.py, added right after the `client_voucher_prefixes` seeding block) stores one row per mapped template column (`client_id`, `template_id`, `template_column_id`, `excel_column`), `UNIQUE(client_id, template_id, template_column_id)`, upserted via delete-then-reinsert on save — mirrors `template_column_mappings`' own one-row-per-column storage and the delete-then-reinsert pattern already used by `update_template()`/`save_document_auth_roles()`. Keyed by client+template (not template alone) since different clients export the same template with differently worded Excel headers. `POST /api/upload/save-mapping` (routers/import_export.py) validates client/template are active (404 otherwise), skips any mapping entry with a blank `excel_column` (nothing meaningful to save for an unmatched column), and fully replaces whatever was previously saved for that client+template. `GET /api/upload/saved-mapping?client_id=&template_id=` deliberately returns `{"has_saved_mapping": false, "mappings": []}` rather than 404 when nothing is saved — keeps the auto-apply-on-load logic (Phase A2) a simple flag check with no special-case error handling. This completes all 3 phases of the Save Column Mapping requirement. **Phase A2 (frontend save action + auto-apply on load, `static/upload.html` + `static/upload.js` only)**: a "💾 Save Mapping" button sits inside `#mappingPanel`'s `.section-title` row (next to `#mappingCount`, not the `#modeActions` action-bar below it — this is a mapping-table-scoped action, not an import action), styled via new `.btn-save-mapping` (upload.html's own `<style>` block, same small icon-button language as `.btn-download-icon`). Its click handler filters `currentMappings` to matched entries only (`SavedMappingEntry.excel_column` is a required `str` server-side, so an unmatched/`null` entry must be dropped client-side before sending, not left to the endpoint's own blank-skip) and POSTs `{client_id, template_id, mappings: [{template_column_id, excel_column}]}` — always a full overwrite, matching the backend's own upsert. New shared `getCurrentClientId()` (upload.js, next to `formatDate()`) factors out the `isClientSelected()`/`getSelectedClientId()`/`localStorage` fallback already used inline in the `importBtn` handler (left untouched, not part of this phase) so this and the auto-apply function below don't duplicate it. New `applySavedMapping()` is called from `autoMapColumns()`'s success path, right after `clearRestorePreview()` and before `renderMapping()` — the single injection point every path that reaches the mapping table (template select, sheet change, file (re)load) already funnels through. It `GET`s the saved mapping for the current client+template and, for each saved `{template_column_id, excel_column}`, overrides the matching `currentMappings` entry's `excel_column`/`is_matched` **only if that exact excel_column string is still present in the current sheet's `excelHeaders`** — the "never force a mismatch" rule is implemented as an exact-header-presence check (the backend stores the literal header text, so this is the closest safe interpretation of "matches closely"); anything not present keeps whatever `autoMapColumns()`'s own backend call already guessed, untouched. A fetch failure or `has_saved_mapping: false` both resolve to "apply nothing" (console.warn only on a genuine fetch error, matching `refreshDateFormatPreview()`'s existing non-fatal-error convention) — never blocks or delays the normal auto-map flow. The success status message gets an appended note when anything was auto-applied (`✅ Auto‑mapped X/Y columns (N from your saved mapping)`). The mapping table's own dropdowns/edit behavior needed zero changes — a saved-mapping override is just a different starting value for `currentMappings`, still fully editable afterward, same as any auto-mapped value. Verified directly against the live `--reload` dev server (port 5000, `netstat`-checked first, not restarted) by calling `POST`/`GET /api/upload/save-mapping`/`saved-mapping` exactly as the new JS does (client 1, template 4 "Gate Pass"): confirmed `has_saved_mapping` goes `false → true` after saving 2 columns and the GET response shape exactly matches what `applySavedMapping()` expects; cleared the test row afterward via an empty-mappings save (`saved_count: 0`, confirmed `has_saved_mapping: false` again). `node --check static/upload.js` passes. No Playwright/browser tool was available this session (same recurring gap as most phases in this log), so the actual button click, live table pre-fill on reload, and the "fall back on a differently-worded header" case were not visually confirmed — worth a manual pass before Phase A3. **Phase A3, FINAL (clear a saved mapping, `routers/import_export.py` + `static/upload.html` + `static/upload.js` only)**: "edit" needed no new UI — Phase A2's Save Mapping button already overwrites on click (delete-then-reinsert), so the one real gap was an explicit way to remove a saved mapping entirely. New `DELETE /api/upload/saved-mapping?client_id=&template_id=` (routers/import_export.py, directly after `get_saved_column_mapping()`) deletes the matching `saved_column_mappings` rows and returns `{"message", "deleted_count"}` — deliberately as lenient as the existing `GET` (no client/template existence checks; "nothing was saved" is a normal outcome, not a 404). Since `execute_write()` returns `cursor.lastrowid` (meaningless for a `DELETE`), `deleted_count` is read via a `SELECT COUNT(*)` immediately before the delete, same "count in Python, not off the write call" pattern `save_column_mapping()`'s own `saved_count` already uses. Frontend: a "🗑️ Clear Saved Mapping" button sits right next to `#saveMappingBtn` in the same `.section-title` row, styled via new `.btn-clear-mapping` (upload.html, same small icon-button sizing as `.btn-save-mapping` but with a red hover treatment matching this app's existing destructive-action color, `.file-detail .clear`'s `#dc2626`) — signals it removes the *persisted* mapping, not the on-screen table. Its click handler (upload.js, right after the Save Mapping handler) reuses `getCurrentClientId()` unchanged, gates on `selectedTemplateId`, shows a plain native `window.confirm()` before calling the new endpoint (chosen over a custom modal since this is a single flat destructive action with no follow-on state, unlike verification.js's multi-step navigation-confirm modals), and reports `deleted_count` back via `showStatus()` — a "cleared" success message when `> 0`, a neutral "nothing was saved" info message when `0` (both are valid outcomes, not errors). Deliberately does not touch the currently-displayed mapping table/`currentMappings` — only the saved copy is removed, so a later reload/re-select for this client+template simply stops auto-applying anything, falling back to ordinary `autoMapColumns()` exactly as if nothing had ever been saved. Verified directly against the live `--reload` dev server (port 5000, same already-running process, `netstat`-confirmed unchanged PID after the edit — reload picked up the change with no restart): saved a 2-column test mapping (client 1, template 4), `DELETE`d it (`deleted_count: 2`), confirmed a follow-up `GET` returned `has_saved_mapping: false`, then called `DELETE` again on the now-empty pair and confirmed it's idempotent (`deleted_count: 0`, no error). `python -m py_compile routers/import_export.py` and `node --check static/upload.js` both pass. No Playwright/browser tool was available this session, so the actual button click and native confirm-dialog flow were not visually confirmed — worth a manual pass. **This completes the entire 3-phase Save Column Mapping requirement** (Phase A1: backend storage + save/load API; Phase A2: frontend save action + auto-apply; Phase A3: this clear action).

Table stays fully editable either way. No backend changes — reused Phase A1's endpoints as-is. Phase A3 (edit/delete a saved mapping) remains. See full entry in the Conventions section above.

New "🗑️ Clear Saved Mapping" button next to Save Mapping calls a new `DELETE /api/upload/saved-mapping?client_id=&template_id=` endpoint (behind a native `confirm()`) that removes the persisted mapping for the current client+template, reporting `deleted_count` back via the status bar. Surfaces only the 4 fields the brief lists (`TB_MAPPING_FIELDS`: Account Code/Name/Debit/Credit) — Phase 1's backend also supports optional Type/Opening Balance/Closing Balance roles, but this UI never shows or sends them (omitting an `Optional[str] = Form(None)` field is a no-op server-side, not an error). **Header list authority**: both the mapping dropdowns' options and the preview table's column labels are sourced from `suggest-mapping`'s own `headers` array (not a separate client-side header parse) — guarantees the dropdown options are always exactly what the upload endpoint will validate against; the preview's row *values* come from the client-side SheetJS parse (`sheet_to_json(sheet, {header:1})`, rows sliced to the first 5 data rows) and are matched to the backend header list purely by column **index**, not by re-matching header text, since both read the same file's first sheet top-to-bottom in the same order. `renderMappingDropdowns()` mirrors `static/upload.js`'s `renderMapping()` interaction pattern exactly (per the brief's explicit instruction to match it): each field's `<select>` excludes whatever header another field has already claimed, and any `change` triggers a full table re-render so every row's exclusion list and ✅/❌ status stay in sync — `upload.js` itself was only read for reference, not edited. `checkMappingComplete()` is a frontend mirror of Phase 1's backend `validate_column_mapping()` — checks all 4 required fields (not only Account Code), reusing the existing `.status-bar`/`.status-bar.error` CSS classes for its inline message (`#mappingValidationMessage`) rather than inventing new styling, and names every still-missing field by label (e.g. "Please map the following required field(s) before uploading: Account Code, Credit."); - **Trial Balance module Phase 3 of 5 (store + retrieve classified accounts, `routers/trial_balance.py` only — no schema/`main.py` changes needed, both already in place from Phases 1-2)**: two read-only `GET` endpoints added right after the existing upload endpoint. `GET /api/trial-balance/accounts?upload_id=&is_leaf=` lists one upload's accounts in original file order (`ORDER BY sort_order`), with an optional `is_leaf` filter (`true`→`classification='leaf'`, `false`→`'parent'`, omitted→both) — confirmed with the user to include, beyond the brief's explicitly-listed fields (code/name/parent_code/level/is_leaf/balances), the row's own `id` (Phase 5 needs a row identifier to target a specific account for a future override) and `manually_overridden` (always `false` today, but part of the same future-proofed shape) and `source_account_type` (the source file's raw cross-check "Type" value, so a reviewer can visually compare it against `is_leaf`) — all three purely additive, nothing from the brief's list was dropped. `classification`'s raw `'leaf'`/`'parent'` TEXT is translated into a boolean `is_leaf` in the response, matching the brief's exact field name rather than exposing the DB's internal string. `GET /api/trial-balance/summary?upload_id=` returns strictly `{total_count, leaf_count, parent_count}` — deliberately no upload metadata (file name/date/status) and no ambiguity-detection logic, per the brief's explicit "counts only" scope (the classification engine doesn't flag any row as ambiguous; that would need to be raised as a separate scope addition, not assumed here). Both endpoints share a new `_require_upload(upload_id)` helper (404 "Trial balance upload not found" if the upload row itself doesn't exist) — an upload that exists but has zero accounts (e.g. it errored during Phase 2's parsing) is **not** an error case for these two endpoints, it's a legitimate state that just returns an empty `accounts` list / all-zero counts. - **Trial Balance module Phase 2 of 5 (parsing & classification engine, new `routers/trial_balance.py` + `main.py` two-line mount + `requirements.txt`)**: one endpoint, `POST /api/trial-balance/upload` (multipart: `file`, `client_id` Form, `as_of_date` Form) — upload + classify + store in one pass, per the confirmed scope (no retrieval endpoint (Phase 3) or review UI (Phase 5) yet). **Column identification**: since TB has no column-mapping UI (deliberately, unlike `import_export.py`/`templates.py`), columns are identified by new `identify_columns()`/`clean_header()` — headers are normalized (lowercased, all non-alphanumeric characters stripped) and matched *exactly* (not substring) against a per-role synonym set, processed Code→Name→Type→Debit→Credit in priority order so one header can never satisfy two roles. Only Code is required (`CODE_SYNONYMS = {"code","accountcode","ledgercode","accode","glcode","accountno","acno"}`) — `identify_columns()` raises `ValueError` if no Code-like header is found, which the endpoint turns into a 400 + an `'error'`-status upload row (not a raw crash). Name/Type/Debit/Credit synonym sets are in the same file, right below. **The core anti-corruption mechanism**: `pd.read_excel(..., dtype=str, keep_default_na=False, engine=...)` forces the *entire* sheet to raw strings at the pandas layer itself, not just the code column — confirmed via a direct side-by-side test that without `dtype=str`, a column containing `"001"` silently becomes the integer `1` (leading zero lost) under pandas' default type inference, while `dtype=str` preserves it exactly; this is the mechanism that prevents the Leather Crop-style code corruption. `engine` is picked by extension (`xlrd` for `.xls`, `openpyxl` for `.xlsx` — the `.xls` branch needed adding the `xlrd` package to `requirements.txt` and installing it, since pandas' `openpyxl` engine can't read legacy `.xls` at all; confirmed with the user before touching `requirements.txt`, outside the originally-confirmed file list). Blank Account Code rows are skipped silently (not stored, not an error, confirmed with the user — e.g. a spacer/section-title row); a duplicate Account Code within the same file is also skipped (keeping the first occurrence) and counted, both counts surfacing in the upload row's `notes` and the response, never blocking the rest of the file. **Classification** (`classify_accounts()`): implements the exact locked rule ("leaf unless some other code starts with `this code + '-'`") by walking every code's own dash-delimited proper prefixes and marking any prefix that is itself a real code in the file as `'parent'` — provably equivalent to an O(n²) any-other-code scan (a full explanation is in the function's own docstring) but runs in O(n · depth) instead. Debit/Credit are best-effort parsed via new `parse_amount()` (strips thousands-commas, honors the accounting parenthesis-negative convention e.g. `"(1,234.56)"` → `-1234.56`; never raises — an unparsable value just becomes `None`, since amounts are secondary to classification this phase); if neither a Debit nor Credit column is found, both fields are simply left null (no single signed "Balance" column fallback, confirmed with the user). The upload row is inserted immediately as `status='pending'` *before* parsing begins, so a failure at any later step updates it to `status='error'` with the exception message in `notes` rather than leaving no trace at all; on success it's updated to `status='parsed'` with the real `row_count` and a `notes` summary of any skipped/duplicate rows. Bulk insert into `trial_balance_accounts` reuses `templates.py`'s `import_backup()` transaction shape exactly (`get_raw_conn()` → `BEGIN TRANSACTION` → loop inserts → `commit()` / `except: rollback()` / `finally: close()`). Verified end-to-end against an isolated copy of `test.db` (not the live one) by calling the endpoint function directly (bypassing the HTTP layer, since `starlette.testclient` needed an `httpx2` package this environment doesn't have) with hand-built `.xlsx`/`.xls` test files: the tricky code `10-10-25-10` round-tripped exactly with correct `level`/`parent_account_code`/`classification`; a small known hierarchy (`1`, `1-100`, `1-100-001`, `1-200`, `2`) classified correctly (`1`/`1-100` parent, the rest leaf); a "Type" column's values landed in `source_account_type` without affecting `classification`; one blank-code row and one duplicate-code row were each correctly skipped and counted; a legacy `.xls` file (no Type column, testing the optional-role gap) parsed correctly; a file with no Code-like header was correctly rejected with `status='error'` and the exact message in `notes`; an unknown `client_id` correctly 404'd and a malformed `as_of_date` correctly 400'd, neither leaving a stray upload row. Confirmed `main.py` mounts the router correctly (`/api/trial-balance/upload` present in the built OpenAPI schema) and that `clients`/`client_data`/`audit_rule_categories` row counts were unaffected by any of this. `python -m py_compile routers/trial_balance.py main.py` passes. The `xlwt` package was installed *temporarily* only to construct the `.xls` test fixture in this session (not a runtime dependency, not added to `requirements.txt`) and was uninstalled again afterward.

Frontend: `buildAssignCategoriesRow()`'s disabled `-- Not assigned --` placeholder became a real, selectable `value="none"` option; the row `<select>` change listener and the force-apply icon's click handler both now convert `"none"` → `null` via a new shared `parseAssignCategoriesSelectValue()` (the force-apply handler also lost its old "select a category first" guard, since "Not assigned" is now a valid force-apply target — exactly what makes case (2) of the requirement work: force-applying "Not assigned" on a parent clears it and cascades that clearing to every descendant, overwriting whatever they had). `getAssignCategoriesCategoryName()` returns `'Not assigned'` for a null/falsy id; `applyCategoryToRows()`/the error-revert path use `categoryId || 'none'` as the `<select>`'s value string, since a real `<select>` has no null value; success-toast wording switches between "Category assigned"/"Category cleared" based on whether the new value is a real category. New "🔄 Reset" button in the Assign Categories header (`.ar-btn-reset-categories`, `margin-left:auto` pushes it to the far right of the existing flex header row) — behind a native `confirm()` (bulk + hard-to-reverse), calls the new reset endpoint, then does a full `loadAssignCategoriesData()` reload rather than a local state patch, simplest way to guarantee the table matches the server after a change touching every row. ## Verification ↔ Assign Categories Link (11 entries)


- **Verification page hard-refresh view persistence (confirmed fix, `static/verification.js` + `static/verification.html`)**: the page's three JS-driven views (dashboard/cashbook/session) are now reflected in the URL via `state`/`id` query params, distinct from the pre-existing **entry-only** `type`/`view` params (`?type=cash`, `?view=cashbook`/`?view=bankbook` — those only mean "open the Start-Verification popup" and are read once by `window.onload`; never reuse those two values for anything else). New scheme: `?state=cashbook&id=<cashbook name>&type=cash|bank` and `?state=session&id=<session id>&type=cash|bank`; dashboard = no `state`/`id` at all. `setVerificationUrl(view, id)` is the single place that writes this, via `history.replaceState` (never `pushState` — this page manages its own "back" behavior through `setBackOverride()`/the global navbar arrow, not the browser's native back button, so no new history entries should ever be introduced here). Two existing functions were split into a thin guard/POST half plus a shared "activate this view" core, so both the normal click-driven path and the hard-refresh restore path go through identical code: `openCashbook()` → `activateCashbookView(cashbook)`; `startSessionFromCashbook()` → `activateSessionView(sessionId)`. New `restoreCashbookView(cashbookName)`/`restoreSessionView(sessionId)` (called only from `window.onload`, checked ahead of the existing `type`/`view` popup-trigger logic, which is otherwise untouched) always re-fetch fresh from the server rather than restoring any cached state — `restoreSessionView()` uses the existing `GET /api/verification/audited_cashbook/{id}` (routers/verification.py) as its existence+data check, since it already 404s cleanly on a missing/cancelled session; **note its response nests session fields under `data.session`, not top-level** (e.g. `data.session.cashbook_name`, not `data.cashbook_name` — a real bug caught during this session's own verification, before it shipped). On a 404/failure, `showDashboardWithMessage(message)` switches back to the dashboard, resets the URL to plain, and shows a new `#dashboardFallbackMessage` div (static/verification.html, inside `#dashboardContent`, reuses the existing `.upload-status`/`.error` classes already used by `#verificationStatus` elsewhere on this page — no new CSS) instead of leaving a broken session screen. `exitCashbookView()`/`exitSession()` each gained one line to keep the URL in sync when leaving a view (`setVerificationUrl('dashboard')` / `setVerificationUrl('cashbook', selectedCashbook)`). The Transaction Report view is intentionally not covered by this scheme (out of the confirmed brief). Verified end-to-end against the user's already-running `--reload` dev server (port 5000, `netstat`-checked first, not restarted) using real ACME data (client 1, session 364): confirmed `GET /api/verification/audited_cashbook/364` returns the nested `{session: {...}, transactions: [...]}` shape (caught and fixed the `data.cashbook_name` bug this way, before it could ship); confirmed a nonexistent session id (`999999`) 404s cleanly with `"Verification session not found or cancelled."`, exercising the fallback path; confirmed `GET /api/verification/cashbooks` (used by `restoreCashbookView()`'s `loadCashbooks()` call) is unaffected. `node --check static/verification.js` passes; grepped the HTML addition and confirmed no inline event handlers were introduced. No Playwright/browser tool was available this session (same recurring gap as most phases in this app's history), so the actual hard-refresh click-through in a real browser (URL updating live, session/cashbook view re-populating on reload, the fallback message rendering for a genuinely-gone session) was not visually confirmed — worth a manual pass. **Follow-up fix, same day**: this visual gap in verification meant a real bug shipped — `activateSessionView()` never explicitly hid `dashboardContent` (unlike `activateCashbookView()`, which already did), so hard-refreshing straight into `?state=session&id=...` rendered the dashboard stacked underneath the session view. Fixed by adding the same `dashboardContent.style.display = 'none';` line `activateCashbookView()` already had. **Lesson**: when adding a new entry path into an existing "activate this view" function (here, calling `activateSessionView()` directly from a URL restore instead of only via `startSessionFromCashbook()`, which happened to always run after the dashboard was already hidden by a prior step), audit that function's own display-toggle completeness independently — don't assume it's correct just because every previous call site happened to reach it in a state where the omission was invisible. **Second follow-up fix, same day**: the same blind spot existed on the way *out* of a session — `exitSession()` manually re-implemented a subset of `activateCashbookView()`'s job (display toggling, back-override, URL, `fetchCashbookData()`) instead of calling it, so it inherited none of `activateCashbookView()`'s/`loadCashbooks()`'s actual population of the cashbook selector/date range, which only mattered once a session became reachable without ever passing through `openCashbook()` first (i.e. via `restoreSessionView()`). Fixed by having `exitSession()` call `restoreCashbookView(selectedCashbook)` directly instead of hand-rolling a partial copy of what it does. **General rule this keeps surfacing**: once a view can be entered from more than one path (normal click-through vs. URL restore), every function that *transitions into or out of* that view must go through the one shared "activate"/"restore" function for it, never a hand-rolled subset — the subset is exactly what silently drifts out of sync when a new entry path is added later. **Third follow-up fix, same day (confirmed fix, `static/verification.js` only)**: a hard refresh correctly restored the right session but always landed on the session's earliest-Pending voucher (`loadNextTransaction()`'s default), not the voucher the auditor was actually on — e.g. after navigating without validating every voucher in strict order. Extended the same scheme with a new `voucher` URL param (the voucher_id string) kept in sync by new `setVerificationUrlVoucher(voucherId)` (a dedicated writer, separate from `setVerificationUrl()` since it fires on every voucher-to-voucher move and shouldn't re-touch `state`/`id`/`type`; no-op outside `state=session`) — called, per explicit confirmation, at all three places `currentVoucherId` is actually assigned, not just Prev/Next: `loadNextTransaction()`, `moveToAdjacentVoucher()` (Prev/Next arrows), and `navigateToTransaction()` (the 🔍 search-popover row click) — `completeTransaction()`'s auto-advance-after-verifying needed no separate wiring since it just calls `loadNextTransaction()` internally, already covered. `setVerificationUrl()` itself now also unconditionally clears the `voucher` param on every view transition, so a stale voucher id from a previous session/cashbook is never carried over. `activateSessionView(sessionId, targetVoucherId = null)` gained the optional second parameter: if given and a matching entry exists in the already-loaded `sessionTransactions`, it calls the existing `navigateToTransaction(matchingDetailId)` directly (reusing its synchronous full-voucher render, zero new fetches) instead of the default `loadNextTransaction()`; falls back to that default if no target was given or the target voucher no longer exists in the session — `startSessionFromCashbook()`'s call (a freshly-started session) omits the param and is completely unaffected. `restoreSessionView()` reads the `voucher` param from the URL and passes it through. No backend/schema changes. Verified end-to-end against the user's already-running `--reload` dev server (port 5000, `netstat`-checked first, not restarted) using real ACME data (session 364, 311 transactions across many distinct vouchers): confirmed `GET /api/verification/audited_cashbook/364`'s per-line `detail_id`/`voucher_id` fields match exactly what the new matching logic in `activateSessionView()` reads; regression-confirmed `GET /api/verification/next/364` and `GET /api/clients` unaffected. `node --check static/verification.js` passes; grepped and confirmed all three `currentVoucherId = ...` assignment sites now call `setVerificationUrlVoucher`. No Playwright/browser tool was available this session, so the actual click-through (navigate to voucher 3 of 7, hard-refresh, land back on voucher 3; same after a popover jump and after completing a voucher) was not visually confirmed — worth a manual pass.

- **Verification ↔ Assign Categories link (new, confirmed 5-phase requirement) — Phase 1 of 5 (database schema, `database.py` only)**: new `account_category_assignments` table, added in `init_db()` right after the Trial Balance module block. Schema only this phase: no backend endpoint, no UI, and deliberately no data migration/backfill from the existing per-upload `trial_balance_accounts.category_id` — that carry-forward logic belongs to Phase 2.
