## Voucher Supporting-Document Linking (incl. follow-up fixes) (33 entries)


- **Observation roll-up should replace-per-procedure, not append-forever (confirmed fix, `routers/verification.py` only) — supersedes the append-based design of every earlier observation-sync fix above.** Reported directly against the screenshots from the previous fix's own live testing: repeatedly editing the *same* procedure's observation box ("Hello World 1" → "2" → "3") kept stacking up separate lines for that one box instead of replacing its own line — the `last_synced_text` duplicate-suppression column (added two fixes ago) only ever stopped an *unchanged* re-save from duplicating; it did nothing for a genuine edit, which is exactly what was happening. Required behaviour: the voucher's Observation field holds **exactly one labelled line per document/procedure at all times** — saving that procedure's box again replaces its own line in place, every other procedure's line stays untouched. **`sync_line_observations_to_voucher()` was rewritten from incremental-append to a full rebuild on every call**, rather than a find/replace on the stored text (considered and rejected as more fragile — opaque string-splicing on an already-assembled blob, vs. deriving the whole field fresh from the one table that's the actual source of truth). Every call now: reads **every** `voucher_line_observations` row across all sibling lines (not filtered to `synced = 0` anymore — this is the key correctness point, since only considering "pending" rows would silently drop an untouched procedure's line from the rebuilt text); dedupes to one row per `document_id`, keeping whichever sibling's entry has the latest `updated_at` (same tie-break `get_line_observations()` already uses for the identical cross-session scenario); drops any document whose current text is blank (so clearing a box removes its line entirely, not leaves a stale one); builds one block per remaining document ordered by `document_id` ascending for a stable order; and **overwrites** `verification_details.observations` with the result (or `NULL` if nothing remains) instead of appending. Confirmed via grep before implementing that this column has exactly one writer in the entire codebase — this same function — and no manual-entry UI exists anywhere that types into it directly, so a full overwrite can't clobber anything else. **`synced`/`last_synced_text` are now bookkeeping-only, not gating logic** — every entry is considered on every rebuild regardless of its synced state, since omitting an already-synced entry would silently drop its line; the two fields are still written per entry (for consistency/audit visibility) but nothing reads them to decide whether to include a block anymore. This makes the two fixes immediately above (orphaned-session sync, immediate-sync-on-save) still fully valid — sibling resolution and the "sync on every explicit save" trigger are both unchanged and still correct — only *how the field is assembled* changed, from append to rebuild. Verified end-to-end against the user's already-running `--reload` dev server (port 5000, `netstat`-checked first, not restarted) using the exact real repro line (voucher CPV-0726-222, "LOCAL PURCHASE (CASH)", client_data_id 5055, detail_id 84644): confirmed the pre-existing 3-line duplicate ("Hello World 1/2/3", all under Purchase Demand); re-saving Purchase Demand's box with new text correctly collapsed this to exactly one line (and, as a genuine side effect of now reading *all* entries not just pending ones, correctly also picked up a previously-orphaned "Purchase Order: hello" line from an *earlier sibling session* — 84333 — that the old append-only/synced-filtered logic had never surfaced at all, itself another small instance of the same class of bug these fixes have been closing); saving a fresh Vendor Bill observation correctly appeared as its own new line with Purchase Demand/Purchase Order untouched; editing Vendor Bill again correctly changed only its own line; clearing Vendor Bill correctly removed its line entirely while the other two lines were untouched. All test-induced state reverted afterward, confirmed via a follow-up query matching the exact pre-test row values. `python -m py_compile routers/verification.py` passes. No frontend changes were needed — `static/verification.js`'s `saveLineObservation()`/`renderVoucherLines()` (wired in the fix directly above) already display whatever `verification_details.observations` currently holds, so the corrected rebuild logic is reflected automatically with no JS changes.

- **Wire up the OBSERVATIONS column + suppress duplicate roll-up blocks (confirmed fix, `database.py` + `routers/verification.py` + `static/verification.js`) — two findings surfaced re-verifying the fix directly above in the browser, not by either fix itself being wrong.** Finding 1: the backend sync was (and is) genuinely correct, but the voucher table's "OBSERVATIONS" column has never displayed anything — it's the `<span class="voucher-line-observations-cell"></span>` placeholder added on 2026-07-15, explicitly logged then as "a future addition, not yet wired to any state/backend field," and nothing since (including the two sync fixes above) ever wired it. Fixed: `_fetch_session_details_grouped()` (routers/verification.py) now also selects `vd.observations`; `_build_verification_line()` returns it as an additive `"observations"` field, so `/next`, `/voucher_nav`, and every other caller of these shared helpers now carry it with no new endpoint. `save_line_observation()`'s response gained an additive `voucher_observations` field (the line's current, just-synced `verification_details.observations` text). `renderVoucherLines()` (static/verification.js) now fills `.voucher-line-observations-cell` from `line.observations` (via the existing `escapeHtml()` helper); `saveLineObservation()` additionally writes the fresh value into `currentVoucherLines` (so a later full re-render stays correct) and directly into the live DOM cell (`` .voucher-line-row[data-detail-id="${uid}"] .voucher-line-observations-cell ``, same "target by data-detail-id" convention `validateTransaction()` already uses for the status cell) — the auditor now sees the update the moment Save is clicked, no navigation needed. **No CSS added** — multi-block text (`\n`-separated in storage) currently collapses to one line in the cell (default `white-space: normal`, no wrap/line-break styling); a future pass could style this, out of scope for this phase's approved file list. Finding 2: because sync now fires on every individual "Save Observation" click (the fix above) rather than once per navigation, saving the *same* text twice in a row now appended two identical blocks instead of the old harmless no-op. Fixed by adding a nullable `last_synced_text` column to `voucher_line_observations` (database.py, standard idempotent `CREATE TABLE` + `ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN` upgrade-block pattern, since the table already has live data) recording what text was last actually rolled up for that `(voucher_line_id, document_id)` — distinct from `observation_text`, which always holds the current saved value even before syncing. `sync_line_observations_to_voucher()` now only appends a block when a pending entry's `observation_text` (stripped) differs from `last_synced_text` (stripped) *and* is non-blank; every processed entry gets `last_synced_text` set to its own `observation_text` alongside `synced = 1` (now a per-row `UPDATE` in a loop, not the previous single bulk `IN (...)` statement, since the value differs per row). A genuine edit still appends its own distinct block — only exact repeats are suppressed. Verified end-to-end against the live `--reload` dev server (auto-reloaded on the edits, not restarted): migration confirmed via an isolated `test.db` copy (added via the `ALTER TABLE` path since the table pre-existed, a second `init_db()` run a clean no-op) and re-confirmed on the real `test.db`; against the real line from this session's trace (voucher CPV-0726-119, "Kitchen Expense CHS Residence", Vendor Bill document) — re-saving identical text a second time correctly produced no new block, while editing and re-saving with different text correctly appended a distinct new block; confirmed `voucher_observations` appears in the save response and `observations` now appears on every line from `GET /api/verification/voucher_nav`. All test-induced state reverted afterward, confirmed via a follow-up query matching the exact pre-test row values. `python -m py_compile database.py routers/verification.py` and `node --check static/verification.js` both pass. No Playwright/browser tool was available this session, so the actual on-screen column rendering and live cell update after clicking Save Observation were not visually confirmed — worth a manual pass.

- **Observation roll-up doesn't fire until an unrelated later action (confirmed fix, `routers/verification.py` only) — a different, narrower gap than the one directly above.** Live-tracing a brand-new observation save (not a pre-existing orphaned record) proved the fix above works correctly — a comment saved under an earlier session's line rolled up the moment `save_line_items()` next ran for it. But the *newest* comment (same voucher/line, current session) was still sitting `synced=0`, simply because **nothing had called `save_line_items()` for that specific line since it was typed** — `POST /api/verification/save_line_observation` (`save_line_observation()`) has always only written the entry and left the roll-up entirely dependent on some later, unrelated action (Next/Prev/Validate/Complete/Exit). From the auditor's side, clicking "💾 Save Observation" reads as a complete action, so waiting on an unrelated later click is a real gap, confirmed with the user. Fixed by having `save_line_observation()` call the existing `sync_line_observations_to_voucher(voucher_line_id)` **immediately** after the upsert, before the response is built (so the response's own `synced` field is truthful right away too) — no changes to `sync_line_observations_to_voucher()` itself, which was already safe to call here as-is: idempotent (no-op if nothing pending) and marks entries synced as it goes, so `save_line_items()`'s own pre-existing call to the same helper (kept, unchanged, as a safety net) correctly finds nothing left to do on a later Next/Prev — no double-append. **Confirmed acceptable side effect**: `sync_line_observations_to_voucher()` has no line-status gate (only `save_line_items()`'s "must be Pending" check does), so an observation can now roll up even after the line has already been validated/completed — this only ever touches the `observations` field, not validation state, so it's a genuine improvement, not a regression. Verified live end-to-end against the exact pending entry from this trace (`voucher_line_id` 84022, document 15, "Hello World"): the very next `save_line_observation` call returned `synced: true` immediately (no `save_line_items` call in between) and `verification_details.observations` picked up the appended block right away; a second edit-and-resave with different text correctly appended a second distinct block (append-only preserved, no overwrite); a follow-up `save_line_items` call for the same line correctly found nothing pending and added nothing further (no double-append). All test-induced state reverted afterward, confirmed via a follow-up query matching the exact pre-test row values. `python -m py_compile routers/verification.py` passes. No frontend changes were needed — the immediate sync happens transparently server-side within the same request `saveLineObservation()` (`static/verification.js`) already makes.

- **Observation sync doesn't roll up across orphaned sessions (confirmed fix, `routers/verification.py` only) — supersedes the Phase 3 entry directly above's claim that `sync_line_observations_to_voucher()` "is untouched — it still only ever rolls an entry into its *own* `voucher_line_id`'s ... field, since that's inherently a per-session concern."** That claim turned out to be the actual bug: diagnosed directly against live `test.db` (not re-derived from code) — every one of the 4 existing `voucher_line_observations` rows was `synced=0` despite belonging to `Pending` lines (ruling out the "line already verified" gate in `save_line_items()` as the cause). Tracing `audit_log`+`verification_sessions` showed the real pattern: each time an observation was saved, a *new* verification session started (same root cause as the Phase 3 entry above — `start_verification_session()` has no resume logic) before that exact `voucher_line_id` ever got another `save_line_items()` call — so the observation's own session-specific id was orphaned before the sync could ever run for it, and `sync_line_observations_to_voucher()`'s `WHERE vlo.voucher_line_id = ?` (literal id only, no sibling resolution) could never find it again from a later session. Fixed by having `sync_line_observations_to_voucher(voucher_line_id)` call the existing `_resolve_sibling_voucher_line_ids()` (same helper the Phase 3 fix already uses for every *read* path) first, then querying/marking-synced across that whole sibling set (`WHERE voucher_line_id IN (...)`) instead of the single literal id — still rolling the collected text into the *current* (active) line's own `observations` field, still append-only, still never raising. Verified against live data: called `save_line_items` for the most recent of 3 sibling lines sharing one `client_data_id` (5055) — all 3 previously-orphaned entries (spanning 3 different sessions) were correctly picked up, their two non-blank texts both appended in one combined block with no duplication, all 3 flipped to `synced=1`, and a 4th, unrelated row (different `client_data_id`) was correctly left untouched, confirming sibling resolution stays scoped per accounting line. Test-induced state fully reverted afterward, confirmed via a follow-up query matching the exact pre-test row values. `python -m py_compile routers/verification.py` passes. No frontend changes were needed — `static/verification.js`'s `saveLineObservation()` already saves correctly against whatever `uid` is open; the gap was entirely in the backend roll-up's read scope.

- **Voucher Supporting-Document Linking follow-up, Phase 3 of 4 — the real (deeper) Browse/Linked Evidence cross-session sync bug (confirmed fix, `routers/verification.py` + `routers/data.py` + `static/verification.js`)**: the fix immediately above solved a real but narrower same-session/different-document-tab disagreement; it did **not** fix the reported "Browse shows Assigned but Linked Evidence doesn't show it" symptom for CPV-0726-222/Purchase Demand, diagnosed this phase directly against `test.db`. **Root cause, confirmed with real data, not re-guessed from code**: `start_verification_session()` (routers/verification.py) has no "resume an existing session" logic — every time a cashbook is opened and verification is (re)started, a brand-new `verification_sessions` row and a brand-new set of `verification_details` rows are inserted for every voucher/line, even ones already worked on before (`test.db` had 393 such sessions for one cashbook at time of diagnosis). `voucher_line_documents` (Phase 1), `voucher_line_procedure_checks` (Phase 5), and `voucher_line_observations` (Phase 6) all key their data off `voucher_line_id` = `verification_details.id` — a **per-session, ephemeral id**, not a stable identity for "this voucher line." Proof: the real "LOCAL PURCHASE (CASH)" line of CPV-0726-222 is `client_data.id = 5055` (stable); in session 382 it was `verification_details.id = 78735` (Purchase Demand evidence linked there); in session 393 (the latest session) the *same* line is `verification_details.id = 82156` — Linked Evidence, filtered by `voucher_line_id = 82156`, could never see the assignment made under 78735, while Browse still correctly (if misleadingly) reported it "Assigned to CPV-0726-222" since it just resolves the assignment's own stored `voucher_line_id` back to a still-valid `transaction_ref` from the *old* session, with no check of whether that belongs to the currently-open one. **Fix (confirmed with the user: read-time resolution only, no schema migration, no change to session-start behavior, writes untouched)**: new `_resolve_sibling_voucher_line_ids(voucher_line_id)` (routers/verification.py, next to `assign_supporting_document`) returns every `verification_details.id` across *all* sessions that shares the same underlying `client_data_id` as the given line — i.e. every past/present copy of that exact accounting line. `get_voucher_line_documents()`, `get_procedure_checks()`, and `get_line_observations()` all now query `WHERE voucher_line_id IN (...)` (the resolved sibling set) instead of `= ?`; `get_procedure_checks()`/`get_line_observations()` additionally dedup in Python by `(document_id, role_name)`/`document_id` respectively, keeping whichever sibling's row has the latest `checked_at`/`updated_at`, since two different sessions could each carry their own tick/observation for the same document — `get_voucher_line_documents()` needs no dedup (the partial unique index on `client_data_id` already guarantees one evidence row is never actively linked under more than one sibling). `sync_line_observations_to_voucher()` (called from `save_line_items()`) is untouched — it still only ever rolls an entry into its *own* `voucher_line_id`'s `verification_details.observations` field, since that's inherently a per-session concern. For Browse's own "is this the same line" check (previously `String(row.assigned_to_voucher_line) === String(uid)`, broken for the same cross-session reason), `get_assignment_status_map()` gained an additive `voucher_line_client_data_id` field (the assigned row's own `vd.client_data_id`), threaded through `routers/data.py`'s `attach_assignment_flags()` as a new additive `assigned_to_line_client_data_id` field on `GET /api/data/preview`. Frontend: new shared `isSameUnderlyingLine(uid, row)` (static/verification.js, next to `formatAssignedVoucherLabel()`) looks up the current line's own `client_data_id` via `currentVoucherLines` (already carries it — confirmed via `_fetch_session_details_grouped()`'s response shape) and compares it against `row.assigned_to_line_client_data_id`, replacing the raw `voucher_line_id === uid` comparison in both `buildProcedureResultRowHtml()`'s `isSameLine` and `buildProcedureBrowseTableHtml()`'s `isOtherDocSameLine`. **Any future new query against `voucher_line_documents`/`voucher_line_procedure_checks`/`voucher_line_observations` that filters by a single `voucher_line_id` should go through `_resolve_sibling_voucher_line_ids()` first** (for reads) — a bare `WHERE voucher_line_id = ?` will silently miss history from any earlier session, exactly as this bug did. Verified end-to-end against the user's already-running `--reload` dev server (port 5000, `netstat`-checked first, not restarted) using the exact known-broken case: `GET /api/verification/voucher_line_documents/82156` now correctly returns the Purchase Demand assignments originally made under session 382's `voucher_line_id=78735` (client_data_id 5662/5663) alongside session 393's own; `GET /api/data/preview` for client_data_id 5662 correctly returns `assigned_to_line_client_data_id: 5055`, matching the current line's own `client_data_id`; `get_procedure_checks`/`get_line_observations` for the same line return correctly (no dedup collisions in the live data); a nonexistent `voucher_line_id` still 404s on all three endpoints; a voucher line with no cross-session history still returns cleanly (single-row `IN (x)` behaves identically to `= x`). `python -m py_compile routers/verification.py routers/data.py` and `node --check static/verification.js` all pass. No Playwright/browser tool was available this session, so the actual browser click-through (Browse showing "Already linked here" and the item appearing in Linked Evidence for the exact same reopened line) was not visually confirmed — worth a manual pass. Phase 4 (confirmatory tick shortcut) not started.

- **Browse-Status vs Linked-Evidence disagreement fix (confirmed fix, `routers/verification.py` + `routers/data.py` + `static/verification.js` + `static/style.css`)**: `get_assignment_status_map(client_data_ids)` (routers/verification.py) previously returned only `voucher_line_id`/`voucher_id` per assigned client_data row — enough to say "this row is assigned to voucher line X" but not "under which Document slot." Since a voucher line's Supporting Documents modal has one tab per Document, and two Documents in the same Category can share the same `template_id`, a row assigned to line X under Document A would still show as `assigned_to_voucher_line === X` when browsing/searching from Document B's own tab on that same line — Browse's Status column (`buildProcedureResultRowHtml()`/`buildProcedureBrowseTableHtml()`) read this as "Already linked here," while the Linked Evidence table (`openProcedureModal()`, filters `voucher_line_documents` by BOTH `voucher_line_id` AND `document_id`) correctly never lists it there, since it belongs to a different tab. Fixed by having `get_assignment_status_map()` also return `document_id`/`document_name` (joined to `audit_rule_documents`), threaded through `routers/data.py`'s `attach_assignment_flags()` as two new additive `GET /api/data/preview` response fields (`assigned_to_document_id`/`assigned_to_document_name`) alongside the pre-existing `is_assigned`/`assigned_to_voucher_line`/`assigned_to_voucher_id`. Frontend: `buildProcedureResultRowHtml()` now takes an `activeDocId` param and only shows "Already linked here" when `assigned_to_document_id` matches the tab actually open; a same-line-different-document match instead shows `Linked to this voucher under "{document name}"` (new distinct wording, not the generic "Assigned to voucher X" used for a genuinely different voucher). `buildProcedureBrowseTableHtml()` similarly appends a muted `(under "{document name}")` note to the Voucher No. cell for the same same-line-different-document case (new `.procedure-browse-other-doc-note` CSS). `GET /api/verification/document_assignment_status` (the other consumer of `get_assignment_status_map()`) was left unchanged — it only reads the specific keys it already used, unaffected by the additive fields. Verified: `node --check static/verification.js` and `python -m py_compile routers/verification.py routers/data.py` all pass; confirmed `static/databank.js` (the other consumer of `GET /api/data/preview`) does not read `is_assigned`/`assigned_to_*` fields at all, so the additive fields are safe there. No Playwright/browser tool was available this session, so the actual Browse/search-dropdown wording for the same-line-different-document case was not visually confirmed — worth a manual pass.

- **Unassign supporting document lines (new, confirmed single-phase requirement) — `database.py` + `routers/verification.py` + `static/verification.js` + `static/style.css`**: **supersedes** the Phase 1 note above's claim that `UNIQUE(client_data_id)` is the enforcement mechanism and that a future unassign endpoint would just `DELETE` the row — that plan was replaced once it became clear a blanket table-level `UNIQUE(client_data_id)` would permanently block reassignment even after a soft-delete flag was added, since the old (now-inactive) row would still occupy the unique slot on that column. `voucher_line_documents` gained `status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'active' CHECK (status IN ('active','unassigned'))` and `unassigned_at TIMESTAMP`; the table-level `UNIQUE(client_data_id)` was replaced by a **partial unique index** — `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX idx_voucher_line_documents_active_client_data ON voucher_line_documents (client_data_id) WHERE status = 'active'` — so "once linked, never assignable again elsewhere" is still enforced at the DB level, but only while the link is active; an unassigned row can coexist with a fresh active link on the same `client_data_id`. **Required a real schema migration**, since SQLite can't drop/alter a table constraint in place and the live `test.db` already had 7 rows on the old shape — followed the exact rename → recreate-with-new-shape → copy rows across (as `status='active'`) → drop-old-table pattern already established by the `client_voucher_prefixes` 5-way category migration (same file, same `.bak-premigrate-<timestamp>` backup convention), gated on detecting the old shape (`PRAGMA table_info` has no `status` column) so it's a no-op on every subsequent startup. **Index-creation ordering gotcha, worth remembering for any future partial-index migration in this file**: the partial unique index's `CREATE INDEX` calls must run *after* the migration block resolves (whether it actually ran or the table was already on the new shape) — placing them directly after the initial `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` (which is a no-op against an old-shape existing table) fails with `no such column: status` on any database still mid-upgrade, since that CREATE TABLE never touches the real existing table. New `POST /api/verification/unassign_document` (body `{assignment_id}` — the `voucher_line_documents.id`, already available client-side as `sel.id`) flips `status`/`unassigned_at`, never deletes the row (`linked_by`/`linked_at` stay intact as a provenance trail); 404s on an unknown id or one already unassigned. **Every existing query reading this table needed a `status = 'active'` filter added** — `assign_supporting_document`'s duplicate-link check, `get_voucher_line_documents` (list-by-line), and `get_assignment_status_map` (the shared helper both this router's `document_assignment_status` endpoint and `routers/data.py`'s `GET /api/data/preview` per-row assignment flags call) — an unassigned row must never be treated as a live link by any of them; a future new query against `voucher_line_documents` must apply the same filter. Frontend: `buildSelectedLinesTable()` (`static/verification.js`) gained a trailing icon-only column with a `.procedure-unlink-btn` ✕ button per row (`data-assignment-id`), wired in `renderProcedureModalPanel()` alongside the existing per-render checklist-checkbox wiring; `unassignSupportingDocument(uid, docId, assignmentId)` gates on a native `confirm()` (matching this app's established single-flat-destructive-action convention), POSTs the new endpoint, then removes the entry from `tabState.selections` and — if that was the tab's last selection — clears `docId` from `lineState.assignedDocIds` (un-filling the tab dot) before re-rendering the tab bar and panel; re-rendering reuses the exact same `getSelectedLinesSummary()`/`buildSelectedLinesTable()` code Phase 4 already built, so the running total and Matches/mismatch badge recalculate with no new logic. Observation text for the tab is deliberately left untouched by this action, per the confirmed brief. No changes to the search/browse assignment flow — a freed row becomes selectable again automatically, since it reads `is_assigned` sourced from the now-active-only `get_assignment_status_map()`. Verified end-to-end against the user's already-running `--reload` dev server (port 5000, `netstat`-checked first, not restarted — the server's own auto-reload picked up the `database.py` edit and ran the migration against the real `test.db` automatically, preserving all 7 pre-existing rows as `status='active'`, confirmed via direct query before and after): unassigned a real link, confirmed it disappeared from `GET /voucher_line_documents/{id}` and `GET /document_assignment_status` reported the row free again, confirmed a duplicate-unassign attempt and an unknown `assignment_id` both 404 with distinct messages, then — the core scenario this migration exists to enable — reassigned the freed `client_data_id` to a *different* voucher line and confirmed it succeeded (`HTTP 200`, new row, old inactive row untouched). All test state reverted afterward (original row restored to `status='active'`, the transient reassignment row deleted) — confirmed via a follow-up `GET` that `test.db` matches its pre-test 7-row state exactly. `python -m py_compile database.py routers/verification.py` and `node --check static/verification.js` both pass; grepped and confirmed zero inline event handlers introduced. No Playwright/browser tool was available this session (same recurring gap as most phases in this app's history), so the actual ✕ click / confirm dialog / table-and-badge refresh in a real browser were not visually confirmed — worth a manual pass.

- **Voucher Supporting-Document Linking, Phase 6 of 6, FINAL (observation flow, `database.py` + `routers/verification.py` + `static/verification.js` + `static/style.css`)**: `voucher_line_observations` (one row per `voucher_line_id`+`document_id`, `UNIQUE` constraint, upserted in place — not an append-only history log) is the persistence layer for each Document tab's own observation text; its `synced` flag is what separates "saved on this tab" from "already rolled into the voucher line's own text field." **The actual roll-up chokepoint is `save_line_items()`** (`routers/verification.py`) — every Save/Next/Prev/Validate/Complete/Exit path in `static/verification.js` already funnels through it once per line (see `saveAllVoucherLines()`), so `sync_line_observations_to_voucher()` was hooked there rather than into `validate_transaction()`/`complete_transaction()` separately; a future phase adding a new "save this line" path must call `save_line_items()` (or explicitly re-invoke the sync helper) rather than bypassing it, or newly-saved observations will silently never reach `verification_details.observations`. **Append-only is enforced by construction, not by a flag check**: the sync helper always reads the field's current value first and concatenates onto it — a manually-typed prior note (if any auditor ever types directly into that column via some other future UI) is never at risk of being clobbered by this feature. **Every explicit save via `POST /api/verification/save_line_observation` unconditionally resets `synced=0`**, regardless of whether the text actually changed — this is deliberate (simpler and always-correct vs. diffing old/new text), so re-clicking Save with identical text is a harmless no-op re-append-preventing operation once synced, but re-triggers a real (if redundant) sync cycle. The auto-suggestion (`buildObservationSuggestion()`) is a **one-shot fill** gated by a client-only `suggestionApplied` flag on each tab's state (never persisted) — it fills an empty box at most once per modal-open lifetime and is never reapplied over auditor-edited or auditor-cleared text, including after an explicit Save (which also sets `suggestionApplied = true`, since a save is a final decision on that tab's text). `getSelectedLinesSummary()` was factored out of `buildSelectedLinesTable()` specifically so the mismatch computation backing both the Phase 4 badge and this phase's suggestion text can never drift apart — extend that one function, not two, if the mismatch rule ever changes.

- **Voucher Supporting-Document Linking, Phase 2 of 6 (search filter on Data Bank preview, `routers/data.py` + `routers/verification.py`)**: backend/query only, no UI. **Two of the brief's three "locked assumptions" turned out to already be satisfied by existing code, not new work**: `GET /api/data/preview`'s existing `search: Optional[str]` param already matches against any column value via `json_each(cd.row_data)` — exactly the "generic filter, not hardcoded to specific field names" requirement — so no new filter param was added; and "filtering is scoped to the template linked via the Document's `template_id`" just describes how a caller picks `template_id` (from `audit_rule_documents.template_id`, already live since Audit Rules Phase 9) before calling the existing endpoint, not a new backend capability. **The actual new work**: each row in the response now carries `is_assigned` (bool), `assigned_to_voucher_line` (int or `null` — `verification_details.id`), and `assigned_to_voucher_id` (str or `null` — the human-readable voucher number), sourced from Phase 1's `voucher_line_documents` table, via a new `attach_assignment_flags(rows)` in `routers/data.py` — mirrors the existing `attach_history_flags(rows)`'s convention exactly (one batched query per page, not one query per row, mutating each row dict in place with additive fields), called right after it in `get_preview_rows()`. **Reuse over duplication**: rather than re-writing the `voucher_line_documents` ⋈ `verification_details` join a second time in `routers/data.py`, Phase 1's `GET /api/verification/document_assignment_status` endpoint (`routers/verification.py`) had its join extracted into a new shared helper `get_assignment_status_map(client_data_ids) -> {client_data_id: {voucher_line_id, voucher_id}}` — the endpoint itself is now a thin wrapper over this helper (pure refactor, same request/response shape, re-verified unchanged), and `routers/data.py` imports and calls the helper directly (no HTTP round-trip). **No circular import**: confirmed before implementing that only `routers/verification.py` imports from other `routers/*` modules (`import_export.py`, `audit_rules.py`) — neither of those imports from `routers/data.py`, so `routers/data.py` importing from `routers/verification.py` is safe; this is the first time `routers/data.py` imports from another router module, so if a future phase adds a reverse dependency (`routers/verification.py` needing something from `routers/data.py`), re-check for a cycle before adding it. `get_dataset_rows()` (the other, upload-scoped preview endpoint in the same file) was deliberately left untouched — a different browsing context with no client+template+date-range scoping, not what Phase 4's search UI will call. Verified end-to-end against the user's already-running `--reload` dev server (port 5000, `netstat`-checked first, not restarted): re-ran Phase 1's `document_assignment_status` test cases (3 unassigned ids) and confirmed identical output to before the refactor; created one disposable test assignment (voucher line 61109, `client_data_id` 5670, document 21) and confirmed `GET /api/data/preview` for that row's client/template/date-range returned `is_assigned: true` with the correct `assigned_to_voucher_line`/`assigned_to_voucher_id`, while 4 other rows on the same page correctly showed `is_assigned: false`; confirmed the existing `search` param still narrows correctly (`search=GP-0626-145` → 1 row, still carrying the correct `is_assigned: true`). Test assignment deleted afterward, re-confirmed via a follow-up `GET /api/data/preview` call that every row on that page is back to `is_assigned: false`. `python -m py_compile routers/data.py routers/verification.py` passes. Phase 3 (tabbed modal shell) not started.

- **Voucher Supporting-Document Linking (new, confirmed 6-phase requirement) — Phase 1 of 6 (locking data model + assignment endpoints, `database.py` + `routers/verification.py`)**: backend/schema only, no UI changes. New `voucher_line_documents` table (`database.py`, added right after `account_category_assignments`) records which Data Bank row (`client_data`) has been linked as supporting evidence to which voucher line (`verification_details.id` — the same "uid"/`detail_id` used throughout `verification.js`), for which Document "slot" (`audit_rule_documents.id` — the live per-Category document list already powering the Supporting column, reused here rather than a free-text document type). **`UNIQUE(client_data_id)` is the actual mechanism enforcing "once linked, never assignable again to any other voucher line"** — a real DB-level constraint, not just an app-layer check. Not removed this phase, per the brief — flagged here for whichever later phase (3: tabbed modal shell) ends up touching that markup. Verified against an isolated copy of `test.db` (not the live one, `database.DB_NAME` reassigned before `init_db()`, per the established isolation approach): table + index created correctly via `PRAGMA table_info()`; `UNIQUE(client_data_id)` correctly rejected a second insert for the same `client_data_id` under a different `voucher_line_id`; a second `init_db()` run was a clean no-op. Verified end-to-end against the user's already-running `--reload` dev server (port 5000, `netstat`-checked first, not restarted) using real ACME data (client 1): assigned a real Gate Pass row (`client_data_id` 5670) to a real voucher line (`detail_id` 61109) for a real Document (id 21, "Cash acknowledgement") — succeeded; a second assign attempt on the same `client_data_id` correctly 400'd naming the voucher/line it's already linked to; list-by-line correctly returned the one assignment with joined Document name and row data; the batch status endpoint correctly reported the assigned row as `assigned: true` (with the right voucher/line) and two other ids as `assigned: false`; bad `voucher_line_id`/`client_data_id`/`document_id` each correctly 404'd with a distinct message. ## Row-level Blank-Field Rejection (8 entries)


- **Row-level blank-field rejection, Phase 4 of 4, FINAL (`static/upload.js`, `routers/import_export.py`, `database.py`)**: this completes the 4-phase requirement. `rejectedRowOverrides` (Phase 3) is now folded into the shared validate/import `payload` object as `force_include_rows: Array.from(rejectedRowOverrides)`, right next to the existing `excluded_rows` line in the `importBtn` click handler — rebuilt fresh on every click, so ticking an override either before or after the Validate call is picked up correctly on the actual Upload click; `performImport()` needed no change since it reuses that same payload object by reference. **Backend design decision**: rather than threading a "this row was force-included" marker through `compare_transactions()`'s own row_data reconstruction, the new `compute_data_quality_flag(row_data, critical_cols)` helper (routers/import_export.py, next to `find_critical_blank_reasons()`) derives the flag from the *final* row_data at insert/update time — if any of the 3 critical columns (Document ID/Amount/Date) is still blank there, the row is flagged `'incomplete'`. This is safe because normal validation already guarantees a non-force-included row can never reach insertion with a blank critical field, so a blank critical field surviving to this point is only possible via an explicit override — no new row-identity tracking was needed, and `compare_transactions()` itself was not touched. `validate_and_import()`'s row-exclusion step changed from unconditionally excluding every `rejected_rows` entry to only excluding those *not* in a new `force_include_set` (built from `ImportRequest.force_include_rows`, same row-number scheme as `excluded_rows`/`rejected_rows[].row_number`) — a force-included row stays in `rows` with its cell genuinely blank, no default ever inserted. All three places a row reaches `client_data` (the "new" and "changed" branches of the change-detection path, and the "first-time upload" insert loop) now compute and persist `data_quality_flag` via this same helper; the "unchanged"/"missing" branches are untouched (no row content changes there). New `client_data.data_quality_flag TEXT DEFAULT NULL` column (database.py) added via the same idempotent `CREATE TABLE` column + `ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN` upgrade-block pattern already used for `document_group_id`/`change_detection_status`/`session_type`. Response: a new `force_included_count` field sits alongside the existing `rejected_count`/`rejected_rows` on `validate_and_import()`'s success response — `rejected_count` keeps its pre-existing meaning (total rows identified as rejected this run, force-included or not), so the frontend derives "truly excluded" as `rejected_count - force_included_count` rather than the backend inventing a third overlapping field. `validate_only()` (the `/validate` preview endpoint) was deliberately left untouched — force-inclusion only matters at actual import time. `showImportSummary()` (static/upload.js) gained a new conditional "Row Exceptions" stat block (same visual pattern as the existing "Change Detection" block, rendered only when `rejected_count > 0`) showing "Rejected (excluded)" and "Imported with missing data" as two explicitly separate tiles — never lumped into one number, per the locked requirement. Verified end-to-end against the live `--reload` dev server (port 5000, `netstat`-checked first, not restarted) using a disposable test client + a 4-row Gate Pass test file (one row each: fully valid, blank Quantity/Amount, blank Transaction Date, blank GP no/Document ID) with `force_include_rows` naming only the blank-Quantity row: `/api/upload/import` correctly inserted 2 rows (the valid one plus the force-included one), left the other two genuinely excluded, returned `rejected_count: 3`/`force_included_count: 1`, and a direct DB query confirmed the force-included row has `Quantity: null` (not a default) and `data_quality_flag: 'incomplete'`, while the fully-valid row has `data_quality_flag: null`. Test client, its `client_data` row, and the uploaded file were deleted afterward. `python -m py_compile`/`node --check` both pass. **Surfacing `data_quality_flag` in Data Bank (icon + All/Complete/Incomplete filter dropdown) is a separate, not-yet-started follow-up phase** — this phase only persists and reports the flag at import time.

- **Row-level blank-field rejection, Phase 3 of 4 (exceptions list UI, `static/upload.html` + `static/upload.js` only)**: `rejectedRowsData` (`Map<excelRowNumber, reasons[]>`) and `rejectedRowOverrides` (`Set<excelRowNumber>`) are the frontend's mirror of a validate/import response's `rejected_rows` field (Phase 2, above) — populated/redrawn by `setRejectedRows(rejectedRowsList)`/`renderRejectedRowsList()`, rendered into `#rowRejectionContainer` (a panel deliberately separate from `#rowExclusionContainer`'s grid — different container, different CSS namespace `.row-rejection-*`, not reusing `.row-flagged`/`.row-validation-failed`/`.row-excluded`). `setRejectedRows()` is called from both places a validate/import response is handled (the `importBtn` click handler's validate branch, `performImport()`'s response handler) exactly the way `setValidationFailedRows()` already is — extend that same pair of call sites, not a new one, if a future phase adds another response-handling path. `rejectedRowOverrides` is **state only as of Phase 3** — nothing yet reads it when building the validate/import payload; Phase 4 is expected to fold `Array.from(rejectedRowOverrides)` into the request payload (mirroring how `excludedRowNumbers` already is) and must also decide what happens to `excludedRowNumbers`/the row-selection grid's own checkbox for a row that's both rejected and overridden. The three reset points (`renderRowExclusionGrid()`, `resetRowExclusionSelections()`, `resetUpload()`) that already clear `validationFailedRows` now also clear `rejectedRowsData`/`rejectedRowOverrides` in lockstep — keep all three in sync if any of these reset points are ever restructured.

- **Row-level blank-field rejection (Phase 2 of 4, `routers/import_export.py`)**: `validate_only()`/`validate_and_import()` no longer flag *any* blank mapped cell as a blocking `"required"` error — only a blank **Document ID**, **Amount**, or **Date** now causes a row-level rejection; a blank value in any other mapped column imports fine (as `None`), same as any other value. Since this schema has no explicit "Document ID"/"Amount"/"Date" column names, the 3 critical roles are identified positionally by new `get_critical_field_columns(template_cols)`: Document ID = the first template column by `sort_order` (same rule `get_document_group_id()` already uses), Amount = the first `Numeric`-typed column, Date = the first `Date`-typed column (both matching `extract_columns_from_row()`'s existing "take first numeric"/"take first date" rules) — a role with no matching column in a given template is simply skipped. New `find_critical_blank_reasons(row, critical_cols, mapping_dict)` (same file, same "blank" test as `apply_edited_cell_values()`) computes per-row rejection reasons, reported in a new, distinct `rejected_rows` field on both endpoints' responses — kept separate from `errors`/`validation_errors`, which now only ever contain genuine data-type mismatches (bad Numeric/Date *format* on a non-blank value) and still block the entire `/api/upload/import` call exactly as before. Blank-critical-field rejections do **not** block the whole import: in `validate_and_import()`, rejected rows are excluded from insertion (reusing the existing `filter_excluded_rows()` helper with the rejected rows' own row numbers — no new filtering logic needed) while every other row in the same file still imports normally. A row can independently appear in both `errors` and `rejected_rows` (e.g. a blank Date in one column plus a bad Numeric format in another) — if `errors` is non-empty the whole import still blocks regardless of `rejected_rows`. Phase 3 (exceptions list UI + override toggle) and Phase 4 (wire overrides through + data quality flag + import summary) are not started — do not assume an override mechanism exists yet; today a critical-field-blank row is unconditionally excluded, no way to force-include it.

## Upload Reliability & Blank-Field Handling (4 entries)


- 2026-07-21: Upload reliability & blank-field handling Phase 2 of 4 (stop the `/api/upload/validate` 500, `routers/import_export.py` only) done — root cause found via the now-working Error Dashboard (Phase 1): ERR-UNK-001 `Object of type time is not JSON serializable`, logged repeatedly against Upload. A Date-typed column's cell (most likely a trailing totals/subtotal row's oddly-formatted Date cell) can come back from pandas as a bare `datetime.time`, which the old `pd.isna()`/`isinstance(value, datetime)` pattern didn't catch (neither flags it), so it fell through into a row_data dict untouched and crashed the first `json.dumps()` call to see it, uncaught. ## Client Data Availability & Coverage Redesign (10 entries)


- **Client Data Availability & Coverage Redesign Phase 3 of 6 (Availability calendar backend, `routers/data.py` only)**: new `GET /api/data/availability/calendar` (`client_id`, one-or-more `template_ids`, `year`, `month`) returns, for each requested template, a per-day status array covering the full month: `present` (client_data exists for that template/date — highest priority, so real data on a Sunday/holiday still counts as present), `sunday` (hardcoded day-of-week check via `datetime(...).strftime('%w') == '0'`, same convention as this file's existing SQL-side `strftime('%w', ...) = '0'` checks — Sundays are never stored in the `holidays` table, per Phase 1's design), `holiday` (resolved via new `_resolve_holidays_for_month(year, month)`, which builds a `{date_str: label}` lookup from the Phase 1 `holidays` table — non-repeating holidays kept only if their stored date falls in the requested year/month; `repeats_yearly` holidays have their month/day projected onto the requested year, so a holiday configured in any past year resolves correctly going forward), or `missing` (none of the above). Each template's response also carries `present_count`/`missing_count`/`sunday_count`/`holiday_count` (always summing to the number of days in the month) so Phase 4's calendar UI doesn't need to re-derive them client-side. This is deliberately a new, additive endpoint, not a modification of the existing `GET /api/data/availability` (which answers a coarser "any data in this date range" question for the still-in-use date-picker/buttons UI) — that endpoint, `database.py`, and `routers/settings.py` were all left completely untouched; holidays are read-only from this endpoint's perspective. Backend-only per the confirmed brief — no frontend changes yet (Phase 4 is the template multi-select + calendar UI that will consume this). Verified end-to-end against the live `--reload` dev server (port 5000, `netstat`-checked first, not restarted) using real ACME data (client 1, July 2026): template 1 (Transaction Report, real data 07-01 to 07-06) correctly returned `present_count: 5` (07-05 is a Sunday, so it's `sunday` not `present`) / `missing_count: 22` / `sunday_count: 4` / `holiday_count: 0`, summing to 31; template 2 (Purchase Demand, no data) correctly returned all-missing/Sunday with `present_count: 0`; temporarily added one one-off holiday (07-14) and one `repeats_yearly` holiday (stored as 2025-07-21) via the existing Phase 1 API and confirmed both resolved correctly as `holiday`-status days for July **2026** (the repeating one correctly projected forward a year) with counts still summing to 31; confirmed 404 on an inactive/nonexistent client or template (naming the specific bad template id) and a clean 422 on `month=13`; confirmed `GET /api/data/availability` and `GET /api/data/preview` are unaffected (regression spot-check). Both test holidays deleted afterward. `python -m py_compile routers/data.py` passes.

New shared `resolve_physical_bill_fields_from_source(source_client_data_id, source_type)` (`source_type` explicitly `'grn'`/`'vendor_bill'`, matching Phase 1's own column values — the caller states which template the row belongs to, this code only confirms the claim, never guesses) resolves Vendor Name/Bill No/Quantity/Rate from a source Store Receiving (GRN) or Vendor Bill (ERP) `client_data` row via `find_named_column()` (reused, already imported) — same pattern as the now-superseded `resolve_vendor_bill_fields_from_grn()` directly above it in the file, which is left completely untouched (its removal is Phase 4). Validates the row's actual `templates.template_name` matches what was claimed (`'store receiving'`/`'vendor bill'`, case-insensitive/trimmed), 400ing with the real name otherwise. Bill No is resolved from a per-source-type column (`'Bill no'` for GRN, `'vendor Bill no'` for Vendor Bill — both confirmed live against real templates before finalizing) and simply omitted (not 400'd) when blank. Amount and Date are deliberately never resolved by this function — Amount is always computed at save time (Qty × Rate), Date stays purely manual. New read-only `GET /api/verification/physical_bill_source_preview/{client_data_id}?source_type=grn|vendor_bill` is a one-line pass-through to the resolver, mirroring `grn_to_vendor_bill_preview`'s own shape. `save_physical_bill` gained 4 new optional params (`quantity`, `rate`, `source_document_row_id`, `source_template`, all `Body(None, embed=True)`) — a manual-entry caller omitting them is byte-identical to before; `amount` itself became optional too, computed server-side (`round(quantity * rate, get_rate_precision())`) whenever quantity+rate are both supplied, otherwise still required and validated exactly as before. The upsert stays full-replace (every column overwritten from `excluded.*`, no `COALESCE`) — confirmed live that a later manual-entry resave of an already-populated bill correctly wipes its quantity/rate/source_* back to NULL, exactly per this design; a future frontend must resend those fields on every save to preserve provenance. `GET /api/verification/physical_bills/{voucher_line_id}` also gained the same 4 columns in its SELECT/response (purely additive) so a later frontend can show "populated from GRN" provenance on reopen. Deliberately not fixed, flagged only: neither `save_physical_bill` nor the new preview endpoint validates that `document_id` is actually a `document_type='physical_bill'` Document — confirmed via investigation this check doesn't exist anywhere today (only `is_active=1` is checked); left alone to avoid changing behavior on an already-shipped manual-entry path, worth a dedicated fix later. Verified via `python -m py_compile routers/verification.py` (passes) and against the user's already-running `--reload` dev server (port 5000, `netstat`-checked, PID 10180, not restarted — auto-reloaded on save): confirmed live column names on both real templates (Store receiving id 5: `Vendor`/`Quantity`/`Rate`/`Bill no`; Vendor Bill id 6: `Vendor`/`Quantity`/`Rate`/`vendor Bill no`) match exactly what the code assumes; the preview endpoint correctly resolved a real GRN row (id 5687, blank Bill no → correctly skipped, `amount_preview: 14400.0`) and a real Vendor Bill row (id 5699, populated Bill No → correctly resolved), correctly 400'd on a claimed-wrong source_type naming the real template, an invalid `source_type`, and a nonexistent row; `save_physical_bill` with `quantity: 10, rate: 25.5` (no `amount`) correctly computed and stored `amount: 255.0` plus the two source fields; a follow-up manual-entry-shape save (no quantity/rate, `amount` required) on the same row correctly reproduced prior behavior exactly, including wiping the previously-set quantity/rate/source_* fields (full-replace, as designed); omitting `amount` with no quantity/rate correctly 400'd; an invalid `source_template` correctly 400'd; `GET physical_bills/1` correctly surfaced all 4 new fields. All disposable test data (the physical bill row and its 2 audit-log entries) removed afterward, confirmed 0 residue; `GET /api/verification/stats` and `GET /api/templates` regression-checked 200. No Playwright/browser tool was available this session — backend-only, no UI surface changed. Remaining 2 phases (frontend trigger on both document types + pre-filled form; cleanup removing the now-superseded Phase-1-original `client_data`-targeted Create-Vendor-Bill-from-GRN code) not started.

- 2026-07-15: Beautified `.cashbook-bar` and added session stats to its left side — "Cashbook: {name}", "Total Vouchers: {n}", "Verified: {n}" (static/verification.js `renderVoucherHeader()`, static/style.css `.cashbook-stats`/`.cashbook-stat*`), bar restyled with a white background + bottom border so it reads as a proper header band, `justify-content: space-between` (stats left, Cashbook button right). Per user's confirmed choice, counts are **voucher-level** (distinct `voucher_id`), not the line-level `total_transactions`/`verified_count` the backend already tracks and the navbar already shows — computed by new `computeVoucherStats()` (static/verification.js, next to `isCurrentTransactionValidated()`), which groups `sessionTransactions` by `voucher_id` and counts a voucher verified only if every one of its lines has `validation_status` Passed/Verified. Caught and fixed a staleness gap during implementation: `sessionTransactions` is fetched once by `loadTransactionList()` and was never patched afterward when a line got validated elsewhere in the flow, so `validateTransaction()` now also writes the fresh `data.validation_status` back into the matching `sessionTransactions` entry (same array `isCurrentTransactionValidated()` already reads) — without this, the new stats (and that pre-existing check) would silently go stale after the first validation. Verified end-to-end with Playwright: stats render correctly (Total Vouchers 7 for the test session) and `computeVoucherStats()` was confirmed correct in isolation by patching two vouchers' lines to Passed via `page.evaluate()` and checking the count came back as 2 — a live UI validate on the actual first test voucher legitimately didn't return "Passed" (a real backend business-rule outcome, not a bug) so it wasn't usable as an end-to-end increment demo; no console errors either way.

- 2026-08-11: **Cashbook Place 2 date range reset on session exit (confirmed fix, `static/verification.js` only)** done. - 2026-08-12: **Audit Workbook restructure, Phase 3 of 3, FINAL (table styling, `static/style.css` only, no JS/backend changes)** done — **this completes the entire 3-phase Audit Workbook restructure requirement.** Root cause of the reported "text flows edge-to-edge, doesn't align under the `<thead>` labels" problem: `.aw-table` had no `table-layout` set (defaults to `auto`), so with a `colspan="6"` voucher header band row mixed in among plain 6-`<td>` line/subtotal rows, the browser's column-width algorithm had no single consistent basis across rows — fixed by `table-layout: fixed` plus explicit `nth-child` percentage widths on `.aw-table th` (12/27/12/14/23/12% across Account/Reference/Amount/Procedures/Observations/Status, Reference/Observations widest since they hold free text/an expandable entries list), which alone makes every row line up under the header regardless of any colspan row's content. Added a light `border-right` (`#e2e8f0`, matching the existing `border-bottom`) to every cell except `:last-child` for a true grid feel, plus `overflow-wrap: break-word` so fixed-width cells wrap instead of overflowing; Amount right-aligned and Procedures/Status centered via `nth-child`, since those hold a number/pill/ring rather than flowing text. **Voucher header band** (`.aw-voucher-header-row td`) gets `#f1f5f9` (this app's existing "muted section" shade, e.g. `.voucher-line-locked`) + bold text + a `border-top: 2px solid #94a3b8` marking the start of a new voucher group, with its own darker hover shade (`#e2e8f0`) since the generic `#f8fafc` hover would visually lighten rather than highlight an already-shaded row. **Subtotal row** (`.aw-subtotal-row td`) reuses this app's already-established total/rollup-row treatment (`#dbeafe` + bold, same as `.aw-total-row`/`.voucher-line-total-row`) plus explicit `border-top`/`border-bottom: 2px solid #94a3b8` per the brief's literal "bordered top/bottom, bold" ask. Deliberately **two different shades** for the band vs. the subtotal (not both `#dbeafe`) — Audit Workbook has three distinct row roles (band/line/subtotal) where the Verification precedent this reuses only has two (header+total bracketing plain lines), so reusing the identical color for both would make the two landmark row types indistinguishable from each other. The existing generic `.aw-table tbody tr:hover` rule was narrowed to `:not(.aw-subtotal-row)` so a non-interactive subtotal row (no `data-voucher-no`/click handler, per Phase 2) never shows a hover state. All colors/border weights are reused from this codebase's own established Verification-module "All Borders" grid convention (`static/style.css` ~2035-2268) — `#94a3b8` as the structural grid-boundary color, `#dbeafe`/bold as the total-row color — not new values, per the confirmed brief's "reuse Verification's existing table/column CSS conventions where they fit." No JS/HTML changes — every new selector targets classes Phase 2 already emits. Verified via a full-file brace-balance check (937 open / 937 close, passes) and against the user's already-running dev server (port 5000, `netstat`-checked — PID changed 9332→9272, restarted outside this session, not by it): `curl`-confirmed the served `style.css` contains all the new selectors (`table-layout: fixed`, `.aw-voucher-header-row td`, `.aw-subtotal-row td`); regression-confirmed `audit_workbook.html`, `verification.html`, and `GET /api/verification/session/458/voucher_stats` all still 200. ## Generic Voucher-Level Checks (6 phases)

- **Full build, Phases 1-6 (`database.py`, `routers/audit_rules.py`, `routers/verification.py`, `static/audit_rules.html`/`.js`, `static/verification.html`/`.js`, `static/style.css`)**: replaced the hardcoded Prepared/Checked/Approved-By voucher-level approval concept with a data-driven, extensible list of global checks. Phase 1: schema — `audit_rule_voucher_checks` (name/sort_order/is_active), `audit_rule_voucher_check_auth_roles` (per-check role gating, modelled on `audit_rule_document_auth_roles`), `voucher_check_status` (per-voucher tick + inline performed-by name, keyed by `client_id`+`transaction_ref` — deliberately not `session_id`+`transaction_ref`, to avoid the sibling-session orphaning bug already fixed three times elsewhere in this module, since reopening a cashbook creates a fresh `verification_sessions` row every time). The old `voucher_approvals` table was left in place, untouched, not dropped/migrated. Phase 2: full soft-delete/restore CRUD in routers/audit_rules.py (`GET/POST /api/audit-rules/voucher-checks`, `GET/PUT .../{id}`, `DELETE .../{id}` + `POST .../{id}/restore`, `POST .../reorder`), mirroring Documents' 6-endpoint pattern; `auth_roles` originally an embedded `List[str]`, delete-then-reinsert on save. Phase 3: a 5th Audit Rules rail entity, ordered by `sort_order` (not alphabetical) with Sortable.js drag-to-reorder POSTing live to the reorder endpoint. Phase 4: `GET /api/verification/voucher_checks` / `POST /api/verification/save_voucher_check` (upsert, no role-based access enforcement — `auth_roles` are informational only, matching the existing Audit Procedures checklist convention) — purely additive alongside the still-live `voucher_approvals` gate, cutover deferred to Phase 5. Phase 5: a persistent voucher-level checks bar (`#procedureVoucherChecksBar`) above the Supporting Documents modal's document rail; `compute_and_persist_cleared_status()`'s voucher-level gate cut over from `voucher_approvals` to "every active check ticked" in `voucher_check_status`; the old `GET/POST /api/verification/voucher_approval`/`save_voucher_approval` endpoints were **deleted** (the `voucher_approvals` table itself stays in the schema, unread/unwritten); the old Voucher Line tab's Prepared/Checked/Approved-By fields were removed. Phase 6: styling — indigo-tinted accent card, compact white pills, a shared custom tick-icon rule applied to both this bar and the per-document Audit Procedures checklist.

- **Voucher-level Checks simplified to name-only + 3-state model (new, confirmed 4-phase follow-up requirement, `routers/audit_rules.py`, `database.py`, `routers/verification.py`, `static/verification.js`/`.html`, `static/style.css`)**: Phase 1 — removed the Authorisation Roles field from Voucher-level Checks entirely (`VoucherCheckCreate`/`VoucherCheckUpdate` no longer accept `auth_roles`; `audit_rule_voucher_check_auth_roles` left in place, unread/unwritten). Phase 2 — `voucher_check_status` gained `state` (`'untouched'|'done'|'not_done'`, backfilled once from the old boolean `ticked`) and `flagged_in_observations` (written only by a new `POST /api/verification/verify_voucher_checks`, never by an ordinary tick); `GET/POST voucher_checks`/`save_voucher_check` now read/write `state` instead of `ticked`/`performed_by_name`; the new `verify_voucher_checks` endpoint 400s if any active check is still `untouched`, otherwise flags every `not_done` check and re-syncs the voucher's Observations. Phase 3 — the bar's checkboxes became tick/cross toggle-pill pairs; a warning line names any check currently `not_done`; a new voucher-scoped "✅ Verify & Next/Close" footer button (`.btn-verify`) replaced the old per-line Next button (← Back stays line-scoped, a locked scope decision). Phase 4 — a subsequent fix made "✅ Verify & Next" step through unverified lines (`cleared_status !== 'Cleared'` and a Category is assigned) within the same voucher before advancing to the next voucher, forward-only, never wrapping.

## Validation Rules Module (7 phases + Account Head recommendation + Category Cleared Requirements summary)

- **Full build, Phases 1-7 (`database.py`, `routers/audit_rules.py`, `routers/verification.py`, `static/audit_rules.html`/`.js`, `static/verification.js`/`.html`, `static/style.css`)**: adds a Cleared-vs-Query status engine per voucher line. Phase 1 schema: `approval_required` on `audit_rule_category_documents` (**since hard-removed, see the follow-up fix below**), `matrix_version` on `audit_rule_categories` (bumped whenever a Category's document/approval requirements change), `signature_specimens` (client_id+document_id+role_name → expected_signatory_name), `signature_exception` on `voucher_line_documents` (default OK, UI control since hidden — see Conventions note), `cleared_status`/`matrix_version_applied` on `verification_details`. Addendum: `voucher_approvals` (client_id+transaction_ref → prepared_by/checked_by/approved_by) — **since superseded and left dead by Generic Voucher-Level Checks Phase 5** (its endpoints deleted, table unread/unwritten). Phase 2 (Audit Rules backend): approval-toggle endpoint + `matrix_version` bump logic; Signature Specimens 5-endpoint CRUD. Phase 3 (Audit Rules frontend): approval checkboxes, matrix-version display, Signature Specimens as a standalone rail entity (later reworked, see "Signature Specimens Soft-Delete Conversion"). Phase 4 (Verification backend): `compute_and_persist_cleared_status(voucher_line_id)` — four AND'ed checks (later expanded, see below): required documents present (`get_category_documents()`), each `approval_required` document has an approver role ticked (**since removed**), `voucher_approvals` complete (**since replaced by the Generic Voucher-Level Checks gate**), no `signature_exception` flagged; called from `save_line_items()`. Phase 5 (Verification frontend): the Cleared/Query badge (`.voucher-line-cleared-badge-slot`, an independent sibling of the validation-status pill so `validateTransaction()`'s innerHTML rewrite can't wipe it), the Sig. Exc. checkbox (**UI since hidden**), the synthetic Voucher Line tab (**since replaced**, see Generic Voucher-Level Checks). Phase 6 (backend): `GET /api/verification/suggest-account-head` — fuzzy-matches (rapidfuzz `WRatio`) a line's description against the client's latest parsed Trial Balance leaf accounts, Category-alignment bonus, keyword-match reason, score band, top 2 results above `ACCOUNT_HEAD_MATCH_THRESHOLD=55`. Phase 7 (frontend): the Account Head Recommendation card in the Voucher Line tab (search-select over `latestTbAccountsCache`, "Use" button, no-match note via a reserved sentinel `document_id=-1` reusing the observation-sync machinery) — later repositioned above Voucher Approval with a TB search-select replacing free text (confirmed fix, same day).

- **Hard-remove Category "Approved" checkbox (confirmed requirement, `database.py`, `routers/audit_rules.py`, `static/audit_rules.js`, `routers/verification.py`)**: approval is now decided entirely at Document level via the "Approved by" role's Required Authority field (below), not per-Category — `audit_rule_category_documents.approval_required` was hard-removed via a full table rebuild (rename→recreate→copy→drop, same convention as the `comparison_type` CHECK-expansion), keeping only `is_required`. `compute_and_persist_cleared_status()`'s old approval-required check was stripped from `all_ok` entirely (no replacement landed yet at the time).

- **Document-level Approved-by authority gate (new, confirmed requirement, `routers/audit_rules.py` + `routers/verification.py`)**: the real replacement for the removed Category-level approval check — for every Category-required Document whose "Approved by"-type role has a Required Authority set, `compute_and_persist_cleared_status()` (check #6) now requires an ACTIVE Signature Specimen on file for that client+document+role whose `authority` matches (case/whitespace-insensitive). This is an **existence check** ("is a qualified signatory on file"), not a per-voucher recorded-signer match — no field anywhere records who actually signed a specific voucher's document, confirmed before designing.

- **Category "Cleared Requirements" summary (new, confirmed requirement, 3 phases, `routers/audit_rules.py` + `static/audit_rules.js` + `static/style.css`)**: read-only `GET /api/audit-rules/categories/{category_id}/cleared-requirements` reports, with no manual toggles, what a Category actually requires — `voucher_level_checks_required`/`account_head_required` always true (global gates), `cross_checks_required` true only if ≥1 active attached Cross-check, `required_documents` filtered to `is_required=1` — same data the real gate reads, not re-derived. Rendered as a "What Cleared Requires" plain-language bullet subsection at the top of each Category's "⚠️ Validation Rules" box.

## Automated Cross-Document Validation Engine (10 phases)

- **Full build, Phases 1-10 (`database.py`, `routers/audit_rules.py`, `routers/verification.py`, `static/audit_rules.html`/`.js`, `static/verification.js`, `static/style.css`)**: lets a Cross-check's configured document chain be evaluated against real linked evidence, not just displayed as guidance text. Phase 1 schema: `is_required` on `audit_rule_category_documents`; `comparison_type` CHECK expanded to 6 values (added `'Must be equal'`/`'May be less, never more'`); `compare_to_voucher_line` on `audit_rule_cross_checks`. Phase 2: `get_document_field_value(client_data_id, field_name)` (routers/verification.py) resolves a named field from linked evidence's `row_data`, validated against the Document's real template columns — dead code until Phase 6 wires it in. Phase 3: the Cross-checks "Field to Compare" dropdown now visibly flags (⚠, amber) a saved value that no longer matches any current option, instead of silently clearing it. Phase 4: a "Required" checkbox alongside the existing "Approved" checkbox on a Category's attached-Documents list, backed by `is_required`; `PUT .../categories/{id}/documents/{doc_id}/required`. Phase 5: 2 new comparison types wired into the config UI plus a "compare to voucher line amount" checkbox (anchor = the last document in chain order, resolved live, never manually picked). Phase 6: `evaluate_cross_checks_for_line(voucher_line_id, category_id)` — chain-aware evaluator: anchor = last **linked** document walked backwards; `May be less, never more` is directional (later ≤ earlier; strictly less = soft "shortfall", strictly more = hard "fail"); `Within tolerance %` uses a placeholder `CROSS_CHECK_DEFAULT_TOLERANCE_PCT=5.0` (no per-rule column exists yet); a Document with multiple linked evidence rows sums the field. Phase 7: wired into `compute_and_persist_cleared_status()` as check #5 — only a `"fail"` blocks Cleared, `"shortfall"`/`"not_evaluated"` do not. Phase 8: `_write_shortfall_observations()` auto-logs a shortfall as a reserved-sentinel observation (`CROSS_CHECK_SHORTFALL_DOC_ID_BASE = -1000` range, one sentinel per Cross-check) that self-clears once the shortfall resolves. Phase 9: `GET /api/verification/cross_check_results/{voucher_line_id}` exposes the evaluator read-only; the Supporting Documents modal's Data Table segment renders a per-document pass/fail/shortfall/not-evaluated rollup with click-to-expand chain detail. Phase 10/FINAL: a live document-chain preview on the Category detail screen — one row of connected pills per attached Cross-check, dimmed pill for a not-required document, "(anchor)" tag on the last pill.

- **"Field to Compare" dropdown / "Amount"→"Rate" — 2 confirmed data-only fixes (no code changes, `static/audit_rules.js` design already correct)**: the dropdown appeared stuck on "Add a document first" because none of the 7 active Documents actually had `cross_check_fields` configured (all prior test rows were soft-deleted) — fixed by setting real `cross_check_fields` (Quantity/Amount, later also Rate) on the 5 template-linked Documents via the existing API, plus a small empty-state message fix distinguishing "no documents added" from "no field common to all selected documents". A follow-up rename request ("Amount"→"Rate") was investigated and **deferred** — none of the 3 templates has a real "Rate" column at the time (Rate as a derived value came later via the Rate-Derivation Requirement).

## Physical Bill Evidence Type (8 phases)

- **Full build, Phases 1-8 (`database.py`, `routers/audit_rules.py`, `routers/verification.py`, `static/audit_rules.html`/`.js`, `static/verification.js`/`.html`, `static/style.css`)**: lets a Category require a manually-keyed "Physical Bill" (Bill No/Date/Amount/Vendor name) instead of a Data Bank template-linked Document. Phase 1 schema: `evidence_type` on `audit_rule_categories` (`'billable'`/`'non_billable'`, nullable with no default — every existing Category needs manual classification before the gate activates), `document_type` on `audit_rule_documents` (`'linked_template'`/`'physical_bill'`, defaulted `'linked_template'` on the ALTER), `voucher_line_physical_bills` (`voucher_line_id`+`document_id` → `bill_no`/`bill_date`/`amount`/`vendor_name`, `UNIQUE(voucher_line_id, document_id)` — carries `document_id` since a Billable Category can attach more than one Physical Bill Document). Phase 2: Documents CRUD supports `document_type`, defaulting to `linked_template` when omitted (a stricter reject was considered and rejected, since the frontend didn't send the field until Phase 4); `apply_document_type_constraints()` forces a `physical_bill`'s `template_id`/`cross_check_fields` empty but leaves `auth_roles` alone (load-bearing at the time — a template-less Document was still satisfied via role ticks until Phase 6 intercepted it). Phase 3: Categories CRUD requires `evidence_type` on both create **and** update (a validator, not a resolver — the strictness asymmetry with Phase 2 is deliberate, since this field drives the gate). Phase 4: Audit Rules frontend pickers for both fields, forced choice with no default, a native `confirm()` guard when switching an existing Document away from `linked_template`. Phase 5: `POST /api/verification/save_physical_bill` (upsert) / `GET .../physical_bills/{voucher_line_id}` (sibling-session-resolved batch read) — plain CRUD, no matching logic yet. Phase 6: wired into `compute_and_persist_cleared_status()`'s check #1 — intercepts `document_type == 'physical_bill'` **before** the template/no-template branches (closing the exact trap Phase 2/3 flagged); `_physical_bill_satisfied()` requires Bill No/Date/Vendor non-blank AND Amount exactly matching `client_data.extract_amount` (epsilon 0.005) — any one gap fails the whole document. Phase 7: the Supporting Documents modal's Physical Bill tab — a dedicated 4-field form (no Audit Procedures segment, since roles no longer gate this doc type), live green ✓ tick beside Amount on an exact match. Phase 8/FINAL: confirmed the reason-popover/Validate-panel's existing generic gate-detail rendering already covers physical-bill outstanding text with no code change needed. **Real blocker found and fixed along the way**: `client_data.extract_amount` was NULL on every real row (see "Rate-Derivation Requirement" for the root cause/fix/backfill) — until that fix, this entire gate was untestable against real data.

- **"Populate Physical Bill from GRN/ERP Vendor Bill" — see the dedicated heading below** (a separate, later 4-phase requirement building on this one).

## Signature Specimens Soft-Delete Conversion (4 phases)

- **Full build, Phases 1-4 (`database.py`, `routers/audit_rules.py`, `static/audit_rules.html`/`.js`)**: converts hard-delete to soft-delete for a Document's signatory records. Phase 1: `signature_specimens` gained `is_active INTEGER DEFAULT 1`; `DELETE .../{id}` now soft-deletes (404 if already inactive), `POST .../{id}/restore` added, plus a separate low-visibility `DELETE .../{id}/hard-delete` for genuine data-entry corrections. Phase 2: the old table-level `UNIQUE(client_id, document_id, role_name)` (which blocked reusing a deactivated slot) was removed via a schema-driven rebuild, replaced by `validate_no_duplicate_active_signatory()` — blocks only a literal duplicate ACTIVE entry for the *same person* (case-insensitive name match); multiple different people can be concurrently active for the same role. Phase 3: confirmed no-op — Verification's signature check (`signature_exception`) is a manual auditor toggle, never queries `signature_specimens` at all. Phase 4/FINAL: moved out of its own standalone rail entity into each Document's own detail view — a per-Role grouped person list with Deactivate/Reactivate + a separate low-visibility hard-delete link; inactive people stay visible, greyed/struck-through, never hidden (a historical record).

- **Authority field on Signature Specimens (new, confirmed requirement, `database.py` + `routers/audit_rules.py` + `static/audit_rules.js` + `static/style.css`)**: `signature_specimens` gained a nullable `authority TEXT`, unconditional on every specimen — the field the Document-level Approved-by authority gate (Validation Rules Module) matches against.

## ID-based Cross-check-eligible Fields (4 phases)

Phase 1: `audit_rule_document_fields` gained a nullable `master_column_id INTEGER`, best-effort backfilled by name-matching each field against its Document's template's mapped columns; `resolve_field_name_to_master_column_id()` (routers/audit_rules.py) also resolves on every future save. Phase 2: the free-text chip input on the Documents detail form became a `<select>` scoped to the Document's linked template's real columns, with an amber-flagged chip for any entry that wouldn't resolve. Phase 3: narrowed a reported "stays empty" bug to a real but different gap — a Document with zero configured fields showed the generic "no common field" message instead of naming the actual cause; fixed the message only. Phase 4/FINAL: `GET /api/columns/{column_id}/usage` — a read-only rename/edit dependency preview (`documents_count`/`cross_checks_count`/`templates_count`) shown in the Add/Edit Column modal.

Phase 1: `get_category_guidance_documents()`/`get_category_guidance_cross_checks()` (feed Verification's live procedure-modal tabs) gained `is_active` filters — the one real gap found. Phase 2: confirmed no-op — Audit Rules' own Category-builder pickers already defaulted `include_inactive=false`. Phase 3: the Supporting Documents modal now synthesizes a locked, dimmed tab (`__inactive: true`) for a Document that already has linked evidence/ticks/an observation but was since deactivated — frozen/read-only, never gates completion, evidence stays unassignable but existing links stay visible and unassign still works. Phase 4: `get_category_for_account()` (Verification's Type auto-fill) and the Trial Balance smart-fill cascade both stopped over-filtering an inactive-but-assigned Category out of a read-only display; the Assign Categories dropdown gained a synthetic "(inactive)" option so a frozen assignment doesn't silently show "-- Not assigned --". Phase 5/FINAL: `compute_and_persist_cleared_status()`'s check #1 (`required_doc_ids`) and the Document-level Approved-by authority gate's document lookup both gained `is_active` filters — without these, a Document deactivated after being attached-but-never-linked could permanently block Cleared with no way to ever satisfy it.

Phase 1 (relocation only): pure move via a scripted line-range extraction (byte-for-byte fidelity, verified via `node --check` + a top-level-identifier collision scan), zero behavior change — `verification.js` shrank 7373→3947 lines. Phase 1b (adapter refactor): replaced bare shared-global-scope reliance (~20 identifiers) with an explicit `hostAdapter` object passed into `openProcedureModal(uid, initialDocId, adapter)`; functions are plain property refs, live/reassignable state (`currentVoucherId`, `voucherLineState`, etc.) are `get` accessor properties so the adapter's view stays live rather than a stale snapshot; `verification.js` gained `buildProcedureModalAdapter()`, called at its 4 real `openProcedureModal()` sites. Phase 2 (Audit Workbook wiring): `static/audit_workbook.js` built its own lean `buildAuditWorkbookAdapter(voucherGroup)` — a direct-to-backend equivalent of `saveLineItems()`, not a reuse of Verification's — required `GET .../audit_workbook` to additionally surface each line's resolved Category *name* and the session's `client_id` (both genuinely needed by the modal, purely additive to the endpoint).
