## Verification Prev/Next Processing UI

**Requirement (2026-08-27, Phase 2 of the same 6-phase Verification nav/UX set whose Phase 1 is
written up under "Verification Nav Skeleton Recovery" above):** the loading UI covered only the
last, fastest step of a voucher navigation, leaving roughly three seconds of total silence during
the save phase, and both Prev/Next buttons stayed clickable throughout so a second click stacked
another full navigation on top of the first.

**Where the silence actually was** (traced, not assumed): `goToPreviousTransaction()` /
`goToNextTransaction()` run `saveCurrentTransaction()` → `saveAllVoucherLines()` → **one sequential
`save_line_items` POST per voucher line**, each preceded by `flushProcedureObservations()` and
`flushAccountHeadNoMatchNote()`. On Next there is then `validateTransaction()` (another save plus a
`validate` POST), and on the passed branch `completeTransaction()` (a third save, another validate,
a `complete` POST). Only the final step — `moveToAdjacentVoucher()`, or `loadNextTransaction()`
inside `completeTransaction()` — painted anything. Hence: click, ~3s of nothing, a brief skeleton
flash, new voucher.

**Button state — two independent conditions ANDed, not two competing writes.** Per the user's
explicit instruction at plan time. `getVoucherNavAllowed()` holds the position half of the rule
(extracted out of `renderVoucherHeader()` so there is one definition of "there is a voucher that
way"); `applyVoucherNavButtonState()` sets `disabled = voucherNavInFlight || !allowed`, and
`renderVoucherHeader()` computes its inline `disabled` attribute from the same two ANDed terms. Had
these been two writers each setting `disabled` at different moments, whichever finished last would
win — so a settling fetch could leave a button live that position says must stay dead. ANDing
removes the race by construction instead of by carefully ordering the writes.

This matters concretely, not theoretically: on the passed branch `completeTransaction()` →
`loadNextTransaction()` re-renders the header **while the navigation is still running**. Without the
AND in `renderVoucherHeader()`, that mid-flight render would re-enable both buttons.

**One guarded entry point.** `runGuardedVoucherNav(message, fn)` wraps the entire save → validate →
fetch → render sequence: it drops the call outright if a navigation is already in flight (the
stacked-call guard, same reasoning as `saveLineItems()`'s `inFlightLineSaves` map one level down),
sets the flag, applies the button state, shows the badge, and restores everything in a `finally`.
Each nav function keeps its existing position early-return *before* the wrapper, so an
at-the-boundary click still no-ops without flashing the buttons off and on for nothing.

**Re-enable audit** (requested explicitly, since a stuck-disabled button would be the same failure
family as Phase 1's stuck skeleton): every exit restores the buttons through that one `finally` —
success (header re-rendered mid-flight, corrected after), boundary (Phase 1 re-renders lines only,
never the header), the error block (Phase 1 replaces the table only, never the header), a cancelled
confirm dialog, and any thrown error. The audit found one real hole: Phase 1's **Try again** button
calls `moveToAdjacentVoucher()` directly, bypassing `goToNextTransaction()`, so a retry would have
run with both nav buttons live. It now goes through the same wrapper.
`verifyAndAdvanceVoucher()` (procedure modal) and `navigateToTransaction()` (popover) are untouched
and unaffected — they render with the flag false.

**Indicator: the existing voucher loading badge**, not a new primitive — the spinner + message pill
beside the voucher title (`showVoucherLoadingBadge()`), already visually proven by
`renderVoucherLines()`'s own per-line batch. It is ref-counted and shared, which creates a real
cross-voucher hazard: on the complete-and-advance path `renderVoucherHeader()` resets the count to 0
and `renderVoucherLines()` starts the **new** voucher's badge, so a naive hide in the `finally`
would decrement that one instead of ours. Closed with the file's own existing marker for exactly
this problem — capture `voucherLoadToken` at show time and skip the hide if it has since moved on,
mirroring the `myLoadToken` guard in `renderVoucherLines()`. The badge is also lowered around
`showNavigationConfirm()` and raised again after, so a spinner never claims work is in progress
while the dialog is actually waiting on the user; the buttons stay disabled throughout.

The table skeleton stays exactly where Phase 1 left it. During the save the table keeps showing real
data — it is the current voucher's own data and still valid — and is only replaced once a genuinely
different voucher is being fetched.

**No `style.css` change.** `.btn-voucher-nav:disabled` already styles the greyed state, so the
project's all-18-pages stylesheet bump is not owed.

**Tests:** 4 cases added to `tests/test_verification_nav_skeleton.py` (9 total), driving the real
`goToNextTransaction()` rather than `moveToAdjacentVoucher()` directly, over a seeded two-voucher
session with `cleared_status: 'Cleared'` so `isCurrentVoucherValidated()` skips the confirm dialog.
The mid-flight assertion needs **no sleeps or delayed responses**: JS is single-threaded and
`runGuardedVoucherNav()` disables the buttons and shows the badge synchronously before its first
`await`, so the navigation is kicked off and the button state read in the same `page.evaluate()` —
deterministic, and exactly the state a user sees the instant their click returns.

**Verified:** 9 passed here (Phase 1's 5 included, no regression); full suite 11 passed plus the 2
known unrelated Postgres-cutover failures already logged in `KNOWN_ISSUES.md`. Against the
pre-Phase-2 file the two behavioural cases fail with the right complaint (`assert 2 == 1` — a second
overlapping navigation issued its own request); the two stuck-disabled cases pass pre-fix by
construction, since nothing disabled the buttons before this phase — they are forward-looking
regression guards, stated plainly rather than overclaimed. Mid-save state screenshotted through the
same harness (both buttons greyed, "Saving your work…" spinner beside the voucher title) by hanging
`saveCurrentTransaction()` from inside the page so the state held still.
`verification.js?v=13` → `?v=14` (verification.html) in the same commit.

**Noted, not touched:** `isNavigating` (verification.js) is written by `loadNextTransaction()` and
read by nothing — dead state predating this work. The new flag is deliberately named
`voucherNavInFlight` to avoid confusion with it.

## Verification Hub Tile Spinner + Click-Lock

**Requirement (2026-08-27, Phase 3 of the Verification nav/UX set):** the hub's Cash vouchers tile
gave no feedback and stayed clickable while the page reloaded into the cashbook popup, so it could
be double-clicked — each extra click restarting the reload and lengthening the wait. Deliberately a
band-aid: visible feedback plus a click-lock. The root cause (the slow `current-client` call on page
load) stays deferred to its own project.

**Read-time finding that reshaped the phase — there are two silent gaps, not one:**

| Gap | Where | Why it was invisible |
|---|---|---|
| A — leaving | click → browser fetches the new page | old DOM stays on screen, tile looks idle |
| B — arriving | new page parsed, popup not yet open | `#dashboardContent` is visible by default, so the tiles render **live and clickable again** while `window.onload` sits on `await window.clientContextReady` |

Gap B is where the double-click race actually bites, and the brief had only anticipated Gap A. The
click handler was confirmed to be a plain `window.location.href` assignment (a real full reload,
matching the earlier investigation), so the two gaps are separated by a genuine document swap.

**Scope widened once, with the user's explicit approval:** from "the Cash tile" to *every* live tile
on this page, current and future. That turned two hardcoded handlers into one data-driven
mechanism — `data-verification-type` on the tile (see the Conventions entry in `CLAUDE.md`) plus a
single delegated listener on `#dashboardContent`. A future tile becomes live, with the same spinner
and lock, by adding the attribute alone; a "Coming soon" tile omits it and `closest()` returns null,
leaving it exactly as inert as before.

**Why the lock is a JS flag, not `disabled`:** a `.module-card` is a `<div>`, so `showSpinner`'s
`isButton` test (`target.disabled !== undefined`) is false and it never sets `disabled` — there is no
native disabled state to use. `hubTileNavigationInFlight` **is** the lock. This is also why no
`style.css` change was owed, and the all-18-pages stylesheet bump was avoided.

**The stuck-spinner trap, found by reading rather than by testing:** `setVerificationUrl()` writes
`state` and `type` **together**, so a hard-refresh URL like `?state=session&id=5&type=cash` carries a
`type` but takes the restore branch and never opens the popup. A naive "is `?type=` present" check
for the arrival lock would have stranded a spinner on the hub permanently there. The arrival lock is
therefore gated on the *identical* condition `window.onload` uses to decide it will open the popup.

**Three release paths, no guessed durations:**

| Path | Covers |
|---|---|
| `finally` around the popup-open region in `window.onload` | normal open, the early-return restore branch, and any throw in between |
| `pageshow` when `event.persisted` | bfcache Back-restore, which brings the page back spinner and flag intact |
| `keydown` Escape | the user pressing Stop mid-navigation — the one remaining case where the old document survives with a locked tile |

Escape was chosen over a safety timeout (which the plan had explicitly ruled out) because it is the
browser's actual Stop-loading gesture: a fixed timeout would also fire during a load that is merely
slow but still perfectly on its way, which is the exact situation this feature exists to support.
Escape while nothing is locked is a no-op, so it cannot interfere with the popup's own handling.

**Wording is shared between both sides** (`hubTileOpeningMessage()`): the click happens before the
reload and the arrival lock after it, so using one message across the document swap makes the reload
read as a single continuous wait instead of two different ones.

**Verified** (Playwright against the running dev server, 17 checks green). Gap A had to be proven
*synchronously* — three earlier attempts to hold the navigation all silently measured the arriving
page instead of the old one (a glob route that doesn't match a query string; `time.sleep` inside a
sync route handler, which blocks Playwright's own driver; and an async hold Chrome had already
committed past). Since assigning `location.href` never commits synchronously, dispatching the click
and reading the tile in the **same JS turn** is deterministic and race-free: guard `false → true`,
spinner in place of the content, repeat clicks swallowed, the bank tile refused, all while
`location.href` is still the original URL. Gap B was verified end-to-end against a genuinely delayed
`/api/auth/current-client`: spinning at first paint, clicks swallowed (0 navigations), released the
moment the popup appears. Also confirmed: the `?state=` restore URL strands no spinner, Escape both
clears the lock and restores the tile's original content, and "Coming soon" tiles stay inert.
`pytest` — same 2 pre-existing Postgres-cutover failures already logged in `KNOWN_ISSUES.md`.
`verification.js?v=14` → `?v=15` (verification.html) in the same commit.

## Verification Cache-Hit DB Round-Trip Fix (F3a)

**Requirement (2026-08-27, Phase 4 of the Verification nav/UX set):** close the gap found in
`INVESTIGATION_VERIFICATION_UX.md` finding **F3a** — a cache "hit" for the category/account-type
lookup still cost a full database round-trip, because the client-existence check ran *before* the
cache was consulted. On this Render↔Supabase deployment every DB call pays a large cross-region
latency floor, so a "hit" was recovering almost none of what the cache was built to save.

**Scope was strictly F3a.** The deferred sibling finding F3b — `invalidate_audit_rules_cache()`'s
blanket `_audit_rules_cache.clear()` also wiping the per-client `category_for_account:*` keys on any
Audit Rules write — was explicitly left as-is for a later phase. Smarter per-category invalidation
is not part of this.

**The one change, in `routers/verification.py` `get_category_for_account()`:** the cache lookup
block (`category_for_account_cache_key()` → `cache_get()` → early return) now runs as the first
thing in the function body, ahead of the `SELECT id FROM clients WHERE id = %s AND is_active = TRUE`
existence check. On a cache hit the function returns with zero DB calls. On a cache **miss** the
existence check still runs exactly as before (so a bad `client_id` on a cold cache still 404s), then
the unchanged latest-TB / `account_category_assignments` fallback path. Skipping the existence check
on a hit is safe: a cached entry can only have been written by an earlier call that already passed
it, and the 10-min TTL plus `invalidate_category_for_account_cache()` hooks (TB upload, category
assignment — `routers/trial_balance.py`) bound staleness. The docstring's "Read-side cache wiring"
paragraph was updated to state this.

**Not touched:** `get_audit_guidance()` (same file) was reviewed and already consults `cache_get()`




as its first statement — no gap. Every cached GET endpoint in `routers/audit_rules.py`
(`get_documents`/`get_document`/`get_category`/`get_cross_checks`/`get_cross_check`/
`get_category_cleared_requirements`) was reviewed and already checks the cache before any DB call —
no change needed on the Audit Rules side. So this phase touched one file, one function.

**Verified:** `pytest tests/ -v` — 11 passed, same 2 pre-existing Postgres-cutover failures already
logged in `KNOWN_ISSUES.md` (confirmed identical on the stashed, unmodified tree). Live-confirmed
against the deployed Render app (`two-python-app.onrender.com`) by `curl`-timing repeated
`GET /api/verification/category-for-account` calls: first lookup of a code (cache miss) ~1.0–1.3s,
every repeat (cache hit) ~0.21–0.26s — i.e. the hit now returns at pure network-RTT with the DB
skipped, ~0.8–1.0s saved per hit, consistent across several distinct codes. Regression check:
`client_id=999999` still returns `404 "Client not found or inactive"`, so the existence check still
runs on a miss.

**2026-08-27 — Phase 6 of the Verification nav/UX requirement, FINAL. Cold-start client-guard
eviction bug. `static/client_context.js` + `static/client_select.js` (frontend only, no backend).**

**Symptom.** On a cold Render instance, clicking the hub's Cash Vouchers tile (→
`verification.html?type=cash`) could throw *"Please select a client from the Dashboard first"* and
bounce the user to `index.html` even when a client was genuinely selected.

**Root cause (confirmed, not assumed).** `loadSessionClient()` had a single `catch` that handled
*every* failure of `GET /api/auth/current-client` — network error, timeout, 5xx (all common while a
cold instance spins up) — identically to a valid "no client selected" response: it nulled
`sessionClientCache` and returned `true` ("session valid, proceed"). `initClientContext()` then
rendered, `renderClientControl()` called `enforceClientSelection()`, `isClientSelected()` was
`false`, so it `alert()`ed and redirected. A real selected client was silently discarded.

**Fix — three parts:**

1. **Retry + transient-failure flag (`loadSessionClient()`).** The fetch now runs in a 2-attempt
   loop: on the first attempt failing (network error **or** `!res.ok`) it waits ~1500 ms and tries
   once more (a cold instance is usually serving by then). A `401` is never retried — the server
   responded, the session is genuinely invalid, redirect to `login.html` as before. If *both*
   attempts fail, the new module-level `sessionClientLoadFailed` flag is set, the cache is nulled,
   and it still returns `true` (the caller must render something).

2. **Guard distinguishes the two cases (`enforceClientSelection()`).** On a client-scoped page with
   no client: if `sessionClientLoadFailed`, it shows *"Couldn't reach the server to load your
   selected client. This can happen on the first request after a period of inactivity — please
   reload the page."* and does **not** redirect (the client may well be selected; a reload succeeds
   once warm). Otherwise — genuinely no client — the message is corrected to *"Please select a
   client from the Client Cards page first."* (was "from the Dashboard") and the redirect goes to
   `client_select.html` (was `index.html` — the dashboard can't fix a missing client) with a
   `?next=` stamp.

3. **Intent preserved via `?next=` (reuses the Client Settings pattern).** New `getEvictionNextKey()`
   in `client_context.js` — a whitelist lookup, never param concatenation — maps
   `verification.html?type=cash`/`bank` to the keys `verification_cash`/`verification_bank`.
   `client_select.js`'s `NEXT_DESTINATIONS` gains those two entries, each with a new optional
   `extra: 'type=cash'` fragment that `resolveNextUrl()` appends after `client_id`/`from`. After the
   user picks a client they land on `verification.html?client_id=<id>&from=dashboard&type=cash` with
   Cash mode active. `verification.html` isn't in `URL_CLIENT_SCOPED_PAGES`, so it ignores
   `client_id`/`from` and reads its client from the now-populated session — `type=` is the fragment
   that matters. The existing `client_settings` entry has no `extra`, so its output is byte-identical.

`static/verification.js` needed no change — the Cash/Bank choice is already in the URL, which
`client_context.js` reads directly.

**Cache-bust:** `client_context.js?v=13→14` (17 pages), `client_select.js?v=2→3` (client_select.html).

**Verification.** Backend `pytest tests/ -q`: 11 passed, 2 failed — both failures
(`test_clients_api_responds_on_fresh_db`, `test_counts_existing_and_new_rows`) pre-exist on a clean
`git stash`ed tree; this phase touched no Python. UI paths (happy path, genuine eviction landing on
`?next=verification_cash`, transient-failure via a blocked `/api/auth/current-client` showing the
reload prompt with no redirect) verified by the user.

**Residual (out of scope, noted):** on a transient failure the page body still renders its own
"no client" state (verification.js reads `getSelectedClientId()` → null); the alert directs a reload
which resolves it. A session expiring mid-flow still routes through `login.html`, which doesn't
carry `?next=` forward (pre-existing, `KNOWN_ISSUES.md`).

## Verification Bulk Tick Persistence — Phase 4A

**Date:** 2026-08-28 | **Files:** `routers/verification.py`, `static/procedure_modal.js`.

**Why:** Live Network logs showed the two bulk tick controls issuing one request per item: three
Audit Procedure role saves and eight voucher-level check saves, each paying the same multi-second
database wait. Optimistic rendering and repeated cache invalidation made the selected ticks appear
to disappear intermittently while those requests were still completing.

**Backend:** Added `POST /api/verification/save_voucher_checks_batch` and
`POST /api/verification/procedure_checks_batch`. Each validates the complete submitted list inside
one `pg_transaction()` context and upserts every item before committing. Any invalid check, line,
document, or role raises before commit, so the batch rolls back as one unit. Existing individual
endpoints remain available for single-tick interactions and backwards compatibility.

**Frontend:** The voucher-level Mark All button now submits one batch request containing the changed
check IDs and target states. The Audit Procedures Mark All button now submits one batch request
containing the changed line/document/role records. Existing optimistic update, single spinner,
success refresh, failure revert, cache invalidation, and dirty-line behavior remain intact.

**Verified:** `py_compile` passed; focused verification tests passed (13); the full test suite passed
(31). The live Network capture showed the prior per-item requests and confirmed the performance
motivation; user testing of the new batch routes remains the final functional check. The full
voucher-wide atomic Save + Verify operation remains Phase 4B and is not included here.

## Phase 1 - durable Rulebook version and explicit session recovery

**Date:** 2026-08-31 | **Files:** `database.py`, `routers/audit_rules.py`, `routers/verification.py`,
`static/verification.js`, `tests/test_audit_rulebook.py`.

The Rulebook configuration version is now durable in both SQLite and Postgres through a dedicated
singleton state record. Audit Rules invalidation advances that stored version and synchronizes the
existing process caches, so a server restart no longer resets the version and falsely invalidates
resumable sessions.

returns structured recovery information and provides an authenticated explicit rebase action. Rebase
updates only the session's captured Rulebook version; verification details, evidence, observations,

and retries the Rulebook load only after the user accepts.

existing non-blocking warnings remain. No Git action was performed until this approved closeout.

## Data Table Cross-check Empty State Redesign

**Date:** 2026-09-02 | **Files:** `routers/verification.py` (Phase 1, read-only investigation, no
change), `static/procedure_modal.js`, `static/style.css`, `static/verification.html`,
`static/audit_workbook.html` (Phase 2).

Replaced the Data Table segment's single generic "`<field>` not enough data" text for a
`not_evaluated` Cross-check rule with a design that distinguishes two different causes:

- **"documents not linked yet"** — the Cross-check is fully configured; this voucher line simply
  hasn't linked enough evidence.
- **"check not configured"** — the Cross-check can never produce a result no matter what gets
  linked (fewer than 2 configured Documents and no voucher-line comparison enabled) — an Audit
  Rules setup gap, not a Verification to-do.

Phase 1 traced `GET /api/verification/cross_check_results/{voucher_line_id}` →
`evaluate_cross_checks_for_line()` → `_evaluate_single_cross_check()` and confirmed the response
already carries everything needed client-side: each rule's `chain[]` has one entry per configured
Document (with `linked`/`document_name`), plus `compare_to_voucher_line`. No backend change was
needed.

Phase 2 added `isCrossCheckRuleUnconfigured(rule)` (`chain.length === 0`, or `chain.length < 2`
with no voucher-line comparison) and used it to branch both the collapsed badge
(`summarizeCrossCheckRule()`) and a new expanded-detail renderer,
`buildCrossCheckEmptyStateDetail()` (delegated to from `buildCrossCheckRuleDetail()` only for
`not_evaluated` — pass/fail/shortfall keep the original raw chain-list rendering unchanged). The
new detail renders a chip row (one ✓/✕ circle per configured Document, reusing the existing
`.procedure-voucher-check-btn` tick/cross visual — green filled = linked, muted grey outline = not
linked — plus a "Voucher Line Amount" chip when `compare_to_voucher_line` is set), a plain-English
explainer sentence that differs by cause, a static `ℹ️` info-icon tooltip (`title` attribute only,
no popover, same convention as `templates.js`'s column-notes icon) with fixed generic copy, and a
footnote that reuses the engine's own already-computed `rule.message` verbatim. The now-unreachable
`.cc-rule-message-not_evaluated` CSS rule was removed.

A reachability finding surfaced during design: `docCrossChecks` filters rules to
`chain.some(c => c.document_id === docId)`, so a rule with a fully empty chain can never render
under any Document tab — the literal `chain.length === 0` condition is dead code today. The
practically-reachable "check not configured" case is a chain of exactly one Document (the open
tab's own) with no voucher-line comparison, which the engine's own `len(comparable) >= 2 or
compare_to_voucher_line` rule means can never evaluate regardless of linking. `isCrossCheckRuleUnconfigured()`
covers both conditions (a strict superset), so the design is demonstrable today without contradicting
the narrower rule confirmed in Phase 1.

Also fixed, discovered while bumping this file's cache-bust version: `verification.html` and
`audit_workbook.html` had drifted to different `procedure_modal.js?v=` numbers (15 vs 14) — both
now share `?v=16`. `style.css?v=` bumped 12→13 on all 18 pages per the existing convention.

**Verified:** full backend suite passed (88 passed, unaffected — no backend change). No login
credentials were available for this live Supabase-backed dev server, and this app holds real
client audit data, so rather than a live logged-in walkthrough, verification used a Playwright
harness (`page.evaluate()`) loading the live server's actual `procedure_modal.js`/`style.css` and
invoking `summarizeCrossCheckRule()`/`buildCrossCheckRuleDetail()`/`buildCrossCheckRollup()`
directly against hand-built `rule` objects covering: two Documents (one linked, one not), a single
linked Document with no voucher-line comparison, a single unlinked Document with voucher-line
comparison enabled, and an unrelated `fail`-status rule. Confirmed via computed styles/bounding
rects and a screenshot: correct chip states, correct branch selection in all four cases, identical
(static) tooltip text across rules, and the `fail` rule still rendering through the untouched old
chain-list path with no `.cc-empty-state` bleed-through. Live in-app confirmation with a real
voucher line is still recommended before considering this fully done end-to-end.

## Cross-check Shortfall Note-Save Invalid Placeholder ID Fix

**Date:** 2026-09-02 | **Files:** `database.py`, `routers/verification.py`,
`routers/audit_rules.py`, `tests/test_verification_atomic_save_verify.py`.

**Symptom:** "Verify & Next Line" on voucher CPV-0826-180 (session 891) returned HTTP 500 from
`POST /api/verification/save_and_verify_voucher_bundle`, reproducibly, 3 times. The browser-side
error body carried no useful detail (a generic 500 JSON), and the app's own `error_log` table
(read read-only to diagnose, no live data touched) showed only a downstream Postgres cascade
message — "current transaction is aborted, commands ignored until end of transaction block" —
truncated before the real originating statement (`log_error()` caps `stack_trace` at 5000 chars).

**Root cause:** `_write_shortfall_observations()` wrote a bookkeeping row into
`voucher_line_observations` for every active Cross-check result, using a synthetic negative
`document_id` (`CROSS_CHECK_SHORTFALL_DOC_ID_BASE - cross_check_id`) that was never a real row in
`audit_rule_documents`. This was harmless on SQLite (`PRAGMA foreign_keys` is never enabled here —
already a documented app-wide gotcha) but `voucher_line_observations.document_id` has a real `REFERENCES
audit_rule_documents(id)` FK on the live Postgres database, so the INSERT was rejected outright.
The function's own `try/except` swallowed that error locally (printed a warning, never reached
`error_log`) but could not undo Postgres's resulting aborted-transaction state — and because the
whole 5-line Save-and-Verify bundle runs in one shared transaction (a deliberate Rulebook-era speed
optimization), every later statement in the same request then failed with the generic cascade,
which is what actually reached the browser as a 500. The code path had been dormant since it was
written (no Category had a real active Cross-check before the cross-check matrix redesign);
Category "Material Purchased" — this voucher's own category — got its first one ("Purchase demand
vs Purchase order", `cross_check_id=31`) on 2026-09-01, so this was the first live trigger.

Confirmed via safe, read-only checks throughout (a live Supabase-backed dev server; no test data
created, no writes made during diagnosis): the real Postgres error message, the resolved category
and its attached Cross-check, and the confirmed absence of any negative-id row in
`audit_rule_documents`.

**Fix (approved approach — lazy get-or-create, not a pre-seeded block):** two additive schema
columns — `audit_rule_documents.is_system` (marks a row as a hidden system placeholder) and
`audit_rule_cross_checks.shortfall_document_id` (caches the one real Document row created for that
Cross-check, `NULL` until first needed). `_get_or_create_cross_check_shortfall_document_id()`
(replacing `_cross_check_shortfall_sentinel_doc_id()`) reads the cached id, or creates one real
`is_system=TRUE, is_active=FALSE` Document row on first use and remembers it — safe for multiple
simultaneous Cross-checks on one category, no guessed reserved ID range. The two label-detection
call sites that used to test the old fixed numeric range (`sync_line_observations_to_voucher()`,
`sync_voucher_observations_to_voucher()`) now check the same `is_system` flag instead.
`get_documents()` (routers/audit_rules.py) excludes `is_system` rows unconditionally (even with
`include_inactive=True`) so the placeholder never appears in the Documents tab.
`ACCOUNT_HEAD_OBSERVATION_DOC_ID` (a separate, still-nonexistent sentinel) is untouched — out of
scope for this fix.

**Verified:** full backend suite passed (89/89, including one new test —
`test_cross_check_shortfall_document_id_created_once_and_reused`, confirming create-once/reuse
behavior). The dev server's own file-watcher auto-reloaded on the `.py` edits; the two new
Postgres columns hadn't actually applied yet at that point, so the app's own idempotent
`init_db_postgres()` was run once directly (safe, additive-only) and re-confirmed read-only:
correct column types/defaults, zero existing rows affected (20 documents, 4 active Cross-checks
unchanged). Live confirmation: Aadil re-ran "Verify & Next Line" on the same voucher (new session
892) — read-only re-check afterward showed zero new errors logged, `cross_check_id=31` now has a
real `shortfall_document_id` pointing at a genuine hidden Document row, and all 5 of the voucher's
lines now have a persisted `cleared_status` (`Query`) instead of being permanently stuck.

## Postgres Pool Stale-Connection Retry

**Date:** 2026-09-02 | **Files:** `database.py`, new `tests/test_pg_pool_retry.py`.
Phase 1 of a two-phase brief; Phase 2 (`PG_POOL_MIN` warm-start) is the next section.

**Problem.** `database.py`'s psycopg2 `ThreadedConnectionPool` never checked whether a
connection it handed back was still alive. On this low-traffic free-tier Supabase (Mumbai),
a pooled connection dropped server-side while idle was handed straight out and the first
statement on it raised — 13 real HTTP 500s across 8 endpoints between 2026-08-25 and
2026-09-02 (dashboard/kpi-stats ×4, auth/login ×2, verification presence/heartbeat ×2,
audit-rules/documents, data/availability, verification latest_cashbook_date /
preview_cashbook / start_session — one each; `KNOWN_ISSUES.md`). A connection that broke
mid-request could also be rolled back into the pool and re-served, spreading the failure.

**Confirmed before building** (read-only): all three pool-borrow chokepoints
(`_PooledConnection` backing `get_db_pg()`, `pg_transaction()`,
`get_raw_conn_pg()`/`release_raw_conn_pg()`) borrowed and used blindly — nothing caught
`psycopg2.InterfaceError`/`OperationalError` anywhere in the pooling layer. `execute_batch_pg`
/ `execute_batch_insert_with_ids_pg` receive an already-borrowed `conn`, so fixing the borrow
points covers them. `_PooledConnection`/`get_db_pg()`/`_ExistingConnection` had exactly two
callers — `execute_query_pg`/`execute_write_pg`.

**Approach** (both decisions confirmed with Aadil):

- `_is_stale_pg_connection_error(exc)` — `True` only for a `psycopg2.InterfaceError` /
  `OperationalError` whose lowercased message contains a known stale marker
  (`_STALE_PG_CONNECTION_MARKERS`: "server closed the connection unexpectedly",
  "connection already closed", "could not connect", "terminating connection due to
  administrator command", SSL-drop, "eof detected", …). Type check first because
  `OperationalError` also covers deadlock / "too many clients" / disk-full, which a blind
  retry must not paper over — those propagate untouched, as does any non-psycopg2 error.
- `_run_pooled_pg(operation)` — the retry-once layer, replacing `_PooledConnection` et al.
  Borrows, runs `operation(conn)`; on a stale failure discards the connection with
  `putconn(close=True)` (pool rebuilds instead of re-serving the corpse) and runs
  `operation` once more on a fresh connection. A second stale failure, or any non-stale
  error, propagates (with a safe rollback + normal return-to-pool first). Also retries once
  if `getconn()` itself transiently fails opening a new physical connection.
  `execute_query_pg()`/`execute_write_pg()` now extract their body to a local `_run(conn)`
  and call `_run_pooled_pg(_run)` on the no-transaction path (unchanged while a
  `pg_transaction()` is active). Covers 12 of the 13 observed 500s.
- `_getconn_pg_checked()` — for `pg_transaction()` and `get_raw_conn_pg()`, which share one
  connection across a multi-statement unit of work and so can't be retried mid-stream. A
  **free client-side** `conn.closed` check (no round trip — deliberately not a `SELECT 1`
  ping, which would double this cross-region app's DB round trips): skip an already-broken
  connection at borrow, up to 3×. `release_raw_conn_pg()` and the `pg_transaction()` finally
  now `putconn(conn, close=bool(conn.closed))` so a connection that broke while held is not
  re-pooled.
- Recovery is logged (added after a log-visibility check with Aadil — the fix is otherwise
  invisible): `[postgres] discarded a stale pooled connection (<reason>), retried OK` on a
  successful retry; `[postgres] stale pooled connection on both attempts (...); failing
  request` on a double failure; `[postgres] skipped N closed pooled connection(s) at
  borrow` from `_getconn_pg_checked()`. Plain ASCII (no emoji, per the console-encoding
  gotcha). The healthy path prints nothing.

**Residual gap** (`KNOWN_ISSUES.md` 2026-09-02, Defer): a connection silently dropped while
idle and first re-used *inside* a bare `pg_transaction()` / `get_raw_conn_pg()` block still
fails that one request — no operation-level retry is possible there. Rare (≤1 of the 13),
and the `close=True` recycling stops it spreading. Closing it fully needs the `SELECT 1`
pre-ping, judged not worth one extra round trip per heavy write.

**Tests** — `tests/test_pg_pool_retry.py`, 10 tests, hand-built fake pool/connection/cursor,
no live Postgres, no `test.db`: retry-once-and-succeed; non-stale error propagates unchanged
with no retry; give up after exactly one retry; transient `getconn` retry; the stale-vs-not
predicate (matches the two documented conditions, rejects deadlock / "too many clients" /
`ProgrammingError` / `ValueError`); `_getconn_pg_checked` skips a closed connection and
leaves a healthy one untouched; each recovery log line fires and the non-stale path is
silent; and the same retry end-to-end through `execute_query_pg`.

**Verified:** `pytest tests/test_pg_pool_retry.py` 10/10; full `pytest tests/` 98/98, no
regressions; `python -c "import database"` clean. Live server boot / Verification-flow check
done by Aadil (browser HAR: all API responses `200`, no errors) — Phase 1 adds no
import-time behaviour and does not touch `get_pg_pool()` construction.

## Postgres Pool Warm-Start (PG_POOL_MIN 1 → 3)

**Date:** 2026-09-02 | **Files:** `database.py`, `.env.example`. Phase 2 (final) of the
two-phase brief above.

**Why.** `PG_POOL_MIN` controls how many connections `get_pg_pool()` opens *eagerly* at
startup; the rest open lazily on first use, and each new physical connection pays a full
round trip to Supabase (Mumbai) — costliest right after a cold start (Render free tier
spins down on idle). The 2026-09-02 investigation measured `procedure_modal_data`'s
`support_data_ms` dropping 3641→1984ms run-over-run at a flat DB-call count, the signature
of that first-use connection cost. `MIN=1` was never a deliberate choice, just the original
default.

**Change.** `get_pg_pool()` — `int(os.environ.get("PG_POOL_MIN", "1"))` → `"3"`, plus a
comment on the reasoning. `3` pre-warms enough for the first small burst of work after a
wake, stays well below `PG_POOL_MAX` (15, unchanged — deliberately raised 10→15 on
2026-08-25 for a real exhaustion incident) and the `asyncio.Semaphore(5)` availability
fan-out cap in `routers/data.py`. `5` was considered and rejected (bigger one-time boot
cost, more idle connections, no clear extra benefit for this traffic). Env var still
overrides. `.env.example` corrected: `Defaults: 1 / 10` → `Defaults: 3 / 15` and the
commented `PG_POOL_MIN`/`PG_POOL_MAX` examples (the MAX line had been stale since the
2026-08-25 bump), plus a half-line explaining MIN vs MAX.

**Cost.** ~+0.5s one-time at startup (3 sequential connects to Mumbai instead of 1). No
per-request change; connections beyond 3 still open on demand exactly as before.

**Verified:** `python -c "import database"` clean; full `pytest tests/` 98/98 (nothing
asserts the constant). Live check by Aadil — dev server restarted, procedure window
open/save/close exercised, browser HAR shows all API responses `200`/`304`, no errors.
Startup line now reads `[postgres] connection pool created (min=3, max=15)`.

## Local tray launcher reliability fix — 2026-09-04

`tray_control.py` now protects the system tray with a Windows user-session mutex, runs
Start/Stop/Restart operations on a serialized background worker, detects an exited server
process early, and allows up to 60 seconds for legitimate application/database startup.
Duplicate operations are ignored without blocking the tray, and Quit is deferred while a
lifecycle operation is active so it cannot leave an orphaned server process.

`start_tray.vbs` adds a narrow WMI command-line guard for transition safety: controllers started
by the older pre-mutex launcher are also detected and not duplicated. `run.bat` and application
startup behavior were unchanged. The stale controller tree was restarted after its exact PIDs
were verified and no server was listening.

Verified with Python compilation, a mocked background-operation serialization check, a live
fixed-controller restart, and a second `start_tray.vbs` launch that kept the process tree at
the expected two launcher/interpreter processes. No server was started during the check.

The Purchase Demand Procedure window received 5,725 rows but displayed dashes for fields that
were selected in Audit Rules. The Document had no saved field-policy payload, and the preview
endpoint incorrectly projected only recognized core fields, so the other Template values were
removed before the browser received the response.

For an unconfigured linked Document, the preview now projects every active column from the
linked Template, matching the Audit Rules default selection. Explicitly saved policies retain
their existing selected-column behavior. The existing browser lookup remains tolerant of minor
stored-key formatting differences.

Verified with Python compilation, all 58 Audit Rules tests, the new unconfigured-policy
regression, and `git diff --check`. Manual confirmation requires restarting the server,
hard-refreshing Verification, and checking the Purchase Demand preview response contains all
seven selected Template columns.

## Form persistence and authoring correction — 2026-09-05

Form Fields were moved directly below the Linked Template control so a Form document reads in the
agreed order: optional prefill source, manual evidence fields, then Authorisation. The normal new
Document flow continues to offer Linked Template and Form; existing Physical Bill records and
their backend compatibility remain unchanged for the controlled Phase H/I migration.

The Document update model now distinguishes an omitted `form_fields` value from an explicit empty
list. Secondary whole-document updates, such as adding an authorisation role, preserve the saved
Form definition instead of clearing it. The main Form save can still intentionally clear all fields.

Verified with 64 focused Audit Rulebook tests, 120 full-suite tests, JavaScript syntax validation,
Python compilation, and `git diff --check`. Aadil confirmed the local browser correction and approved
Git closeout. Phase D is the next implementation phase.

## Form Procedure-window rendering - Phase D - 2026-09-06

Form field definitions are now included in both live category guidance and the compiled
Verification Rulebook. The shared Procedure modal recognizes `document_type: form` and renders
manual Header fields plus repeatable Item rows with Text, Date, and Numeric controls. Optional
Linked Column mappings are displayed as prefill metadata only; Copy from lines remains Phase E.

Form evidence uses the existing typed `voucher_line_form_entries` and
`voucher_line_form_values` tables. A full-replace save endpoint validates document ownership,
row scope, duplicate fields, dates, numeric values, and explicit clearing. Reads use the existing
stable sibling-session convention so saved evidence reloads consistently. The Verification atomic
Save/Verify bundle also accepts dirty Form entries; Physical Bill handling is unchanged.

Updated the shared-modal cache version for Verification and Audit Workbook. Added focused Form
contract tests; JavaScript syntax, Python compilation, `git diff --check`, and the full test suite
(124 tests) pass. Manual browser confirmation is still required before Git commit/push. Phase E is next.

Follow-up correction: Form documents with an optional Linked Template now use Template columns only
for Linked Column mapping. They no longer enter the separate linked-template Verification Data
Fields validation, which had incorrectly shown the reselect-Template error during Save. The Audit
Rules asset version was bumped to `v=13`; 69 Audit Rulebook tests pass after the correction.

Follow-up correction: Existing Postgres databases could still retain the pre-Form
`audit_rule_documents_document_type_check` because the bootstrap marker intentionally skips the
full schema pass after the first successful startup. The startup path now performs an idempotent
constraint inspection and upgrades that check to allow `linked_template`, `form`, and
`physical_bill` without changing document rows. Form template loading also keeps the separate
Verification Data Fields policy panel hidden while it loads Linked Column choices, including on
load failure. The Audit Rules asset version is now `v=14`.

Verified with the focused Audit Rules and Postgres bootstrap suites (81 tests), JavaScript syntax
validation, and `git diff --check`. The first full-suite run found and then covered one stale test
expectation for the new migration query; a clean full-suite rerun remains required before Git
closeout. Manual browser retest is required: restart the server, hard-refresh Audit Rules, save a
Form with an optional Linked Template, and confirm the Linked Column list loads without the error.

Render acceptance then exposed a second legacy-schema gap: `audit_rule_document_fields` existed on
the deployed Postgres database without the later `field_type`, `field_scope`, and `linked_column`
columns. The Form payload and linked-column mapping were correct; the 500 occurred when the backend
persisted those fields. The completed-schema startup path now inspects `information_schema` and adds
only missing columns with safe defaults, preserving all existing definitions. The migration is
transactional and idempotent.

The Render error response identified this exact missing-column failure. Added regression coverage for
missing-column and no-op paths. The targeted suites pass 83 tests and the full suite passes 129
tests, with only existing deprecation/cache warnings. Manual Render retest remains required before
the next commit/push.

## Form Copy from lines - Phase E - 2026-09-06

Verification now has a read-only `form_copy_sources` endpoint. It resolves active linked-template
evidence rows for the current voucher line's stable `client_data_id`, limited to the Form's selected
Template and active linked-template Documents. Audit Rules remains configuration-only; source data is
not copied or stored there.

The shared Procedure modal now shows `Copy from lines` for Forms with Linked Column mappings. It
copies the first source row into blank Header fields and source rows into blank/repeated Item rows,
preserving every non-empty auditor value. Date values are normalized for HTML date controls, item
rows are created only as needed, and the editor remains dirty until the normal Form save/Verify path
persists the reviewed values. Empty-source, no-mapping, no-change, and request-error feedback is
shown in the Form panel. Shared modal cache versions were bumped in Verification and Audit Workbook.

Added backend regression coverage for same-line/template source resolution and the no-mapping short
path. JavaScript syntax, Python compilation, focused tests (76), and the full suite (131) pass; six
existing warnings remain. Manual browser acceptance is required: link source rows, copy into a Form,
confirm Header/Item mapping, confirm existing values are not overwritten, save/reopen, and retry with
 no source rows. No commit/push until that test is confirmed.

## Category Applicable Documents - Phase D2 - 2026-09-06

Category Applicable Documents is now the explicit document-membership source for Category authoring.
The Category editor exposes the existing add/remove/required controls, and Procedure/Evidence choices
are limited to active selected Documents, including Form Documents. Saving a Category sends only the
selected Category document IDs; Procedure rows and Applied Cross-checks no longer expand that set.

The validation-rules endpoint now verifies that every Procedure/Evidence Document ID belongs to the
Category before checking that the Document is active. This preserves the existing reusable Cross-check
model; dependency containment and activation behavior remain the approved D4 scope.

Added focused regression coverage for accepted and rejected Procedure document membership. The user
manually confirmed the Category selector, save behavior, and Procedure/Evidence eligibility. The
remaining Physical Vendor Bill presentation issue is recorded for D6/H implementation and P7 UX
refinement; it does not block D2.

## Category Procedure/Evidence ownership - Phase D3 - 2026-09-06

Procedure/Evidence rows now require a valid risk level and a role/signatory detail for all
role-based conditions. The Category editor provides an explicit `Import Document audit checks`
action that seeds Category-owned rows from the selected Documents' authorisation roles; it does not
silently import or synchronize anything. The compiled Rulebook resolves the selected detail to its
Document role and only exposes signatories for that role, while preserving client-scoped Signature
Specimens as the reference source. The Audit Rules editor now restores saved risk values instead of
defaulting every reopened row to Medium.

Verification checklist matching now honors the Category-selected role or signatory detail and no
longer activates an unrelated role. Added backend, Rulebook, and browser regression coverage.
Focused tests (74) and the full suite (134) pass. The user manually confirmed Document-role import,
risk persistence, and the Verification Procedure checklist. D3 is complete; D4 is next.

## Cross-check dependency validation - Phase D4 - 2026-09-06

Applied Cross-checks now remain rule-only. The Cross-check list exposes ordered dependency summaries
through one set-based query, so the Category picker disables rules whose Documents are missing from
Applicable Documents or inactive. Existing invalid assignments are shown as blocked instead of
pretending they are active.

Category Rulebook compilation now excludes invalid attached Cross-checks and emits structured
dependency warnings. The direct Verification evaluator applies the same containment and active-
Document guard, so neither path creates hidden Procedure documents or evaluates an undeclared rule.

Focused Rulebook tests (75), Cross-check performance tests (5), full suite (135), Python compilation,
JavaScript syntax checks, and diff checks passed. Manual browser confirmation confirmed the expected
block for the legacy inactive Vendor Bill dependency. D4 is complete; D5 is next.

## Verification document visibility - Phase D5 - 2026-09-06

Verification now treats the frozen session Rulebook as authoritative: a missing Category profile no
longer falls back to live Audit Rules guidance and silently changes the session. Compiled and live
Category guidance now expose active-state metadata, while the shared Procedure modal filters to
active, unique, explicitly selected Category Documents only. Cross-check dependencies and saved
evidence references cannot create additional Procedure tabs.

Added regression coverage for active/unique Procedure tab projection and frozen-session no-fallback
behavior. Focused Rulebook tests (77), Cross-check performance tests (5), full suite (137), Python
compilation, JavaScript syntax checks, and diff checks passed. The user manually confirmed the
Category-only Procedure tabs, active-document behavior, and absence of hidden Cross-check tabs.
D5 is complete; D6 is next.

## Form Vendor Bill integration - Phase D6 - 2026-09-06

Form Documents now expose one stable Cross-check field contract: the saved Form field name and type
are authoritative, while `linked_column` remains source metadata for prefill and display. Matrix
authoring and cell validation expose/accept Form fields, and compiled Rulebook documents carry the
Form field options needed by the Audit Rules UI. Legacy linked-template and Physical Bill field
behavior remains compatible.

Verification now reads saved numeric Form values by `(client_data_id, document_id)`, selecting the
latest sibling-session entry, and evaluates them through the existing matrix/single-rule engine.
This reuses the same Document ID as Procedure/Evidence and never creates hidden tabs or silently
remaps the legacy Vendor Bill Document. A legacy Vendor Bill dependency therefore remains visibly
blocked until the explicit D8 migration.

The Form Procedure panel received scoped presentation styling for typed Header/Item fields, mapped
column context, item-row actions, Copy from lines feedback, focus states, empty configuration, and
responsive layout. Added regression coverage for Form field metadata, validation, latest-value
selection, and Document-ID matrix evaluation. Focused Rulebook tests (81) pass; manual browser
confirmation was completed before D6 closeout; D7 is next and D8 remains the later migration phase.

September 7 correction: live Document 42 defines Form field `Quantity`, mapped to template 5's
`Receive Quantity`. Matrix validation incorrectly preferred nonempty template columns, rejecting
the valid Form field. Validation now branches by Document Type: Forms use their fields, legacy
Physical Bills use fixed fields, and linked-template Documents use only their template columns.
The regression reproduced the reported 400 before the fix; it now covers saving `Quantity` and
rejecting template-only/unknown Form operands. Full suite: 141 tests and 3 subtests passed; Python
compilation and diff checks passed. The user manually confirmed Quantity selection, save, and reopen.

## Category/document governance hardening - Phase D9 - 2026-09-07

Category and Cross-check persistence now rejects duplicate IDs and new inactive attachments. Active
Cross-checks must have at least one Document dependency, and every dependency must be active and
already present in the Category's Applicable Documents. Existing inactive assignments remain readable
so administrators can remove them safely. Cross-check Document columns also reject duplicate or
inactive Documents.

Document Template/type changes now preflight active Cross-check shared, per-Document, and matrix cell
fields against the proposed field contract; invalid changes are blocked with the affected rule and
field named. The Categories UI keeps inactive attached Documents visible for removal and adds removal
actions for unavailable or blocked Cross-check assignments. Active add-pickers remain active-only.

Changed files: `routers/audit_rules.py`, `static/audit_rules.js`, `tests/test_audit_rulebook.py`,
`DEVELOPMENT_PLAN.md`, and `CLAUDE.md`. Focused Audit Rules tests: 99 passed, 1 existing cache
warning, 3 subtests. Full-suite, syntax, and diff checks remain before closeout; manual Audit Rules
confirmation is required because the Categories behavior is user-facing. P1 follows confirmation.

Focused regression tests: 118 passed; full suite: 166 passed, 6 existing warnings, 3 subtests;

## Storage Cleanup Phase A — read-only administrator preview — 2026-09-14

Added `services/storage_cleanup.py`, `routers/storage_cleanup.py`, and the Setup-linked
`storage_cleanup.html`/`.js` firm-level admin screen. The preview reads PostgreSQL database/table
sizes, removable log totals, retired unlinked `client_data` candidates, and protected
`client_data`/`verification_details`/Trial Balance counts. It performs no writes, deletion, or

## Storage Cleanup Phase B — confirmation-gated cleanup — 2026-09-14

Added the approved in-app cleanup operation across `database.py`, `services/storage_cleanup.py`,
`routers/storage_cleanup.py`, `static/storage_cleanup.html`/`.js`, and the CLI. The administrator
must submit a fresh preview hash and type `DELETE APPROVED STORAGE DATA`; the service then removes
only the four approved application logs, dependency-free retired `client_data`, deleted and
unreferenced upload metadata, stale presence, and expired sessions in one PostgreSQL transaction.
Current Data Bank rows, Verification details, Trial Balance tables, and linked evidence are guarded
by explicit predicates and post-delete count checks. Each successful run stores operator, scope,
preview hash, status, and deleted counts in `storage_cleanup_runs`. VACUUM/compaction remains
deferred. Focused tests cover confirmation, stale-preview rejection, and route forwarding; no live
cleanup was invoked during development.

## Storage Cleanup Phase B correction — existing-schema startup migration — 2026-09-14

Investigation of the first live apply attempt found the preview succeeded but the POST returned
503 because `init_db_postgres()` returned through its existing-schema fast path without creating
`storage_cleanup_runs`; the apply transaction therefore rolled back before any deletion. Added a
shared idempotent table definition/ensure step to that path in `database.py`, with regression
coverage in `tests/test_storage_cleanup.py`. The cleanup scope and protected-data rules were not
changed, and no live cleanup was invoked while correcting this issue.

## Assertions Master Entity — Audit Rules Phase 1 of 5 - 2026-09-20

New `audit_rule_assertions` table (SQLite `database.py` `init_db()`, Postgres `init_db_postgres()`),
seeded with the 5 fixed entries in conventional audit-standard order (Existence/Occurrence,
Completeness, Accuracy/Valuation, Cut-off, Authorisation), each with a `sort_order` column so list
order stays fixed rather than alphabetical — same non-alphabetical precedent `audit_rule_voucher_checks`
already established. This is the first of a 5-phase requirement; later phases (not built here) will
let a Category's attached Documents/Cross-checks/Voucher-level Checks be tagged against this list,
plus a per-Category coverage-gap warning. Tags live on the attachment, not the entity, per the
confirmed brief — no schema for that yet.

`routers/audit_rules.py` gained `AssertionCreate`/`AssertionUpdate` models, `row_to_assertion()`, and
six endpoints (list/get/create/update/soft-delete/restore) mirroring the Categories entity exactly —
same `cache_get`/`cache_set`/`invalidate_audit_rules_cache()` wiring, same
`Depends(ensure_no_active_verification_sessions)` write guard this router uses instead of admin auth,
same soft-delete-then-restore shape (no hard delete). `static/audit_rules.html` gained a 5th rail
button/list-section/detail-section, mirroring the Voucher-level Checks detail form (Name + one text
field) rather than Categories' (no document/cross-check picker needed here). `static/audit_rules.js`
gained a full parallel "ASSERTIONS" section (DOM refs, state, load/render/select/save/delete/restore,
listener wiring) plus a `switchEntityType()`/`AR_VALID_ENTITY_TYPES` branch — same full-duplication-
per-entity-type convention the file already follows for Documents/Cross-checks/Categories/Voucher-level
Checks. No pagination (unlike Documents/Categories) — this list stays small, same as Voucher-level
Checks' own unpaginated load. `client_context.js`'s `NAV_MANIFEST` gained an "Assertions" child under
Audit Rules, using the real `?entity=` param `restoreAuditRulesViewFromUrl()` actually reads — its five
sibling entries (Documents/Cross-checks/Categories/Voucher-level Checks/Assign Categories/Signature
Specimens) all use the dead `?feature=` param instead (pre-existing, confirmed via grep that
`audit_rules.js` never reads it; left alone as out of scope for this phase).

Two bugs found and fixed during live verification, both against the real Supabase database (not a
throwaway):

1. **Postgres bootstrap-marker gap.** `init_db_postgres()` skips its entire declarative CREATE TABLE
   pass — including a newly-added one — on any database that already has the `audit_rules_config_state`
   marker table (i.e. any already-bootstrapped database, confirmed live: this app's own Supabase hit
   this path and returned `UndefinedTable: relation "audit_rule_assertions" does not exist` on first
   request). Fixed by adding `_ensure_postgres_audit_rule_assertions(conn)` — same idempotent
   `to_regclass()`-check-then-`CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` (+ `ON CONFLICT (name) DO NOTHING` seed)
   pattern as the existing `_ensure_postgres_form_tables()` — and calling it from the fast-path branch
   alongside the other `_ensure_postgres_*` migrations. See the new Conventions entry in CLAUDE.md — any
   future new Postgres table needs this same companion function, not just a CREATE TABLE in the full
   bootstrap section.
2. **`updateAuditRulesUrl()` didn't know about the new entity type** — its `currentEntityType →
   selectedId` lookup object was a hardcoded list of the 4 existing entities, so selecting an Assertion
   never wrote `&id=` into the URL, and a hard refresh silently dropped back to whatever the URL's
   `?entity=assertions` alone would restore (no specific row re-selected). Added `assertions:
   editingAssertionId` to that lookup.

Verified: `pytest tests/ -v` (266 passed; the 16 pre-existing failures were confirmed unrelated via a
`git stash`-based before/after comparison — none touch any file this phase changed); Python
`py_compile` and `node -c` syntax checks on every changed backend/frontend file; a throwaway server on
port 5050 (the user's own port-5000 dev server was left untouched, per this file's port-5000-check
convention) driven end-to-end with Playwright against the real database — login, client selection, the
new Assertions rail tab rendering all 5 seeded entries in order, row select/edit/save with the edit
confirmed to survive a page reload, and full create/delete/restore/update round-trips via direct API
calls. All test data was cleaned up afterward (seed rows reset to their original `description: null`
state). Aadil then manually confirmed the feature working on his own port-5000 server before this was
committed.

## Tag Documents with Assertions — Audit Rules Phase 2 of 5 - 2026-09-20

New `audit_rule_category_document_assertions` join table (SQLite + Postgres, same dual-schema
requirement as Phase 1) letting a Category's attached Document be tagged with one or more
Assertions from the Phase 1 master list. Keyed by the same `(category_id, document_id)` pair the
existing `is_required` flag already uses to address a Category-Document attachment — not the
attachment's own surrogate `id`, which is never exposed to the frontend — via a composite FK
against `audit_rule_category_documents`' existing `UNIQUE(category_id, document_id)` constraint,
plus `assertion_id` FK'd to `audit_rule_assertions`. `UNIQUE(category_id, document_id, assertion_id)`
prevents duplicate tags; two indexes support the lookup and Phase 5's future "which Assertions have
zero tagged items" query. No UI (Phase 4's job), no coverage-gap logic (Phase 5's job), and no
`matrix_version` bump — that field drives the Cleared/Query engine and Assertions are explicitly out
of engine scope.

`routers/audit_rules.py` gained `get_category_document_assertions()`/
`save_category_document_assertions()` helpers (full-replace, not diff — same convention
`save_category_documents()` already uses) and two endpoints mirroring the existing `is_required`
toggle's shape exactly: `GET`/`PUT .../categories/{category_id}/documents/{document_id}/assertions`
(404 if the Document isn't attached to the Category, 400 naming the specific id if an unknown
`assertion_id` is submitted — same per-id error style `validate_category_payload()` uses). Kept as a
dedicated sub-resource rather than folded into `CategoryCreate`/`CategoryUpdate`, for the same reason
the `is_required` toggle's own comment already gives — keeping that already-live payload shape
untouched.

Followed the Postgres bootstrap-marker Convention CLAUDE.md gained during Phase 1: added a companion
`_ensure_postgres_category_document_assertions(conn)` migration function (same idempotent
`to_regclass()`-check-then-`CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` pattern as
`_ensure_postgres_audit_rule_assertions()`) alongside the full-bootstrap `CREATE TABLE`, and wired it
into `init_db_postgres()`'s fast-path branch — confirmed necessary again live (the real Supabase
database took this path, and the migration log correctly reported
`audit_rule_category_document_assertions created`).

A pre-existing regression was found and fixed along the way, not caused by this phase:
`tests/test_storage_cleanup.py::test_existing_postgres_schema_path_ensures_cleanup_run_ledger`'s mock
only queued 2 fake `cursor()` results and never patched out Phase 1's own
`_ensure_postgres_audit_rule_assertions()` (added to the same fast-path branch this test exercises),
so that function's real, unmocked `conn.cursor()` call exhausted the mock's `side_effect` list and
raised `StopIteration` — confirmed via `git stash` to already fail at Phase 1's committed state, before
any Phase 2 changes existed. Fixed by patching out both `_ensure_postgres_audit_rule_assertions()` and
the new `_ensure_postgres_category_document_assertions()` in that test, matching how it already patches
the other four sibling migration functions. User confirmed this scope addition before it was made.

Verified: `pytest tests/ -v` back to exactly the same 16 pre-existing failures Phase 1 already
confirmed unrelated (was 17 before the storage-cleanup mock fix); `py_compile` on both changed
backend files; a throwaway server on port 5050 against the real Supabase database (port 5000 was not
running this session, so no collision risk) — confirmed the migration log line, then exercised GET

## Tag Cross-checks and Voucher-level Checks with Assertions — Audit Rules Phase 3 of 5 - 2026-09-21

Extended Phase 2's tagging pattern to the other two rule types. Cross-checks fit the pattern exactly:
new `audit_rule_category_cross_check_assertions` table, keyed by the same `(category_id,
cross_check_id)` pair `audit_rule_category_cross_checks` already uses, composite FK against that
table's existing `UNIQUE(category_id, cross_check_id)` constraint. Endpoints
`GET`/`PUT .../categories/{category_id}/cross-checks/{cross_check_id}/assertions` mirror Phase 2's
Document endpoints byte-for-byte in shape.

**Architectural fork found while looking at "Phase 2's actual table," as that phase's brief asked**:
Voucher-level Checks have no Category attachment at all — `audit_rule_voucher_checks` has no
`category_id` column and no `audit_rule_category_voucher_checks` join table exists anywhere in the
schema (confirmed by grep), matching this project's own documented fact that the same check applies
uniformly to every Category. So "tag lives on the attachment, not the entity" had nothing to attach
to for this one entity type. Resolved by tagging the entity directly: new
`audit_rule_voucher_check_assertions(voucher_check_id, assertion_id)`, endpoints
`GET`/`PUT /api/audit-rules/voucher-checks/{voucher_check_id}/assertions`. Functionally equivalent to
a Category-scoped tag when there's exactly one universal scope. Flagged in the plan before
implementation rather than silently deviating from the brief's locked assumption.

Both `routers/audit_rules.py` helper pairs (`get_category_cross_check_assertions()`/
`save_category_cross_check_assertions()`, `get_voucher_check_assertions()`/
`save_voucher_check_assertions()`) are direct copies of Phase 2's Document-assertion helpers — same
full-replace-not-diff convention, same per-id `HTTPException(400, f"Assertion ID {id} not found")`
validation, no `matrix_version` bump (tags don't drive the Cleared/Query engine).

Two more companion `_ensure_postgres_category_cross_check_assertions(conn)` /
`_ensure_postgres_voucher_check_assertions(conn)` migration functions were added per the Phase 1
Convention, wired into `init_db_postgres()`'s fast-path branch — confirmed live again (migration log:
`audit_rule_category_cross_check_assertions created; audit_rule_voucher_check_assertions created`).
`tests/test_storage_cleanup.py`'s mock (already patched once in Phase 2 for the same reason) needed
patching again for both new functions, same `StopIteration`-from-an-exhausted-mock-`cursor.side_effect`
failure mode.

**A real bug was found and fixed during this phase's own verification, before anything was shown to
Aadil**: the two new SQLite index-creation calls (`CREATE INDEX ... ON audit_rule_voucher_check_assertions`)
were initially added to the wrong batch in `init_db()` — the early "Audit Rules module Phase 1 of 9"
batch, which runs *before* the Voucher-level Checks table section appears later in the function body.
This broke `init_db()` outright (`sqlite3.OperationalError: no such table`), which was caught

## Coverage Gap Warning — Audit Rules Phase 5 of 5, FINAL - 2026-09-21

Completes the 5-phase Assertions feature. Shows a compact amber warning at the very top of
Category detail listing any Assertion that's in use somewhere in the app but has zero coverage for
that specific Category — a live, uncached read over the three join tables Phases 2/3 built.

**Resolved a real ambiguity in the brief, not glossed over**: read literally, "relevant Assertions
= tagged on at least one item attached to this Category" makes a zero-coverage gap logically
impossible (a relevant Assertion, by that definition, already has ≥1 tag on this exact Category).
The brief's own follow-on sentence — "a gap is only meaningful once at least one Assertion is in
use somewhere in the app" — resolves it: "relevant" is a firm-wide filter (only warn about
Assertions someone has actually started using, anywhere), and the gap check itself is scoped
per-Category. **Voucher-level Checks count toward every Category's coverage**, not just their own
"relevant" contribution — they have no `category_id` at all (Phase 3's architectural fork) and run
on every voucher of every Category uniformly, so a Voucher-level Check tag is coverage for every
Category simultaneously, not a category-specific fact. Confirmed live: tagging Voucher-level Check
8 with an Assertion cleared an existing gap on an unrelated Category that had never itself tagged
anything with that Assertion.

`routers/audit_rules.py` gained one new read-only endpoint,
`GET /api/audit-rules/categories/{category_id}/assertion-gaps`, a single CTE query (`relevant`
firm-wide, `covered` per-Category via Documents/Cross-checks attached to it plus any active
Voucher-level Check) rather than a Python set-difference over multiple round-trips. Deliberately
**not** added to `row_to_category()` (the function backing both the single-Category fetch and the
paginated Categories list) — computing a firm-wide aggregation on every row of every list page
would be real, unnecessary cost against the brief's "no caching" requirement, for a UI element that
only belongs on the single-Category detail view.

`static/audit_rules.js`'s `selectCategory()` fires the new gap fetch alongside its existing
Phase 4 parallel per-document/per-cross-check tag fetches (`Promise.all`, not sequential);
`renderCategoryAssertionGaps()` populates a new static container
(`#arCategoryAssertionGapsWarning`, `audit_rules.html`, first child of `arCategoryDetailForm` —
literally the top of Category detail) with one line per gap ("`<Name>`: no control mapped"),
hidden entirely when there are none. `startNewCategory()` clears/hides it — a brand-new Category
has no attachments yet, so showing every relevant Assertion as "missing" would be noise, not
signal, same spirit as the Phase 4 unsaved-row picker gating. New `.ar-category-gap-warning` CSS
deliberately reuses the exact amber pair (`#76551e`/`#fff6e5`) already used by the adjacent
`.ar-category-callout` "Status rule" box on the same screen, for visual consistency, rather than
the plan's originally-proposed generic app-wide amber pair. `style.css?v=26`/`audit_rules.js?v=25`
bumped (style.css on all 20 pages that load it).

Verified: `py_compile`/`node -c`/HTML parse checks; `pytest tests/ -v` back to the same 16
pre-existing unrelated failures. Live curl transcript against the real Supabase database (port 5000
was running the user's own session this time, left untouched; a throwaway port-5050 instance was
used instead) proved the full rule live: tagging Document 21 (Category 11) with Cut-off produced
`[]` for Category 11's own gap check but `[{"id":4,"name":"Cut-off"}]` for unrelated Category 3;
tagging Voucher-level Check 8 with the same Assertion then cleared Category 3's gap to `[]`; a
nonexistent category correctly 404s. Playwright screenshot confirmed the rendered warning
("⚠ Cut-off: no control mapped") on Category 3 and its correct absence on covered Category 11. All
test tags cleared back to empty afterward.

## Rulebook architecture decision and snapshot foundation - 2026-09-22

**Scope:** approved Step 4 investigation followed by Step 5 foundation in database.py, routers/audit_rules.py,
tests/test_audit_rulebook.py and the four project notes. Existing client/session Rulebooks remain authoritative
for Verification; this phase does not integrate snapshot consumption or change saved statuses.

**Investigation:** Git HEAD 7c46e2e already stored Category snapshots, but shared procedures could retain a
client-resolved role after specimen stripping; inactive snapshots were deleted, resetting restore revisions.
Assertions were absent, saves rebuilt every active Category, and cold client loads republished snapshots.
The grouped Verify path supplies one client Rulebook; Save-only resolves it per line. Status evaluation
still reads Category matrices, Document/template/Form definitions and roles live; voucher evidence stays live.

**Step 4 baseline:** real functions extracted through AST, warm caches, disposable in-memory SQLite adapter,
five same-Category lines with linked/Form/no-template Documents, 11 repetitions. Counts are per bunch;
times are local medians, not PostgreSQL/network/HTTP/commit latency or a speedup claim.

| Path | Reads | Writes | Batch calls | SQLite audit writes | Median ms |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Status only | 70 | 5 | 0 | 0 | 3.2 |
| Status plus matrix | 100 | 15 | 5 | 0 | 6.3 |
| Grouped Verify | 113 | 17 | 7 | 5 | 9.2 |
| Grouped Verify plus matrix | 143 | 27 | 12 | 5 | 6.5 |

Timing jitter prevents comparisons between these tiny local runs. Existing metrics omit batch calls and
SQLite audit writes; reproducible production benchmarking remains Step 7.

**Approved contract / implementation:** schema-v2 neutral Category JSON includes Documents, Forms,
Cross-check matrix order/cells, authored procedure selectors, dependency warnings and Assertion tags.
One global block holds active voucher checks and Assertion metadata. Client specimens/account assignments
never enter shared compilation; raw signer selectors are retained for later client-role resolution.
Canonical SHA-256 content fingerprints advance revisions; evaluation fingerprints exclude coverage/risk/notes
and legacy non-gating settings. Schema/evaluator versions make interpretation explicit.

SQLite upgrades retain old revisions; PostgreSQL uses the same additive helper on existing and fresh schemas.
Inactive Categories retain snapshots; restore increments revisions. Known dependency changes rebuild impacted
Categories, voucher-check changes update the global block, and unknown scope/version gaps force full recovery.
Cold client loads repair missing/old snapshots through neutral compilation instead of publishing client packets.
Atomic publication locks the durable version, rejects obsolete or wrongly scoped packets, and rolls back
partial writes. This does not make existing multi-commit rule-authoring endpoints atomic; see KNOWN_ISSUES.md.

**Next-phase boundary:** consume these snapshots through the existing client/session architecture, combine
Category/global/resolved-role evaluation hashes, and persist the applied hash. Preserve historical Cleared/Query;

read-only status reason reports `current`, `needs_recheck`, or `legacy_unknown` without writing. Session rebase still
changes only `verification_sessions.rulebook_version`, preserving historical status and applied hash. Active

### Correction: existing-Postgres startup skipped the applied_ruleset_hash migration - 2026-09-22

The `applied_ruleset_hash` column above was only added to `init_db_postgres()`'s full-bootstrap branch
(new database only). Any already-bootstrapped Postgres database — including the one used for local
acceptance testing — takes the fast path at the top of that function, which returns before reaching the
bootstrap branch, so the column was never added and Save/Verify returned a `500`. This is the same
companion-migration gap documented under the `audit_rule_assertions` incident (2026-09-20 entry).

**Fix (`database.py`):** added `_ensure_postgres_applied_ruleset_hash(conn)`, modeled on the existing
single-column companion `_ensure_postgres_form_field_columns`, and wired it into the fast-path whitelist
in `init_db_postgres()` alongside the other `_ensure_postgres_*` calls.

**Verification:** added a Postgres-mocked correctness test (column added when missing, no-op when
present) plus a wiring test asserting the new call sits before the fast-path `return`, not only in the
bootstrap-only branch — the specific gap that let this ship — in `tests/test_audit_rulebook.py`. Full
`tests/` suite: 295 passed, 36 subtests passed, 17 failed, 1 error; every failing/erroring test was
individually confirmed to already fail identically at `HEAD` (`8fef0b2`) before this session's changes —
stale `_ensure_postgres_*` mock patch lists from earlier phases and one Windows temp-dir permission
error, none touching `applied_ruleset_hash` or the fast-path wiring added here. Local server restart +
live Save/Verify retest against the real Postgres database remains the user's to confirm.

### Correction: scoped Category snapshots after a global-only rebuild - 2026-09-22

A live Material Purchased save returned `503` because its valid Category snapshot remained at source version 300
after an unrelated global Voucher-level Check edit advanced the global Rulebook to 301. Targeted rebuilds are
intended to preserve unaffected Category packets, but the persisted-reader incorrectly required the Category version
to equal the requested global version. It now accepts an older Category version while retaining exact global
version/schema validation and rejecting a future Category packet. Focused tests cover the valid older packet and the
future-packet rejection. The separate Phase 4 query-batching experiment remains uncommitted: its one successful
two-line live save took 9.97 seconds, so it cannot be considered an improvement; it does not run on voucher loading
or procedure-modal requests, whose observed latency therefore remains a separate investigation.

## Cashflows derived classification and SQL aggregation - 2026-09-27

**Scope:** Completed the approved Cashflows synchronization/performance foundation through the
derived classification, backfill, upload application, Account Control Centre synchronization,
SQL-first reporting, and read-only verification phases. Raw uploaded transaction data remains
unchanged.

**Implementation:** Account Control Centre is the single source of truth for Cash/Bank accounts
and categories. Each transaction line receives a versioned derived classification record. New
uploads apply the active configuration; add, edit, and deactivate operations reclassify affected
existing derived lines, with deactivation preserving audit history. Cashflows filters the derived
layer by client, configured template, current status, non-zero amount, and date in SQL; joins
counter-account lines by voucher ID; and aggregates category/month totals in SQL. Python formats
the compact aggregate instead of repeatedly parsing raw JSON rows. A compatibility fallback is
retained for empty derived fixtures, and no source upload is deleted or rewritten.

**Measured result:** The local Leather Crop WebInspector run returned HTTP 200 for all four
periods: 1 day **2.45 s** (baseline 4.57 s, 46.5% faster), 15 days **2.93 s** (5.62 s,
47.8% faster), 1 month **4.16 s** (9.10 s, 54.3% faster), and 6 months **3.60 s** (36.57 s,
90.2% faster). Nearly all request time was backend wait time; payload transfer was only a few
milliseconds on localhost. The six-month result is not required to be slower than one month
because the output is already aggregated and database/cache state affects a single run.

**Startup and verification:** Optional Postgres schema initialization is now non-blocking so the
tray health check can succeed while the database reports `initializing` or `degraded`. The
Cashflows/Account Control Centre regression set passed **66 tests**; syntax, staged whitespace,
and the real server health smoke test passed. The HAR also showed a separate 65.5-second
`/api/auth/current-client` wait, attributed to the user's temporary internet connectivity issue,
not the Cashflows preview requests.
